units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
यदात्थ मां महाभाग तच्चिकार्षितमेव मे।
ब्रह्मा भवो लोकपालाः सर्वे मामभिकाङ्क्ष्णिः॥ ११/७/१॥
units.english: The Lord said: O greatly fortunate Uddhava, you have accurately revealed My desire to withdraw the Yadu dynasty from the earth and return to My own abode in Vaikuṇṭha. Thus Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and all other planetary rulers are now praying for Me to resume My residence in Vaikuṇṭha.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O greatly fortunate Uddhava, you have accurately revealed My desire to withdraw the Yadu dynasty from the earth and return to My own abode in Vaikuṇṭha. Thus Lord Brahmā, Lord Śiva and all other planetary rulers are now praying for Me to resume My residence in Vaikuṇṭha.

units.sanskrit:
मया निष्पादितं ह्यत्र देवकार्यमशेषतः।
यदर्थमवतीर्णोऽहमंशेन ब्रह्मणाऽर्थितः॥ ११/७/२॥
units.english: Answering the prayer of Lord Brahmā, I descended within this world along with My plenary portion, Lord Baladeva, and performed various activities on behalf of the gods. I have now completed My mission here.

meta.english_verbatim: Answering the prayer of Lord Brahmā, I descended within this world along with My plenary portion, Lord Baladeva, and performed various activities on behalf of the demigods. I have now completed My mission here.

units.sanskrit:
कुलं वै शापनिर्दग्धं नङ्क्ष्यत्यन्योन्यविग्रहात्।
समुद्रः सप्तमे ह्येनां पुरीं च प्लावयिष्यति॥ ११/७/३॥
units.english: Now due to the brāhmaṇas’ curse the Yadu dynasty will certainly perish by fighting among themselves; and on the seventh day from today the ocean will rise up and inundate this city of Dvārakā.

meta.english_verbatim: Now due to the brāhmaṇas’ curse the Yadu dynasty will certainly perish by fighting among themselves; and on the seventh day from today the ocean will rise up and inundate this city of Dvārakā.

units.sanskrit:
यर्ह्येवायं मया त्यक्तो लोकोऽयं नष्टमङ्गळः।
भविष्यत्यचिरात् साधो कलिनापि निराकृतः॥ ११/७/४॥
units.english: O saintly Uddhava, in the near future I will abandon this earth. Then, being overwhelmed by the Age of Kali, the earth will be bereft of all piety.

meta.english_verbatim: O saintly Uddhava, in the near future I will abandon this earth. Then, being overwhelmed by the Age of Kali, the earth will be bereft of all piety.

units.sanskrit:
न वस्तव्यं त्वयैवेह मया त्यक्ते महीतळे।
जनोऽधर्मरुचिर्भद्र भविष्यति कलौ युगे॥ ११/७/५॥
units.english: My dear Uddhava, you should not remain here on the earth once I have abandoned this world. My dear devotee, you are sinless, but in Kali-yuga the people will be addicted to all types of sinful activities; therefore do not stay here.

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Uddhava, you should not remain here on the earth once I have abandoned this world. My dear devotee, you are sinless, but in Kali-yuga the people will be addicted to all types of sinful activities; therefore do not stay here.

units.sanskrit:
त्वं तु सर्वं परित्यज्य स्नेहं स्वजनबन्धनम्।
मय्यावेश्य मनः सम्यक् समदृग् विचरस्व गाम्॥ ११/७/६॥
units.english: Now you should completely give up all attachment to your personal friends and relatives and fix your mind on Me. Thus being always conscious of Me, you should observe all things with equal vision and wander throughout the earth.

meta.english_verbatim: Now you should completely give up all attachment to your personal friends and relatives and fix your mind on Me. Thus being always conscious of Me, you should observe all things with equal vision and wander throughout the earth.

units.sanskrit:
यदिदं मनसा वाचा चक्षुर्भ्यां श्रवणादिभिः।
नश्वरं गृह्यमाणं च विद्धि मायां मनोमयीम्॥ ११/७/७॥
units.english: My dear Uddhava, the material universe that you perceive through your mind, speech, eyes, ears and other senses is an illusory creation that one imagines to be real due to the influence of māyā. In fact, you should know that all of the objects of the material senses are temporary.

parts.sanskrit:
यदिदं मनसा वाचा चक्षुर्भ्यां श्रवणादिभिः।
नश्वरं गृह्यमाणं च विद्धि मायां मनोमयीम्॥ ११/७/७॥

विद्धि मायां मनोमयीम्। मन्मनःप्रधानप्रकृतिनिर्मितम्।
“प्रकृतिः सा परा मह्यं रोदसी लोकधारिणी।
ऋता सत्याऽमराऽजय्या लोकानामात्मसञ्ज्ञिता॥”
इति मोक्षधर्मेषु॥ ७॥

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Uddhava, the material universe that you perceive through your mind, speech, eyes, ears and other senses is an illusory creation that one imagines to be real due to the influence of māyā. In fact, you should know that all of the objects of the material senses are temporary.

units.sanskrit:
पुंसोऽयुक्तस्य नानार्थे भ्रमः स गुणदोषकृत्।
कर्माकर्मविकर्मेति गुणदोषधियो१ भिदा॥ ११/७/८॥
units.english: One whose consciousness is bewildered by illusion perceives many differences in value and meaning among material objects. Thus one engages constantly on the platform of material good and evil and is bound by such conceptions. Absorbed in material duality, such a person contemplates the performance of compulsory duties, nonperformance of such duties and performance of forbidden activities.

meta.english_verbatim: One whose consciousness is bewildered by illusion perceives many differences in value and meaning among material objects. Thus one engages constantly on the platform of material good and evil and is bound by such conceptions. Absorbed in material duality, such a person contemplates the performance of compulsory duties, nonperformance of such duties and performance of forbidden activities.

units.sanskrit:
तस्माद् युक्तेन्द्रियजयो युक्तचित्त इदं जगत्।
आत्मनीक्षस्व विततमात्मानं मय्यधीश्वरे॥ ११/७/९॥
units.english: Therefore, bringing all your senses under control and thus subduing the mind, you should see the entire world as situated within the self, who is expanded everywhere, and you should also see this individual self within Me, the Lord.

parts.sanskrit:
तस्माद् युक्तेन्द्रियजयो युक्तचित्त इदं जगत्।
आत्मनीक्षस्व विततमात्मानं मय्यधीश्वरे॥ ११/७/९॥

“स्वर्गाद्याश्च गुणाः सर्वे दोषाः सर्वे तथैव च।
आत्मनः कर्तृताभ्रान्त्या जायन्ते नात्र संशयः।
परमात्मानमेवैकं कर्तारं वेत्ति यः पुमान्।
स मुच्यतेऽस्मात् संसारात् परमात्मानमेति च॥”
इति भारते।
इदं मया क्रियते, इदं मया न क्रियते, इदं विपरीतं क्रियते - इति बुद्धिभेदो रजस्तमोगुणनिमित्तो भ्रमः। सर्वं हि परमेश्वरः करोति।
“आत्मशब्दोदितो ब्रह्मा परमात्माभिधो ह्यहम्।
सर्वं ब्रह्मणि वीक्षेत मयि ब्रह्माणमेव च॥”
इति कालसंहितायाम्॥ ८-९॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Therefore, bringing all your senses under control and thus subduing the mind, you should see the entire world as situated within the self, who is expanded everywhere, and you should also see this individual self within Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.

units.sanskrit:
ज्ञानविज्ञानसंयुक्त आत्मभूतः शरीरिणाम्।
आत्मानुभवतुष्टात्मा नान्तरायैर्विहन्यसे॥ ११/७/१०॥
units.english: Being fully endowed with conclusive knowledge of the Vedas and having realized the ultimate purpose of such knowledge in practice, you will be able to perceive the pure self, and thus your mind will be satisfied. At that time you will become dear to all living beings, headed by the gods, and you will never be hampered by any disturbance in life.

parts.sanskrit:
ज्ञानविज्ञानसंयुक्त आत्मभूतः शरीरिणाम्।
आत्मानुभवतुष्टात्मा नान्तरायैर्विहन्यसे॥ ११/७/१०॥
आत्मभूतः आत्मवद् भूतः। “आत्मौपम्येन सर्वत्र समं पश्यति योऽर्जुन” इति वचनात्॥ १०॥

meta.english_verbatim: Being fully endowed with conclusive knowledge of the Vedas and having realized the ultimate purpose of such knowledge in practice, you will be able to perceive the pure self, and thus your mind will be satisfied. At that time you will become dear to all living beings, headed by the demigods, and you will never be hampered by any disturbance in life.

units.sanskrit:
दोषबुद्ध्योभयातीतो निषेधान्न निवर्तते।
गुणबुद्ध्या च विहितं न करोति यथाऽर्भकः॥ ११/७/११॥
units.english: One who has transcended material good and evil automatically acts in accordance with religious injunctions and avoids forbidden activities. The self-realized person does this spontaneously, like an innocent child, and not because he is thinking in terms of material good and evil.

parts.sanskrit:
दोषबुद्ध्योभयातीतो निषेधान्न निवर्तते।
गुणबुद्ध्या च विहितं न करोति यथाऽर्भकः॥ ११/७/११॥

“कर्तृत्वमात्मनो यस्माज्ज्ञाननिष्ठो न मन्यते।
अतः कुर्वन्नपि
सदा दोषबुद्ध्या न निन्दितम्।
गुणबुद्ध्या न विहितं किन्त्वीशप्रेरितोऽस्म्यहम्।
स एव च मयि स्थित्वा निन्द्यानिन्द्ये करोत्यजः।
न मे दोषो नच गुणः कर्तृत्वाभावतः स्फुटम्।
स्वतन्त्रत्वान्नचेशस्य येऽज्ञास्तेषु भवेदपि।
इति मत्वा निवर्तेत निन्द्यात् कुर्याद् गुणानपि॥”
इति बोद्धव्ये।
“अनित्या मे गुणा न स्युर्दोषा नैव कथञ्चन।
इति मत्वा शुभं कुर्यान्निवर्तेदशुभादपि।
ज्ञानी त्वकर्तृतामानादीशकर्तृत्वनिश्चयात्।
किन्तु पूर्णगुणायैव नतु दोषापनुत्तये।
नचाल्पगुणसिद्ध्यर्थं बालवत् कृतनिश्चयः॥”
इति वैशारद्ये॥ ११॥

meta.english_verbatim: One who has transcended material good and evil automatically acts in accordance with religious injunctions and avoids forbidden activities. The self-realized person does this spontaneously, like an innocent child, and not because he is thinking in terms of material good and evil.

units.sanskrit:
सर्वभूतसुहृच्छान्तो ज्ञानविज्ञाननिश्चलः।
पश्यन् मदात्मकं विश्वं न विपद्येत वै पुनः॥ ११/७/१२॥
units.english: One who is the kind well-wisher of all living beings, who is peaceful and firmly fixed in knowledge and realization, sees Me within all things. Such a person never again falls down into the cycle of birth and death.

parts.sanskrit:
सर्वभूतसुहृच्छान्तो ज्ञानविज्ञाननिश्चलः।
पश्यन् मदात्मकं विश्वं न विपद्येत वै पुनः॥ ११/७/१२॥

“वैलक्षण्याद्धरेर्भिन्नं तत्तन्त्रत्वात् तदात्मकम्।
इति विश्वं प्रपश्यन्ति ज्ञाननिष्ठा हरेः प्रियाः॥”
इति सार्वज्ञे ॥ १२॥

meta.english_verbatim: One who is the kind well-wisher of all living beings, who is peaceful and firmly fixed in knowledge and realization, sees Me within all things. Such a person never again falls down into the cycle of birth and death.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीशुक उवाच
इत्यादिष्टो भगवता महाभागवतो नृप।
उद्धवः प्रणिपत्याह तत्वजिज्ञासुरच्युतम्॥ ११/७/१३॥
units.english: Śukācārya said: O King, Lord Kṛṣṇa, thus instructed His devotee Uddhava, who was eager to receive knowledge from the Lord. Uddhava then offered obeisances to the Lord and spoke as follows.

english_edits.rule: 'the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa' -> 'Lord Kṛṣṇa' (appositive dropped)

meta.english_verbatim: Śrī Śukadeva Gosvāmi said: O King, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Kṛṣṇa, thus instructed His pure devotee Uddhava, who was eager to receive knowledge from the Lord. Uddhava then offered obeisances to the Lord and spoke as follows.

units.sanskrit:
उद्धव उवाच
योगेश योगविन्यास योगात्मन् योगसम्भव।
निःश्रेयसाय मे प्रोक्तस्त्यागः संन्यासलक्षणः॥ ११/७/१४॥
units.english: Uddhava said: My dear Lord, You alone award the results of yoga practice, and You are so kind that by Your own influence You distribute the perfection of yoga to Your devotee. Thus You are the Supreme Soul who is realized through yoga, and it is You who are the origin of all mystic power. For my supreme benefit You have explained the procedure for giving up the material world through the process of sannyāsa, or renunciation.

parts.sanskrit:
उद्धव उवाच
योगेश योगविन्यास योगात्मन् योगसम्भव।
निःश्रेयसाय मे प्रोक्तस्त्यागः संन्यासलक्षणः॥ ११/७/१४॥

योगो देवादिषु तेन न्यस्त इति योगविन्यासः।
“ज्ञानं तु योगशब्दोक्तं युज्यतेऽनेन यत् सुखम्।
क्वचिद् योग उपायः स्यात् क्वचिच्चित्तनिरोधनम्॥”
इति दत्तात्रेययोगे।
अत्र ज्ञानमुपायश्च॥ १४॥

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

meta.english_verbatim: Śrī Uddhava said: My dear Lord, You alone award the results of yoga practice, and You are so kind that by Your own influence You distribute the perfection of yoga to Your devotee. Thus You are the Supreme Soul who is realized through yoga, and it is You who are the origin of all mystic power. For my supreme benefit You have explained the procedure for giving up the material world through the process of sannyāsa, or renunciation.

units.sanskrit:
त्यागोऽयं दुष्करो भूमन् कामानां विषयात्मभिः।
सुतरां त्वयि सर्वात्मन्नभक्तैरिति मे मतिः॥ ११/७/१५॥
units.english: My dear Lord, O Supreme Soul, for those whose minds are attached to sense enjoyment, and especially for those bereft of devotion unto You, such renunciation of material enjoyment is most difficult to perform. That is my opinion.

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Lord, O Supreme Soul, for those whose minds are attached to sense gratification, and especially for those bereft of devotion unto You, such renunciation of material enjoyment is most difficult to perform. That is my opinion.

units.sanskrit:
सोऽहं ममाहमिति मूढमतिर्विगाढ
स्त्वन्मायया विरचितात्मनि सानुबन्धे।
तत्त्वञ्जसा निगदितं भवता यथाऽहं
संसाधयामि भगवन्ननुशाधि भृत्यम्॥ ११/७/१६॥
units.english: O my Lord, I myself am most foolish because my consciousness is merged in the material body and bodily relations, which are all manufactured by Your illusory energy. Thus I am thinking, “I am this body, and all of these relatives are mine.” Therefore, my Lord, please instruct Your poor servant. Please tell me how I can very easily carry out Your instructions.

meta.english_verbatim: O my Lord, I myself am most foolish because my consciousness is merged in the material body and bodily relations, which are all manufactured by Your illusory energy. Thus I am thinking, “I am this body, and all of these relatives are mine.” Therefore, my Lord, please instruct Your poor servant. Please tell me how I can very easily carry out Your instructions.

units.sanskrit:
सत्यस्य ते स्वदृश आत्मन आत्मनोऽन्यं
वक्तारमीश विबुधेष्वपि नानुचक्षे।
सर्वे विमोहितधियस्तव माययेमे
ब्रह्मादयस्तनुभृतो बहिरर्थभावाः॥ ११/७/१७॥
units.english: My dear Lord, You are the Absolute Truth, the Lord, and You reveal Yourself to Your devotees. Besides Your Lordship, I do not see anyone who can actually explain perfect knowledge to me. Such a perfect teacher is not to be found even among the gods in heaven. Indeed, all of the gods, headed by Lord Brahmā, are bewildered by Your illusory potency. They are conditioned souls who accept their own material bodies and bodily expansions to be the highest truth.

parts.sanskrit:
सत्यस्य ते स्वदृश आत्मन आत्मनोऽन्यं
वक्तारमीश विबुधेष्वपि नानुचक्षे।
सर्वे विमोहितधियस्तव माययेमे
ब्रह्मादयस्तनुभृतो बहिरर्थभावाः॥ ११/७/१७॥

अभगवत्स्वरूपत्वात् तनुभृत्त्वम्। बहिरर्थापेक्षयैव च तेषां मोहः। परमसुखसाधनादन्योऽर्थो बहिरर्थः।
“अशरीरः सदा विष्णुः पूर्णानन्दत्वतः सदा।
इच्छा च क्रीडयैवास्य न फलाय यतो विभोः।
अतो बाह्यार्थकामोऽपि निष्काम इति कथ्यते।
ब्रह्मा निरभिमानित्वाच्छरीर्यप्यशरीरवान्।
नित्यानन्दोपयोग्यन्यकामस्योज्झितितः सदा।
बहिरर्थविनिर्मुक्तस्तथाऽपि तनुधारणात्।
अमूढो मूढ इतिवदुच्यते च सरस्वती।
रुद्राद्यास्तन्वभीमानाद् बहिरर्थयुजस्तथा।
सर्वेषां ब्रह्मपदवीयोग्यानां पूर्वमेव तु।
अभावस्त्वपरोक्षस्य मोहो ज्ञानस्य भण्यते।
ब्रह्मणस्त्वंशरूपेषु भारत्या ज्ञानवर्जनम्।
ब्रह्मगायत्रिभावे तु नांशावतरणं क्वचित्।
शतजन्मसु पूर्वं तु ज्ञानोदय उदीर्यते।
आपरोक्ष्येण पारोक्ष्यात् पूर्णज्ञानं सदैव तु।
शतजन्मगतायाश्च आपरोक्षोज्झितिर्भवेत्।
क्वचित्क्वचित् सरस्वत्यामंशावतरणेष्विति॥”
इति शक्तिविवेके।
“अशरीरो वायुरभ्रं विद्युत् स्तयित्नुरशरीराणि वा एतानि” इति च श्रुतिः।
“श्रुतिभिः स्तनयित्नुत्वात् स्तनयित्नुर्हरिः स्मृतः।
अभ्रं भूतानि भरणाच्छ्रीर्वायुर्भरतः स्मृतः।
विद्युत् तु भारती प्रोक्ता एत एवाशरीरिणः।
व्यत्यासेनापि नाम स्यादेतेषां महतां सदा॥”
इत्युभयनिरुक्ते ॥ १७॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Lord, You are the Absolute Truth, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and You reveal Yourself to Your devotees. Besides Your Lordship, I do not see anyone who can actually explain perfect knowledge to me. Such a perfect teacher is not to be found even among the demigods in heaven. Indeed, all of the demigods, headed by Lord Brahmā, are bewildered by Your illusory potency. They are conditioned souls who accept their own material bodies and bodily expansions to be the highest truth.

units.sanskrit:
तस्माद् भवन्तमनवद्यमनन्तपारं
सर्वज्ञमीश्वरमखण्डविकुण्ठधिष्ण्यम्।
निर्वेदधीरहरहर्व्रजिनाभितप्तो
नारायणं नरसखं शरणं प्रपद्ये॥ ११/७/१८॥
units.english: Therefore, O Lord, feeling weary of material life and tormented by its distresses, I now surrender unto You because You are the perfect master. You are the unlimited, all-knowing the Lord, whose spiritual abode in Vaikuṇṭha is free from all disturbances. In fact, You are known as Nārāyaṇa, the true friend of all living beings.

parts.sanskrit:
तस्माद् भवन्तमनवद्यमनन्तपारं
सर्वज्ञमीश्वरमखण्डविकुण्ठधिष्ण्यम्।
निर्वेदधीरहरहर्व्रजिनाभितप्तो
नारायणं नरसखं शरणं प्रपद्ये॥ ११/७/१८॥

“विष्णोर्वायोरनन्तस्य त्रिभिरंशैर्नरः स्मृतः।
सेन्द्रैश्चतुर्भिः पार्थस्तु द्वाभ्यां तु बललक्ष्मणौ॥”
इत्यंशविवेके॥ १८॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Therefore, O Lord, feeling weary of material life and tormented by its distresses, I now surrender unto You because You are the perfect master. You are the unlimited, all-knowing Supreme Personality of Godhead, whose spiritual abode in Vaikuṇṭha is free from all disturbances. In fact, You are known as Nārāyaṇa, the true friend of all living beings.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रायेण मनुजा लोके लोकतत्वविचक्षणाः।
समुद्धरन्ति ह्यात्मानमात्मनैवाशुभाशयात्॥ ११/७/१९॥
units.english: The Supreme Lord replied: Generally those human beings who can expertly analyze the actual situation of the material world are able to raise themselves beyond the inauspicious life of gross material gratification.

parts.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रायेण मनुजा लोके लोकतत्वविचक्षणाः।
समुद्धरन्ति ह्यात्मानमात्मनैवाशुभाशयात्॥ ११/७/१९॥

लोके तत्त्वे च विचक्षणाः।
“पारोक्ष्येणैव तत्त्वं तु लोकं चापि विदन्ति ये।
तेऽपि सत्स्नेहनिर्मुक्तास्तमो यान्ति विनिश्चयात्।
आपरोक्ष्यान्नच ज्ञानं तेषामुत्पद्यते क्वचित्॥”
इति षाड्गुण्ये॥ १९॥

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Lord replied: Generally those human beings who can expertly analyze the actual situation of the material world are able to raise themselves beyond the inauspicious life of gross material gratification.

units.sanskrit:
आत्मनो गुरुरात्मैव पुरुषस्य विशेषतः।
यत् प्रत्यक्षानुमानाभ्यां श्रेयोऽसावनुविन्दते॥ ११/७/२०॥
units.english: An intelligent person, expert in perceiving the world around him and in applying sound logic, can achieve real benefit through his own intelligence. Thus sometimes one acts as one’s own instructing teacher.

meta.english_verbatim: An intelligent person, expert in perceiving the world around him and in applying sound logic, can achieve real benefit through his own intelligence. Thus sometimes one acts as one’s own instructing spiritual master.

units.sanskrit:
पुरुषत्वे च मां धीराः साङ्ख्ययोगविशारदाः।
आविस्तारं प्रपश्यन्ति सर्वशक्त्युपबृंहितम्॥ ११/७/२१॥
units.english: In the human form of life, those who are self-controlled and expert in the spiritual science of Sāṅkhya can directly see Me along with all of My potencies.

meta.english_verbatim: In the human form of life, those who are self-controlled and expert in the spiritual science of Sāṅkhya can directly see Me along with all of My potencies.

units.sanskrit:
एकद्वित्रिचतुष्पादो बहुपादस्तथाऽपदः।
बह्व्यः सान्त पुरः सृष्टास्तासां मे पौरुषी प्रिया॥ ११/७/२२॥
units.english: In this world there are many kinds of created bodies — some with one leg, others with two, three, four or more legs, and still others with no legs — but of all these, the human form is actually dear to Me.

meta.english_verbatim: In this world there are many kinds of created bodies — some with one leg, others with two, three, four or more legs, and still others with no legs — but of all these, the human form is actually dear to Me.

units.sanskrit:
अत्र मां मार्गयन्त्यद्धा युक्ता हेतुभिरीश्वरम्।
गृह्यमाणैरात्मलिङ्गैः स्वबाह्यमनुमानतः॥ ११/७/२३॥
units.english: Although I, the Supreme Lord, can never be captured by ordinary sense perception, those situated in human life may use their intelligence and other faculties of perception to directly search for Me through both apparent and indirectly ascertained symptoms.

meta.english_verbatim: Although I, the Supreme Lord, can never be captured by ordinary sense perception, those situated in human life may use their intelligence and other faculties of perception to directly search for Me through both apparent and indirectly ascertained symptoms.

units.sanskrit:
अत्राप्युदाहरन्तीममितिहासं पुरातनम्।
अवधूतस्य संवादं यदोरमिततेजसः॥ ११/७/२४॥
units.english: In this regard, sages cite a historical narration concerning the conversation between the greatly powerful King Yadu and an avadhūta.

meta.english_verbatim: In this regard, sages cite a historical narration concerning the conversation between the greatly powerful King Yadu and an avadhūta.

units.sanskrit:
अवधूतं द्विजं कञ्चिच्चरन्तमकुतोभयम्।
कविं निरीक्ष्य निपुणं यदुः पप्रच्छ धर्मवित्॥ ११/७/२५॥
units.english: King Yadu once observed a certain brāhmaṇa avadhūta, who appeared to be quite young and learned, wandering about fearlessly. Being himself most learned in spiritual science, the King took the opportunity and inquired from him as follows.

meta.english_verbatim: Mahārāja Yadu once observed a certain brāhmaṇa avadhūta, who appeared to be quite young and learned, wandering about fearlessly. Being himself most learned in spiritual science, the King took the opportunity and inquired from him as follows.

units.sanskrit:
कुतो बुद्धिरियं ब्रह्मन्नकर्तुस्ते विशारदा।
यामासाद्य भवान् लोकान् विद्वांश्चरति बालवत्॥ ११/७/२६॥
units.english: Yadu said: O brāhmaṇa, I see that you are not engaged in any practical religious activity, and yet you have acquired a most expert understanding of all things and all people within this world. Kindly tell me, sir, how did you acquire this extraordinary intelligence, and why are you traveling freely throughout the world behaving as if you were a child?

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

meta.english_verbatim: Śrī Yadu said: O brāhmaṇa, I see that you are not engaged in any practical religious activity, and yet you have acquired a most expert understanding of all things and all people within this world. Kindly tell me, sir, how did you acquire this extraordinary intelligence, and why are you traveling freely throughout the world behaving as if you were a child?

units.sanskrit:
प्रायो धर्मार्थकामेषु विवित्सायां च मानवाः।
हेतुनैव समीहन्ते आयुषो यशसः श्रियः॥ ११/७/ २७॥
त्वं तु कल्यः कविर्दक्षः सुभगोऽमृतभाषणः।
न कर्तुमीहसे किञ्चिज्जडोन्मत्तपिशाचवत्॥ ११/७/२८॥
units.english: You, however, although capable, learned, expert, handsome and most eloquent, are not engaged in doing anything, nor do you desire anything; rather, you appear stupefied and maddened as if you were a ghostly creature.

meta.english_verbatim: You, however, although capable, learned, expert, handsome and most eloquent, are not engaged in doing anything, nor do you desire anything; rather, you appear stupefied and maddened as if you were a ghostly creature.

units.sanskrit:
जनेषु दह्यमानेषु कामलोभदवाग्निना।
न तप्यसेऽग्निना मुक्तो गङ्गाम्भःस्थ इव द्विपः॥ ११/७/२९॥
units.english: Although all people within the material world are burning in the great forest fire of lust and greed, you remain free and are not burned by that fire. You are just like an elephant who takes shelter from a forest fire by standing within the water of the Ganges River.

meta.english_verbatim: Although all people within the material world are burning in the great forest fire of lust and greed, you remain free and are not burned by that fire. You are just like an elephant who takes shelter from a forest fire by standing within the water of the Ganges River.

units.sanskrit:
त्वं हि नः पृच्छतां ब्रह्मन्नात्मन्यानन्दकारणम्।
ब्रूहि स्पर्शविहीनस्य भवतः केवलात्मनः॥ ११/७/३०॥
units.english: O brāhmaṇa, we see that you are devoid of any contact with material enjoyment and that you are traveling alone, without any companions or family members. Therefore, because we are sincerely inquiring from you, please tell us the cause of the great ecstasy that you are feeling within yourself.

parts.sanskrit:
त्वं हि नः पृच्छतां ब्रह्मन्नात्मन्यानन्दकारणम्।
ब्रूहि स्पर्शविहीनस्य भवतः केवलात्मनः॥ ११/७/३०॥
केवलात्मनः शरीरमात्रपरिग्रहस्य॥ ३०॥

meta.english_verbatim: O brāhmaṇa, we see that you are devoid of any contact with material enjoyment and that you are traveling alone, without any companions or family members. Therefore, because we are sincerely inquiring from you, please tell us the cause of the great ecstasy that you are feeling within yourself.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
यदुनैवं महाभागो ब्रह्मण्येन सुमेधसा।
पृष्टः सभाजितः प्राह प्रश्रयावनतं द्विजः॥ ११/७/३१॥
units.english: Lord Kṛṣṇa continued: The intelligent King Yadu, always respectful to the brāhmaṇas, waited with bowed head as the brāhmaṇa, pleased with the King’s attitude, began to reply.

meta.english_verbatim: Lord Kṛṣṇa continued: The intelligent King Yadu, always respectful to the brāhmaṇas, waited with bowed head as the brāhmaṇa, pleased with the King’s attitude, began to reply.

units.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
सन्ति मे गुरवो राजन् बहवो बुद्ध्युपाश्रिताः।
यतो बुद्धिमुपादाय मुक्तोऽटामीह तान् शृणु॥ ११/७/३२॥
units.english: The brāhmaṇa said: My dear King, with my intelligence I have taken shelter of many teachers. Having gained transcendental understanding from them, I now wander about the earth in a liberated condition. Please listen as I describe them to you.

meta.english_verbatim: The brāhmaṇa said: My dear King, with my intelligence I have taken shelter of many spiritual masters. Having gained transcendental understanding from them, I now wander about the earth in a liberated condition. Please listen as I describe them to you.

units.sanskrit:
पृथिवी वायुराकाश आपोऽग्निश्चन्द्रमा रविः।
कपोतोऽजगरः सिन्धुः पतङ्गो मधुकृद् गजः॥ ११/७/३३॥
मधुहा हरिणो मीनः पिङ्गळा कुररोऽर्भकः।
कुमारी शरकृत् सर्प ऊर्णनाभिः सुपेशकृत्॥ ११/७/३४॥
एते मे गुरवो राजन् चतुर्विंशतिराश्रिताः।
शिक्षावृत्तिभिरेतेषामन्वशिक्षमहं मनः॥ ११/७/३५॥
units.english: O King, I have taken shelter of twenty-four gurus, who are the following: the earth, air, sky, water, fire, moon, sun, pigeon and python; the sea, moth, honeybee, elephant and honey thief; the deer, the fish, the prostitute Piṅgalā, the kurara bird and the child; and the young girl, arrow maker, serpent, spider and wasp. My dear King, by studying their activities I have learned the science of the self.

meta.english_verbatim: O King, I have taken shelter of twenty-four gurus, who are the following: the earth, air, sky, water, fire, moon, sun, pigeon and python; the sea, moth, honeybee, elephant and honey thief; the deer, the fish, the prostitute Piṅgalā, the kurara bird and the child; and the young girl, arrow maker, serpent, spider and wasp. My dear King, by studying their activities I have learned the science of the self.

units.sanskrit:
यतो यदनुशिक्षामि यथा वा नाहुषात्मज।
तत् तथा पुरुषव्याघ्र निबोध कथयामि ते॥ ११/७/३६॥
units.english: Please listen, O son of King Yayāti, O tiger among men, as I explain to you what I have learned from each of these gurus.

meta.english_verbatim: Please listen, O son of Mahārāja Yayāti, O tiger among men, as I explain to you what I have learned from each of these gurus.

units.sanskrit:
भूतैराक्रम्यमाणोऽपि धीरो दैववशानुगैः।
तद्विदां न चलेन्मार्गादनुशिक्षन् क्षितेर्व्रतम्॥ ११/७/३७॥
units.english: A sober person, even when harassed by other living beings, should understand that his aggressors are acting helplessly under the control of God, and thus he should never be distracted from progress on his own path. This rule I have learned from the earth.

meta.english_verbatim: A sober person, even when harassed by other living beings, should understand that his aggressors are acting helplessly under the control of God, and thus he should never be distracted from progress on his own path. This rule I have learned from the earth.

units.sanskrit:
शश्वत् परार्थसर्वेहां परार्थैकान्तसम्भवम्।
साधुः शिक्षेत भूमेश्च अनुशिक्षं व्रतान्तरम्॥ ११/७/३८॥
units.english: A saintly person should learn from the mountain to devote all his efforts to the service of others and to make the welfare of others the sole reason for his existence. Similarly, as the disciple of the tree, he should learn to dedicate himself to others.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly person should learn from the mountain to devote all his efforts to the service of others and to make the welfare of others the sole reason for his existence. Similarly, as the disciple of the tree, he should learn to dedicate himself to others.

units.sanskrit:
प्राणवृत्त्यैव सन्तुष्येत् मुनिर्नैवेन्द्रियप्रियैः।
ज्ञानं यथा न नश्येत नावकार्येत वाङ्मनः॥ ११/७/३९॥
units.english: A learned sage should take his satisfaction in the simple maintenance of his existence and should not seek satisfaction through gratifying the material senses. In other words, one should care for the material body in such a way that one’s higher knowledge is not destroyed and so that one’s speech and mind are not deviated from self-realization.

meta.english_verbatim: A learned sage should take his satisfaction in the simple maintenance of his existence and should not seek satisfaction through gratifying the material senses. In other words, one should care for the material body in such a way that one’s higher knowledge is not destroyed and so that one’s speech and mind are not deviated from self-realization.

units.sanskrit:
विषयेष्वाविशन् योगी नानाधर्मेषु सर्वतः।
गुणदोषान्वयेनात्मा न विषज्जेत वायुवत्॥ ११/७/४०॥
units.english: Even a transcendentalist is surrounded by innumerable material objects, which possess good and bad qualities. However, one who has transcended material good and evil should not become entangled even when in contact with the material objects; rather, he should act like the wind.

meta.english_verbatim: Even a transcendentalist is surrounded by innumerable material objects, which possess good and bad qualities. However, one who has transcended material good and evil should not become entangled even when in contact with the material objects; rather, he should act like the wind.

units.sanskrit:
पार्थिवेष्विह देहेषु प्रविष्टस्तद्गुणाश्रयः।
गुणैर्न युज्यते योगी गन्धैर्वायुरिवात्मदृक्॥ ११/७/४१॥
units.english: Although a self-realized soul may live in various material bodies while in this world, experiencing their various qualities and functions, he is never entangled, just as the wind which carries various aromas does not actually mix with them.

meta.english_verbatim: Although a self-realized soul may live in various material bodies while in this world, experiencing their various qualities and functions, he is never entangled, just as the wind which carries various aromas does not actually mix with them.

units.sanskrit:
अन्तर्बहिश्च स्थिरजङ्गमेषु ब्रह्मात्मभावेन समन्वयेन।
व्याप्त्याऽव्यवच्छेदमसङ्गमात्मनो मुनिर्नभोवद् विततस्य भावयेत्॥ ११/७/४२॥
units.english: A thoughtful sage, even while living within a material body, should understand himself to be pure spirit soul. Similarly, one should see that the spirit soul enters within all forms of life, both moving and nonmoving, and that the individual souls are thus all-pervading. The sage should further observe that the Lord, as the Supreme Self, is simultaneously present within all things. Both the individual soul and the Supreme Self can be understood by comparing them to the nature of the sky: although the sky extends everywhere and everything rests within the sky, the sky does not mix with anything, nor can it be divided by anything.

parts.sanskrit:
अन्तर्बहिश्च स्थिरजङ्गमेषु ब्रह्मात्मभावेन समन्वयेन।
व्याप्त्याऽव्यवच्छेदमसङ्गमात्मनो मुनिर्नभोवद् विततस्य भावयेत्॥ ११/७/४२॥

परार्थैकान्तसम्भवम्। आत्मनो वृद्धिश्च परार्थेति।
“सज्जनार्थेऽनुमन्येत
ऐहिकीं वृद्धिमात्मनः।
पारत्रिकीमैहिकीं च प्रीतये गुरुदेवयोः।
देवतानां च सर्वेषां स्वोत्तमानां च सर्वशः॥”
इति च॥ ३८॥
“जीवान्तर्यामको विष्णुरात्मनामा समीरितः।
तस्य तु ब्रह्मरूपत्वाद् बहिरन्तस्तथैव च।
पश्येदाकाशवद् व्याप्तिमसङ्गत्वं च नित्यशः॥”
इति तन्त्रभागवते॥ ४२॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: A thoughtful sage, even while living within a material body, should understand himself to be pure spirit soul. Similarly, one should see that the spirit soul enters within all forms of life, both moving and nonmoving, and that the individual souls are thus all-pervading. The sage should further observe that the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as the Supersoul, is simultaneously present within all things. Both the individual soul and the Supersoul can be understood by comparing them to the nature of the sky: although the sky extends everywhere and everything rests within the sky, the sky does not mix with anything, nor can it be divided by anything.

units.sanskrit:
तेजोम्ब्वन्नमयैर्भावैर्मेघाद्यैर्वायुनेरितैः।
न स्पृश्यते नभस्तद्वत् कालसृष्टैर्गुणैः पुमान्॥ ११/७/४३॥
units.english: Although the mighty wind blows clouds and storms across the sky, the sky is never implicated or affected by these activities. Similarly, the spirit soul is not actually changed or affected by contact with the material nature. Although the living being enters within a body made of earth, water and fire, and although he is impelled by the three modes of nature created by eternal time, his eternal spiritual nature is never actually affected.

meta.english_verbatim: Although the mighty wind blows clouds and storms across the sky, the sky is never implicated or affected by these activities. Similarly, the spirit soul is not actually changed or affected by contact with the material nature. Although the living entity enters within a body made of earth, water and fire, and although he is impelled by the three modes of nature created by eternal time, his eternal spiritual nature is never actually affected.

units.sanskrit:
स्वच्छः प्रकृतितः स्निग्धो मधुरस्तीर्थवन्नृणाम्।
मुनिः पुनात्यघान्मित्रमीक्षणस्पर्शकार्तनैः॥ ११/७/४४॥
units.english: O King, a saintly person is just like water because he is free from all contamination, gentle by nature, and by speaking creates a beautiful vibration like that of flowing water. Just by seeing, touching or hearing such a saintly person, the living being is purified, just as one is cleansed by contact with pure water. Thus a saintly person, just like a holy place, purifies all those who contact him because he always chants the glories of the Lord.

meta.english_verbatim: O King, a saintly person is just like water because he is free from all contamination, gentle by nature, and by speaking creates a beautiful vibration like that of flowing water. units.sanskrit:
तेजस्वी तपसा दीप्तो दुर्धर्षो दूरभाजनः।
सर्वभक्षोऽपि युक्तात्मा नादत्ते पापमग्निवत्॥ ११/७/४५॥
units.english: Saintly persons become powerful by execution of austerities. Their consciousness is unshakable because they do not try to enjoy anything within the material world. Such naturally liberated sages accept foodstuffs that are offered to them by destiny, and if by chance they happen to eat contaminated food, they are not affected, just like fire, which burns up contaminated substances that are offered to it.

parts.sanskrit:
तेजस्वी तपसा दीप्तो दुर्धर्षो दूरभाजनः।
सर्वभक्षोऽपि युक्तात्मा नादत्ते पापमग्निवत्॥ ११/७/४५॥

“गुणान् जीवस्य चेष्टव्यान् सिद्धान् विष्णोर्गुणांस्तथा।
तत्तद्दृष्ट्या विचिन्वीत पृथगेव सुधीः सदा॥”
इति लोकतत्त्वे।
“मधु नाम सुखं विन्द्यान्माधुर्यं सुखहेतुता।
सुखे रतिर्वा सम्प्रोक्ता शब्दतत्त्वविचक्षणैः॥”
इति शब्दनिर्णये॥ ४४॥
दूरत एव भजनीयः।
“पराभवो धर्षणं
स्यादवज्ञानमथापि वा।
न तत् सत्सु सदा कुर्यात् सहशय्यासनं नच॥”
इति षाड्गुण्ये ॥ ४५॥

meta.english_verbatim: Saintly persons become powerful by execution of austerities. Their consciousness is unshakable because they do not try to enjoy anything within the material world. Such naturally liberated sages accept foodstuffs that are offered to them by destiny, and if by chance they happen to eat contaminated food, they are not affected, just like fire, which burns up contaminated substances that are offered to it.

units.sanskrit:
क्वचिच्छन्नः क्वचित् स्पष्ट उपास्यः श्रेय इच्छताम्।
भुङ्क्ते सर्वत्र दातॄणां दहन् प्रागुत्तराशुभम्॥ ११/७/४६॥
units.english: A saintly person, just like fire, sometimes appears in a concealed form and at other times reveals himself. For the welfare of the conditioned souls who desire real happiness, a saintly person may accept the worshipable position of teacher, and thus like fire he burns to ashes all the past and future sinful reactions of his worshipers by mercifully accepting their offerings.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly person, just like fire, sometimes appears in a concealed form and at other times reveals himself. For the welfare of the conditioned souls who desire real happiness, a saintly person may accept the worshipable position of spiritual master, and thus like fire he burns to ashes all the past and future sinful reactions of his worshipers by mercifully accepting their offerings.

units.sanskrit:
स्वमायया सृष्टमिदं सदसल्लक्षणं विभुः।
प्रविष्ट ईयते तत्तत्सरूपोऽग्निरिवैधसि॥ ११/७/४७॥
units.english: Just as fire manifests differently in pieces of wood of different sizes and qualities, the omnipotent Supreme Soul, having entered the bodies of higher and lower life forms created by His own potency, appears to assume the identity of each.

parts.sanskrit:
स्वमायया सृष्टमिदं सदसल्लक्षणं विभुः।
प्रविष्ट ईयते तत्तत्सरूपोऽग्निरिवैधसि॥ ११/७/४७॥

“जीवस्य च्छन्नतां शिक्षेत् प्रविष्टत्वं परात्मनः।
तत्तद्गुणविडम्बं च वह्नेः सर्वमथापि वा।
अल्पदारौ यथाऽल्पोऽग्निरेवमल्पशरीरगः।
दृश्यते परमात्माऽपि स्थूलः स्थूलशरीरगः॥”
इति वैभवे॥ ४६-४७॥

meta.english_verbatim: Just as fire manifests differently in pieces of wood of different sizes and qualities, the omnipotent Supreme Soul, having entered the bodies of higher and lower life forms created by His own potency, appears to assume the identity of each.

units.sanskrit:
विसर्गाद्याः श्मशानान्ता भावा देहस्य नात्मनः।
कलानामिव चन्द्रस्य कालेनाव्यक्तवर्त्मना॥ ११/७/४८॥
units.english: The various phases of one’s material life, beginning with birth and culminating in death, are all properties of the body and do not affect the soul, just as the apparent waxing and waning of the moon does not affect the moon itself. Such changes are enforced by the imperceptible movements of time.

meta.english_verbatim: The various phases of one’s material life, beginning with birth and culminating in death, are all properties of the body and do not affect the soul, just as the apparent waxing and waning of the moon does not affect the moon itself. Such changes are enforced by the imperceptible movements of time.

units.sanskrit:
कालनद्योघवेगेन भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ।
नित्यावपि न दृश्येते आत्मनोऽग्नेर्यथाऽर्चिषाम्॥ ११/७/४९॥
units.english: The flames of a fire appear and disappear at every moment, and yet this creation and destruction is not noticed by the ordinary observer. Similarly, the mighty waves of time flow constantly, like the powerful currents of a river, and imperceptibly cause the birth, growth and death of innumerable material bodies. And yet the soul, who is thus constantly forced to change his position, cannot perceive the actions of time.

parts.sanskrit:
कालनद्योघवेगेन भूतानां प्रभवाप्ययौ।
नित्यावपि न दृश्येते आत्मनोऽग्नेर्यथाऽर्चिषाम्॥ ११/७/४९॥

“अवयव्यवयवानां च गुणानां गुणिनस्तथा।
शक्तिशक्तिमतोश्चैव क्रियायास्तद्वतस्तथा।
स्वरूपांशांशिनोश्चैव नित्याभेदो जनार्दने।
जीवस्वरूपेषु तथा तथैव प्रकृतावपि।
चिद्रूपयामतोऽनंशा अगुणा अक्रिया इति।
हीना अवयवैश्चेति कथ्यन्ते तेऽत्यभेदतः।
पृथग्गुणाद्यभावाच्च नित्यत्वादुभयोरपि।
विष्णोरचिन्त्यशक्तेश्च सर्वं सम्भवति ध्रुवम्।
क्रियादेरपि नित्यत्वं व्यक्त्यव्यक्तिविशेषणम्।
भावाभावविशेषेण व्यवहारश्च तादृशः।
विशेषस्य विशिष्टस्याप्यभेदस्तद्वदेव तु।
सर्वं चाचिन्त्यशक्तित्वाद् युज्यते परमेश्वरे।
तच्छक्त्यैव तु जीवेषु चिद्रूपप्रकृतावपि।
भेदाभेदौ तदन्यत्र ह्युभयोरपि दर्शनात्।
कार्यकारणयोश्चापि निमित्तं कारणं विना॥”
इति ब्रह्मतर्के।
“आत्मनि चैवं विचित्राश्च हि” “सर्वोपेता च तद्दर्शनात्” “सर्वधर्मोपपत्तेश्च” “स्वाभाविकी ज्ञानबलक्रिया च” “यत्रा सप्तऋषीन् पर एकमाहुः” इत्यादेश्च।
“विना दोषांच्छ्रुतमद्धाऽवगम्यं तथा स्मृतं परमे सत्यरूपम्।
नैवासत्यं क्वचिदस्मिन् परेशे सर्वं युक्तं पूर्णशक्तेः सदैव॥”
इति च विश्वम्भरश्रुतिः।
तस्मादेकस्मिन्नपि शरीरे भेदाभेदात् प्रभवाप्ययौ युज्येते। नच विरोधः। स्थूलसूक्ष्मवत्। आपेक्षिकमत्रापि युज्यते॥ ४९॥

meta.english_verbatim: The flames of a fire appear and disappear at every moment, and yet this creation and destruction is not noticed by the ordinary observer. Similarly, the mighty waves of time flow constantly, like the powerful currents of a river, and imperceptibly cause the birth, growth and death of innumerable material bodies. And yet the soul, who is thus constantly forced to change his position, cannot perceive the actions of time.

units.sanskrit:
गुणैर्गुणानुपादत्ते यथाकालं विमुञ्चति।
न तेषु सज्जते योगी गोभिर्गा इव गोपतिः॥ ११/७/५०॥
units.english: Just as the sun evaporates large quantities of water by its potent rays and later returns the water to the earth in the form of rain, similarly, a saintly person accepts all types of material objects with his material senses, and at the appropriate time, when the proper person has approached him to request them, he returns such material objects. Thus, both in accepting and giving up the objects of the senses, he is not entangled.

meta.english_verbatim: Just as the sun evaporates large quantities of water by its potent rays and later returns the water to the earth in the form of rain, similarly, a saintly person accepts all types of material objects with his material senses, and at the appropriate time, when the proper person has approached him to request them, he returns such material objects. Thus, both in accepting and giving up the objects of the senses, he is not entangled.

units.sanskrit:
बुद्धिसंस्थेन भेदेन व्यक्तस्थ इव तद्गतः।
लक्ष्यते स्थूलमतिभिरात्मा चाम्बुस्थितार्कवत्॥ ११/७/५१॥
units.english: Even when reflected in various objects, the sun is never divided, nor does it merge into its reflection. Only those with dull brains would consider the sun in this way. Similarly, although the soul is reflected through different material bodies, the soul remains undivided and nonmaterial.

parts.sanskrit:
बुद्धिसंस्थेन भेदेन व्यक्तस्थ इव तद्गतः।
लक्ष्यते स्थूलमतिभिरात्मा चाम्बुस्थितार्कवत्॥ ११/७/५१॥

“बुद्धिसंस्थस्त्वात्मभेदो व्यक्तस्थो जीव उच्यते।
तेनैव सह संस्थानात् परात्मा स्थूलबुद्धिभिः।
जीववल्लक्ष्यते विष्णुर्यथैवाम्बुस्थितार्कवत्।
परमार्कः पारिमाण्याद् वर्तुलत्वादिना तथा।
अर्कस्वरूपानभिज्ञैः शिरःपादादिवर्जितः।
अचेतनश्च कल्प्येत तत्तेजोमात्रदर्शिभिः।
सूर्यदेहादिभिन्नं हि तेजोमण्डलमेव तु।
दृश्यते स्थूलमतिभिरेवमेव जनार्दनः॥”
इति प्रभासके॥ ५१॥

meta.english_verbatim: Even when reflected in various objects, the sun is never divided, nor does it merge into its reflection. Only those with dull brains would consider the sun in this way. Similarly, although the soul is reflected through different material bodies, the soul remains undivided and nonmaterial.

units.sanskrit:
नातिस्नेहः प्रसङ्गो वा कर्तव्यः क्वापि केनचित्।
कुर्वन् विन्देत सन्तापं कपोत इव दीनधीः॥ ११/७/५२॥
units.english: One should never indulge in excessive affection or concern for anyone or anything; otherwise one will have to experience great suffering, just like the foolish pigeon.

meta.english_verbatim: One should never indulge in excessive affection or concern for anyone or anything; otherwise one will have to experience great suffering, just like the foolish pigeon.

units.sanskrit:
कपोतः कश्चनारण्ये कृतनीडो वनस्पतौ।
कपोत्या भार्यया सार्धमुवास कतिचित् समाः॥ ११/७/५३॥
units.english: There once was a pigeon who lived in the forest along with his wife. He had built a nest within a tree and lived there for several years in her company.

meta.english_verbatim: There once was a pigeon who lived in the forest along with his wife. He had built a nest within a tree and lived there for several years in her company.

units.sanskrit:
कपोतौ स्नेहगुणितहृदयौ गृहधर्मिणौ।
दृष्टिं दृष्ट्याऽङ्गमङ्गेन बुद्धिं बुद्ध्या बबन्धतुः॥ ११/७/५४॥
units.english: The two pigeons were very much devoted to their household duties. Their hearts being tied together by sentimental affection, they were each attracted by the other’s glances, bodily features and states of mind. Thus, they completely bound each other in affection.

meta.english_verbatim: The two pigeons were very much devoted to their household duties. Their hearts being tied together by sentimental affection, they were each attracted by the other’s glances, bodily features and states of mind. Thus, they completely bound each other in affection.

units.sanskrit:
शय्यासनाटनस्थानवार्ताक्रीडाशनादिषु।
मिथुनीभूय विस्रब्धौ चेरतुर्वनराजिषु॥ ११/७/५५॥
units.english: Naively trusting in the future, they carried out their acts of resting, sitting, walking, standing, conversing, playing, eating and so forth as a loving couple among the trees of the forest.

meta.english_verbatim: Naively trusting in the future, they carried out their acts of resting, sitting, walking, standing, conversing, playing, eating and so forth as a loving couple among the trees of the forest.

units.sanskrit:
यद्यद् वाञ्छति सा राजन् तदर्थमनुकम्पितः।
तं तं समानयत् कामं कृच्छ्रेणाप्यजितेन्द्रियः॥ ११/७/५६॥
units.english: Whenever she desired anything, O King, the she-pigeon would flatteringly cajole her husband, and he in turn would gratify her by faithfully doing whatever she wanted, even with great personal difficulty. Thus, he could not control his senses in her association.

meta.english_verbatim: Whenever she desired anything, O King, the she-pigeon would flatteringly cajole her husband, and he in turn would gratify her by faithfully doing whatever she wanted, even with great personal difficulty. Thus, he could not control his senses in her association.

units.sanskrit:
कपोती प्रथमं गर्भं गृह्णती काल आगते।
अण्डानि सुषुवे नीडे स्वपत्युः सन्निधौ सती॥ ११/७/५७॥
units.english: Then the female pigeon experienced her first pregnancy. When the time arrived, the chaste lady delivered a number of eggs within the nest in the presence of her husband.

meta.english_verbatim: Then the female pigeon experienced her first pregnancy. When the time arrived, the chaste lady delivered a number of eggs within the nest in the presence of her husband.

units.sanskrit:
प्रजाः पुपुषतुः प्रीतौ दम्पती पुत्रवत्सलौ।
शृण्वन्तौ कूजितं तासां रवन्तौ कळभाषितैः॥ ११/७/ ५९॥
तासां पतत्रैः सुस्पर्शैः कूजितैर्मुखचेष्टितैः।
प्रत्युद्गमैरदीनानां पितरौ मुदमापतुः॥ ११/७/६०॥
units.english: The parent birds became very joyful by observing the soft wings of their children, their chirping, their lovely innocent movements around the nest and their attempts to jump up and fly. Seeing their children happy, the parents were also happy.

meta.english_verbatim: The parent birds became very joyful by observing the soft wings of their children, their chirping, their lovely innocent movements around the nest and their attempts to jump up and fly. Seeing their children happy, the parents were also happy.

units.sanskrit:
स्नेहबद्धानुहृदयावन्योन्यं विष्णुमायया।
विमोहितौ दीनधियौ शिशून् पुपुषतुः प्रजाः॥ ११/७/६१॥
units.english: Their hearts bound to each other by affection, the foolish birds, completely bewildered by the illusory energy of Lord Viṣṇu, continued to take care of the young offspring who had been born to them.

meta.english_verbatim: Their hearts bound to each other by affection, the foolish birds, completely bewildered by the illusory energy of Lord Viṣṇu, continued to take care of the young offspring who had been born to them.

units.sanskrit:
एकदा जग्मतुस्तासामशनार्थं कुडुम्बिनौ।
परितः कानने तस्मिन्नर्थिनौ चेरतुश्चिरम्॥ ११/७/६२॥
units.english: One day the two heads of the family went out to find food for the children. Being very anxious to feed their offspring properly, they wandered all over the forest for a long time.

meta.english_verbatim: One day the two heads of the family went out to find food for the children. Being very anxious to feed their offspring properly, they wandered all over the forest for a long time.

units.sanskrit:
दृष्ट्वा तान् लुब्धकः कश्चिद् यदृच्छातो वनेचरः।
जगृहे जालमातत्य चरतः स्वालयान्तिके॥ ११/७/६३॥
units.english: At that time a certain hunter who happened to be wandering through the forest saw the young pigeons moving about near their nest. Spreading out his net he captured them all.

meta.english_verbatim: At that time a certain hunter who happened to be wandering through the forest saw the young pigeons moving about near their nest. Spreading out his net he captured them all.

units.sanskrit:
कपोतश्च कपोती च प्रजापोषे सदोत्सुकौ।
गतौ पोषणमादाय स्वनीडमुपजग्मतुः॥ ११/७/६४॥
units.english: The pigeon and his wife were always anxious for the maintenance of their children, and they were wandering in the forest for that purpose. Having obtained proper food, they now returned to their nest.

meta.english_verbatim: The pigeon and his wife were always anxious for the maintenance of their children, and they were wandering in the forest for that purpose. Having obtained proper food, they now returned to their nest.

units.sanskrit:
कपोती स्वात्मजान् वीक्ष्य बालकान् जालसंवृतान्।
तानभ्यधावत् क्रोशन्ती क्रोशतो भृशदुःखिता॥ ११/७/६५॥
units.english: When the lady pigeon caught sight of her own children trapped within the hunter’s net, she was overwhelmed with anguish, and crying out, she rushed toward them as they cried out to her in return.

meta.english_verbatim: When the lady pigeon caught sight of her own children trapped within the hunter’s net, she was overwhelmed with anguish, and crying out, she rushed toward them as they cried out to her in return.

units.sanskrit:
साऽसकृत्स्नेहगुणिता दीनचित्ताऽजमायया।
स्वयं चाबध्यत सिचा१ बद्धान् पश्यन्त्यपस्मृतिः॥ ११/७/६६॥
units.english: The lady pigeon had always allowed herself to be bound by the ropes of intense material affection, and thus her mind was overwhelmed by anguish. Being in the grip of the illusory energy of the Lord, she completely forgot herself, and rushing forward to her helpless children, she was immediately bound in the hunter’s net.

meta.english_verbatim: The lady pigeon had always allowed herself to be bound by the ropes of intense material affection, and thus her mind was overwhelmed by anguish. Being in the grip of the illusory energy of the Lord, she completely forgot herself, and rushing forward to her helpless children, she was immediately bound in the hunter’s net.

units.sanskrit:
कपोतश्चात्मजान् बद्धानात्मनोऽप्यधिकप्रियान्।
भार्यां चात्मसमां दीनां विललापातिदुःखितः॥ ११/७/६७॥
units.english: Seeing his own children, who were more dear to him than life itself, fatally bound in the hunter’s net along with his dearmost wife, whom he considered equal in every way to himself, the poor male pigeon began to lament wretchedly.

meta.english_verbatim: Seeing his own children, who were more dear to him than life itself, fatally bound in the hunter’s net along with his dearmost wife, whom he considered equal in every way to himself, the poor male pigeon began to lament wretchedly.

units.sanskrit:
अहो मे पश्यतापायमल्पपुण्यस्य दुर्मतेः।
अतृप्तस्याकृतार्थस्य गृहस्त्रैवर्गिको हतः॥ ११/७/६८॥
units.english: The male pigeon said: Alas, just see how I am now destroyed! I am obviously a great fool, for I did not properly execute pious activities. I could not satisfy myself, nor could I fulfill the purpose of life. My dear family, which was the basis of my religiosity, economic development and sense enjoyment, is now hopelessly ruined.

units.sanskrit:
अनुरूपाऽनुकूला च यस्य मे पतिदेवता।
शून्ये गृहे मां संत्यज्य पुत्रैः स्वर्याति साधुभिः॥ ११/७/ ६९॥
सोऽहं शून्यगृहे दीनो मृतदारो मृतप्रजः।
जिजीविषे किमर्थं वा विधुरो दुःखजीवनः॥ ११/७/७०॥
units.english: Now I am a wretched person living in an empty home. My wife is dead; my children are dead. Why should I possibly want to live? My heart is so pained by separation from my family that life itself has become simply suffering.

meta.english_verbatim: Now I am a wretched person living in an empty home. My wife is dead; my children are dead. Why should I possibly want to live? My heart is so pained by separation from my family that life itself has become simply suffering.

units.sanskrit:
तांस्तथैवावृतान् सिग्भिर्मृत्युग्रस्तान् विचेष्टतः।
स्वयं च कृपणः सिक्षु पश्यन्नप्यबुधोऽपतत्॥ ११/७/७१॥
units.english: As the father pigeon wretchedly stared at his poor children trapped in the net and on the verge of death, pathetically struggling to free themselves, his mind went blank, and thus he himself fell into the hunter’s net.

meta.english_verbatim: As the father pigeon wretchedly stared at his poor children trapped in the net and on the verge of death, pathetically struggling to free themselves, his mind went blank, and thus he himself fell into the hunter’s net.

units.sanskrit:
तं लब्ध्वा लुब्धकः क्रूरः कपोतं गृहमेधिनम्।
कपोतकान् कपोतीं च सिद्धार्थः प्रययौ गृहम्॥ ११/७/७२॥
units.english: The cruel hunter, having fulfilled his desire by capturing the head pigeon, his wife and all of their children, set off for his own home.

meta.english_verbatim: The cruel hunter, having fulfilled his desire by capturing the head pigeon, his wife and all of their children, set off for his own home.

units.sanskrit:
एवं कुडुम्ब्यशान्तात्मा द्वन्द्वारामः पतत्रिवत्।
पुष्णन् कुडुम्बं कृपणः सानुबन्धोऽवसीदति॥ ११/७/७३॥
units.english: In this way, one who is too attached to family life becomes disturbed at heart. Like the pigeon, he tries to find pleasure in mundane sex attraction. Busily engaged in maintaining his own family, the miserly person is fated to suffer greatly, along with all his family members.

meta.english_verbatim: In this way, one who is too attached to family life becomes disturbed at heart. Like the pigeon, he tries to find pleasure in mundane sex attraction. Busily engaged in maintaining his own family, the miserly person is fated to suffer greatly, along with all his family members.

units.sanskrit:
यः प्राप्य मानुषं लोकं मुक्तिद्वारमपावृतम्।
गृहेषु खगवत् सक्तस्तमारूढच्युतं विदुः॥ ११/७/७४॥
units.english: The doors of liberation are opened wide to one who has achieved human life. But if a human being simply devotes himself to family life like the foolish bird in this story, then he is to be considered as one who has climbed to a high place only to trip and fall down.

meta.english_verbatim: The doors of liberation are opened wide to one who has achieved human life. But if a human being simply devotes himself to family life like the foolish bird in this story, then he is to be considered as one who has climbed to a high place only to trip and fall down.

units.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
सुखमौन्द्रयकं राजन् स्वर्गे नरक एव वा।
देहिनां यद् यथा दुःखं तस्मान्नेच्छेत तद् बुधः॥ ११/८/१॥
units.english: The saintly brāhmaṇa said: O King, the embodied living being automatically experiences unhappiness in heaven or hell. Similarly, happiness will also be experienced, even without one’s seeking it. Therefore a person of intelligent discrimination does not make any endeavor to obtain such material happiness.

Similarly, happiness will also be experienced, even without one’s seeking it. Therefore a person of intelligent discrimination does not make any endeavor to obtain such material happiness.

units.sanskrit:
शयीताहानि भूरीणि निराहारोऽनुपक्रमः।
यदि नोपनमेद् ग्रासो महाहिरिव दिष्टभुक्॥ ११/८/३॥
units.english: If at any time food does not come, then a saintly person should fast for many days without making endeavor. He should understand that by God’s arrangement he must fast. Thus, following the example of the python, he should remain peaceful and patient.

meta.english_verbatim: If at any time food does not come, then a saintly person should fast for many days without making endeavor. He should understand that by God’s arrangement he must fast. Thus, following the example of the python, he should remain peaceful and patient.

units.sanskrit:
ओजःसहोबलयुतं बिभ्रद् देहमकर्मकम्।
शयानो वीतनिद्रश्च नेहेतेन्द्रियवानपि॥ ११/८/४॥
units.english: A saintly person should remain peaceful and materially inactive, maintaining his body without much endeavor. Even though possessed of full sensual, mental and physical strength, a saintly person should not become active for material gain but rather should always remain alert to his actual self-interest.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly person should remain peaceful and materially inactive, maintaining his body without much endeavor. Even though possessed of full sensual, mental and physical strength, a saintly person should not become active for material gain but rather should always remain alert to his actual self-interest.

units.sanskrit:
मुनिः प्रसन्नगम्भीरो दुर्विगाह्यो दुरत्ययः।
अनन्तपारो ह्यक्षोभ्यः स्तिमितोद इवार्णवः॥ ११/८/५॥
units.english: A saintly sage is happy and pleasing in his external behavior, whereas internally he is most grave and thoughtful. Because his knowledge is immeasurable and unlimited he is never disturbed, and thus in all respects he is like the tranquil waters of the unfathomable and unsurpassable ocean.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly sage is happy and pleasing in his external behavior, whereas internally he is most grave and thoughtful. Because his knowledge is immeasurable and unlimited he is never disturbed, and thus in all respects he is like the tranquil waters of the unfathomable and unsurpassable ocean.

units.sanskrit:
समृद्धकामो हीनो वा नारायणपरो मुनिः।
नोत्सर्पेत न शुष्येत सरिद्भिरिव सागरः॥ ११/८/६॥
दृष्ट्वा स्त्रियं देवमायां तद्भावैरजितेन्द्रियः।
प्रलोभितः पतन्त्यन्धे तमस्यग्नौ पतङ्गवत्॥ ११/८/७॥
units.english: During the rainy season the swollen rivers rush into the ocean, and during the dry summer the rivers, now shallow, severely reduce their supply of water; yet the ocean does not swell up during the rainy season, nor does it dry up in the hot summer. In the same way, a saintly devotee who has accepted the Lord as the goal of his life sometimes will receive by providence great material opulence, and sometimes he will find himself materially destitute. However, such a devotee of the Lord does not rejoice in a flourishing condition, nor is he morose when poverty-stricken.

parts.sanskrit:
समृद्धकामो हीनो वा नारायणपरो मुनिः।
नोत्सर्पेत न शुष्येत सरिद्भिरिव सागरः॥ ११/८/६॥
दृष्ट्वा स्त्रियं देवमायां तद्भावैरजितेन्द्रियः।
प्रलोभितः पतन्त्यन्धे तमस्यग्नौ पतङ्गवत्॥ ११/८/७॥

“महतां वनिताकामः पतन्यन्धे तमस्यलम्।
अन्यत्र निरयं याति दुःखवान् स्याद् विपर्यये॥”
इति धर्मसंहितायाम्॥ ७॥
“मोहकारणभूतां तु मायेत्याहुर्मनीषिणः।
अविद्यमानं मेत्युक्तं तज्ज्ञापयति यत् स्वयम्।
कुत्रचिज्ज्ञानरूपं सल्लाभरूपं च भण्यते।
मयं प्राचुर्यमुद्दिष्टं माया स्यात् प्रचुरेत्यपि॥”
इति तन्त्रनिरुक्ते।
“स्वतन्त्रं परमार्थाख्यं स्वतन्त्रैका हरेर्मतिः।
सैव माया समुद्दिष्टा मुख्यतस्तत्स्वरूपिका।
मतिमन्मतिभेदोऽपि न विष्णोः क्वचिदिष्यते।
पारमार्थ्येन नास्त्येव तदन्यत् तद्वशं यतः।
अनाद्यनन्तकालेषु विद्यमानमपि ध्रुवम्।
अतो मायामयं प्राहुः सर्वं तद्वशगं यतः॥”
इति मायावैभवे।
“स्वाधीनं सदिति प्रोक्तं पराधीनमसत् स्मृतम्।
अविद्यमानमेतस्माज्जगदाहुर्विपश्चितः।
अनाद्यनन्तकालेषु विद्यमानमपि ध्रुवम्।
अस्वातन्त्र्यात् तु नास्त्येवेत्येवं वाच्यं जगत् सदा।
सदा वृत्तेर्विद्यमानमिति ब्रूयाद् यदि क्वचित्।
तथाऽपि नाशवद्धीदं प्रवाहाद्ध्यस्य नित्यता।
अतो निवर्त्यमित्याहुः प्रपञ्चो ह्यस्ति यद्यपि।
विष्णोरिच्छावशत्वाच्च मायामात्रमिति स्फुटम्।
परमार्थं त्वेकमेव स्वातन्त्र्याद् विष्णुमव्ययम्।
यदि कल्पयतीदं स स एव विनिवर्तयेत्।
विष्णुस्तस्मात् तद्वशत्वान्नास्तीति द्वैतमुच्यते।
स्वातन्त्र्येण हरौ ज्ञाते पराधीनत्वनिश्चयात्।
इत्याहुरुपदेष्टार आचार्यास्तत्त्ववेदिनः।
यथैव राजनि ज्ञाते नान्योऽस्तीति स्फुटं वचः।
स्वातन्त्र्यात् पारतन्त्र्याच्च तद्भृत्यादिषु सत्स्वपि।
यथैकच्छत्रवांश्चैव एकवीर इतीव च।
तथैव सर्वप्राधान्यादद्वितीयो हरिः स्मृतः।
एवं मुक्ता विजानन्ति सायुज्यं प्रापिता विभोः।
अनन्तकालं पश्यन्तो जगदेतच्चराचरम्।
तस्यैतस्य ह्यविज्ञानात् केवलभ्रान्तिरूपकम्।
जगदुक्त्वा तमो यान्ति ईशितव्येशशापतः॥”
इति च।
“पुत्रा मे यदि विद्यन्ते मरिष्यन्त्येव ते ध्रुवम्।
यदि राज्यं करोत्येष नश्यत्येतदसंशयम्॥”
इति धृतराष्ट्रवचनवत्, “प्रपञ्चो यदि विद्येत” इत्यादि।
“यदिशब्दस्त्ववस्तुत्वे चास्वातन्त्र्ये च संशये।
अवस्तुशब्दश्चाशक्ते ह्यल्पशक्तौ च कीर्त्यते॥”
इति शब्दनिर्णये॥ ७॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

However, such a devotee of the Lord does not rejoice in a flourishing condition, nor is he morose when poverty-stricken.

units.sanskrit:
योषित्सु तल्पशरणाभरणाम्बरादिद्रव्येषु१ मायारचितेषु मूढः।
प्रलोभितात्मा ह्युपभोगबुद्ध्या पतङ्गवन्नश्यति नष्टदृष्टिः॥ ११/८/८॥
units.english: One who has failed to control his senses immediately feels attraction upon seeing a woman’s form, which is created by the illusory energy of the Supreme Lord. Indeed, when the woman speaks with enticing words, smiles coquettishly and moves her body sensuously, his mind is immediately captured, and thus he falls blindly into the darkness of material existence, just as the moth maddened by the fire rushes blindly into its flames.

units.sanskrit:
स्तोकं स्तोकं ग्रसन् ग्रासं देहो वर्तेत यावता।
गृहान् व्रजेत् समातिष्ठन् वृत्तिं माधुकरीं मुनिः॥ ११/८/९॥
units.english: A foolish person with no intelligent discrimination is immediately aroused at the sight of a lusty woman beautifully decorated with golden ornaments, fine clothing and other cosmetic features. Being eager for sense enjoyment, such a fool loses all intelligence and is destroyed just like the moth who rushes into the blazing fire.

meta.english_verbatim: A foolish person with no intelligent discrimination is immediately aroused at the sight of a lusty woman beautifully decorated with golden ornaments, fine clothing and other cosmetic features. Being eager for sense gratification, such a fool loses all intelligence and is destroyed just like the moth who rushes into the blazing fire.

units.sanskrit:
अणुभ्यश्च महद्भ्यश्च शास्त्रेभ्यः कुशलो नरः।
सर्वतः सारमादद्यात् पुष्पेभ्य इव षट्पदः॥ ११/८/१०॥
units.english:
A saintly person should accept only enough food to keep his body and soul together. He should go from door to door accepting just a little bit of food from each family. Thus he should practice the occupation of the honeybee.
[Text 10] Just as the honeybee takes nectar from all flowers, big and small, an intelligent human being should take the essence from all religious scriptures.

units.sanskrit:
सायन्तनं श्वस्तनं वा न सङ्गृह्णीत भिक्षितम्।
पाणिपात्रोदरामत्रो मक्षिकेव न सङ्ग्रही।
मक्षिका इव सङ्गृह्णन् सह तेन विनश्यति॥ ११/८/११॥
units.english: A saintly person should not think, “This food I will keep to eat tonight and this other food I can save for tomorrow.” In other words, a saintly person should not store foodstuffs acquired by begging. Rather, he should use his own hands as his plate and eat whatever fits on them. His only storage container should be his belly, and whatever conveniently fits into his belly should be his stock of food. Thus one should not imitate the greedy honeybee who eagerly collects more and more honey.

units.sanskrit:
पदाऽपि युवतीं भिक्षुर्न स्पृशेद् दारवीमपि।
स्पृशन् करीव बध्येत करिण्या अङ्गसङ्गतः॥ ११/८/१२॥
units.english: A saintly mendicant should not even collect foodstuffs to eat later in the same day or the next day. If he disregards this injunction and like the honeybee collects more and more delicious foodstuffs, that which he has collected will indeed ruin him.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly mendicant should not even collect foodstuffs to eat later in the same day or the next day. If he disregards this injunction and like the honeybee collects more and more delicious foodstuffs, that which he has collected will indeed ruin him.

units.sanskrit:
नाधिगच्छेत् स्त्रियं प्राज्ञः कर्हिचिन्मृत्युमात्मनः।
बलाधिकैर्विहन्येत गजैरन्यैर्गजो यथा॥ ११/८/१३॥
units.english: A saintly person should never touch a young girl. In fact, he should not even let his foot touch a wooden doll in the shape of a woman. By bodily contact with a woman he will surely be captured by illusion, just as the elephant is captured by the she-elephant due to his desire to touch her body.

units.sanskrit:
न देयं नोपभोग्यं च लुब्धैर्यद् दुःखसञ्चितम्।
भुङ्क्ते स्वमपि तच्चान्यो मधुहेवार्थविन्मधु॥ ११/८/१४॥
units.english: A greedy person accumulates a large quantity of money with great struggle and pain, but the person who has struggled so much to acquire this wealth is not always allowed to enjoy it himself or give it in charity to others. The greedy man is like the bee who struggles to produce a large quantity of honey, which is then stolen by a man who will enjoy it personally or sell it to others. No matter how carefully one hides his hard-earned wealth or tries to protect it, there are those who are expert in detecting the whereabouts of valuable things, and they will steal it.

units.sanskrit:
सुदुःखोपार्जितैर्वित्तैराशासानां गृहाशिषः।
मधुहेवाग्रतो भुङ्क्ते यतिर्वै गृहमेधिनाम्॥ ११/८/१५॥
units.english: Just as a hunter takes away the honey laboriously produced by the honeybees, similarly, saintly mendicants such as brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs are entitled to enjoy the property painstakingly accumulated by householders dedicated to family enjoyment.

meta.english_verbatim: Just as a hunter takes away the honey laboriously produced by the honeybees, similarly, saintly mendicants such as brahmacārīs and sannyāsīs are entitled to enjoy the property painstakingly accumulated by householders dedicated to family enjoyment.

units.sanskrit:
ग्राम्यगीतं न शृणुयाद् यतिर्वनचरः क्वचित्।
शिक्षेऽहं हरिणाद् बद्धान्मृगयोर्गीतमोहितात्॥ ११/८/१६॥
units.english: A saintly person dwelling in the forest in the renounced order of life should never listen to songs or music promoting material enjoyment. Rather, a saintly person should carefully study the example of the deer, who is bewildered by the sweet music of the hunter’s horn and is thus captured and killed.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly person dwelling in the forest in the renounced order of life should never listen to songs or music promoting material enjoyment. Rather, a saintly person should carefully study the example of the deer, who is bewildered by the sweet music of the hunter’s horn and is thus captured and killed.

units.sanskrit:
नृत्यवादित्रगीतानि जुषन् ग्राम्याणि योषिताम्।
आसां क्रीडनकान्धः स्याद् ऋष्यशृङ्गो मुनिर्यथा॥ ११/८/१७॥
units.english:
Becoming attracted to the worldly singing, dancing and musical entertainment of beautiful women, even the great sage Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, the son of a deer, fell totally under their control, just like a pet animal.
[Text 19] Just as a fish, incited by the desire to enjoy his tongue, is fatally trapped on the fisherman’s hook, similarly, a foolish person is bewildered by the extremely disturbing urges of the tongue and thus is ruined.

units.sanskrit:
जिह्वयाऽतिप्रमाथिन्या जनो रसविमोहितः।
मृत्युमृच्छत्यतद्बुद्धिमत्स्यस्तु बिळशैर्यथा॥ ११/८/१८॥
units.english: By fasting, learned men quickly bring all of the senses except the tongue under control, because by abstaining from eating such men are afflicted with an increased desire to gratify the sense of taste.

meta.english_verbatim: By fasting, learned men quickly bring all of the senses except the tongue under control, because by abstaining from eating such men are afflicted with an increased desire to gratify the sense of taste.

units.sanskrit:
तावज्जितेन्द्रियो न स्याद् विजितान्येन्द्रियः पुमान्।
न जयेद् रसनं यावज्जितं सर्वं जिते रसे॥ ११/८/२०॥
units.english: Although one may conquer all of the other senses, as long as the tongue is not conquered it cannot be said that one has controlled his senses. However, if one is able to control the tongue, then one is understood to be in full control of all the senses.

meta.english_verbatim: Although one may conquer all of the other senses, as long as the tongue is not conquered it cannot be said that one has controlled his senses. However, if one is able to control the tongue, then one is understood to be in full control of all the senses.

units.sanskrit:
पिङ्गळा नाम वेश्याऽऽसीद् विदेहनगरे पुरा।
तस्याः संशिक्षितं किञ्चिन्निबोध नृपसत्तम॥ ११/८/२१॥
units.english:
O son of kings, previously in the city of Videha there dwelled a prostitute named Piṅgalā. Now please hear what I have learned from that lady.
[Text 23] Once that prostitute, desiring to bring a lover into her house, stood outside in the doorway at night showing her beautiful form.

meta.english_verbatim:

units.sanskrit:
मार्ग आगच्छतो वीक्ष्य पुरुषान् पुरुषर्षभ।
तान् शुल्कदान् वित्तवतः कान्तान् मेनेऽर्थकामुका॥ ११/८/२३॥
units.english: O best among men, this prostitute was very anxious to get money, and as she stood on the street at night she studied all the men who were passing by, thinking, “Oh, this one surely has money. I know he can pay the price, and I am sure he would enjoy my company very much.” Thus she thought about all the men on the street.

units.sanskrit:
आगतेष्वपयातेषु सा सङ्केतोपजीवना।
अप्यन्यो वित्तवान् कोपि मामुपेष्यति भूरिदः॥ ११/८/२४॥
units.english: As the prostitute Piṅgalā stood in the doorway, many men came and went, walking by her house. Her only means of sustenance was prostitution, and therefore she anxiously thought, “Maybe this one who is coming now is very rich… Oh, he is not stopping, but I am sure someone else will come. Surely this man who is coming now will want to pay me for my love, and he will probably give lots of money.” Thus, with vain hope, she remained leaning against the doorway, unable to finish her business and go to sleep. Out of anxiety she would sometimes walk out toward the street, and sometimes she went back into her house. In this way, the midnight hour gradually arrived.

units.sanskrit:
एवं दुराशयध्वस्तनिद्रा द्वार्यवलम्बती।
निर्गच्छन्ती प्रविशती निशीथं समपद्यत॥ ११/८/२५॥
units.english: As the night wore on, the prostitute, who intensely desired money, gradually became morose, and her face dried up. Thus being filled with anxiety for money and most disappointed, she began to feel a great detachment from her situation, and happiness arose in her mind.

meta.english_verbatim: As the night wore on, the prostitute, who intensely desired money, gradually became morose, and her face dried up. Thus being filled with anxiety for money and most disappointed, she began to feel a great detachment from her situation, and happiness arose in her mind.

units.sanskrit:
तस्या वित्ताशया शुष्यद्वक्त्राया दीनचेतसः।
निर्वेदः प्रथमो जज्ञे चिन्ताहेतिः सुखावहः॥ ११/८/२६॥
units.english: The prostitute felt disgusted with her material situation and thus became indifferent to it. Indeed, detachment acts like a sword, cutting to pieces the binding network of material hopes and desires. Now please hear from me the song sung by the prostitute in that situation.

meta.english_verbatim: The prostitute felt disgusted with her material situation and thus became indifferent to it. Indeed, detachment acts like a sword, cutting to pieces the binding network of material hopes and desires. Now please hear from me the song sung by the prostitute in that situation.

units.sanskrit: तथा निर्विण्णचित्ताया गीतं शृणु यथा मम॥ ११/८/२७॥
units.english: O King, just as a human being who is bereft of spiritual knowledge never desires to give up his false sense of proprietorship over many material things, similarly, a person who has not developed detachment never desires to give up the bondage of the material body.

meta.english_verbatim: O King, just as a human being who is bereft of spiritual knowledge never desires to give up his false sense of proprietorship over many material things, similarly, a person who has not developed detachment never desires to give up the bondage of the material body.

units.sanskrit:
निर्वेद आशापाशानां पुरुषस्य यथा ह्यसिः।
नह्यङ्गाजातनिर्वेदो देहबन्धं जिहासति॥ ११/८/२८॥
पिङ्गळोवाच
अहो मे मोहविततिं पश्यताविजितात्मनः।
या कान्ताद् व्रजतः कामं कामये येन बालिशा॥ ११/८/२९॥
units.english: The prostitute Piṅgalā said: Just see how greatly illusioned I am! Because I cannot control my mind, just like a fool I desire lusty pleasure from an insignificant man.

meta.english_verbatim: The prostitute Piṅgalā said: Just see how greatly illusioned I am! Because I cannot control my mind, just like a fool I desire lusty pleasure from an insignificant man.

units.sanskrit:
सन्तं समीपे रमणं रतिप्रदं वित्तप्रदं नित्यमिमं विहाय।
अकामदं दुःखभयाधिशोकमोहप्रदं तुच्छमहं वृणेऽज्ञा॥ ११/८/३०॥
units.english: I am such a fool that I have given up the service of that person who, being eternally situated within my heart, is actually most dear to me. That most dear one is the Lord of the universe, who is the bestower of real love and happiness and the source of all prosperity. Although He is in my own heart, I have completely neglected Him. Instead I have ignorantly served insignificant men who can never satisfy my real desires and who have simply brought me unhappiness, fear, anxiety, lamentation and illusion.

Instead I have ignorantly served insignificant men who can never satisfy my real desires and who have simply brought me unhappiness, fear, anxiety, lamentation and illusion.

units.sanskrit:
अहो मयाऽऽत्मा परितापितो वृथा साङ्केत्यवृत्त्याऽतिविगर्ह्यवार्तया।
स्त्रैणान् नरांश्चार्थतृषाऽनुशोच्यान् क्रात्वा हि वित्तं रतिमात्मनेच्छती॥ ११/८/३१॥
units.english: Oh, how I have uselessly tortured my own soul! I have sold my body to lusty, greedy men who are themselves objects of pity. Thus practicing the most abominable profession of a prostitute, I hoped to get money and sex pleasure.

meta.english_verbatim: Oh, how I have uselessly tortured my own soul! I have sold my body to lusty, greedy men who are themselves objects of pity. Thus practicing the most abominable profession of a prostitute, I hoped to get money and sex pleasure.

units.sanskrit:
यदस्थिभिर्निर्मितवंशवंश्यस्थूणं त्वचारोमनखैः पिनद्धम्।
क्षरन्नवद्वारमगारमेतद् विण्मूत्रपूर्णं मदुपैति काऽन्या॥ ११/८/३२॥
units.english: This material body is like a house in which I, the soul, am living. The bones forming my spine, ribs, arms and legs are like the beams, crossbeams and pillars of the house, and the whole structure, which is full of stool and urine, is covered by skin, hair and nails. The nine doors leading into this body are constantly excreting foul substances. Besides me, what woman could be so foolish as to devote herself to this material body, thinking that she might find pleasure and love in this contraption?

meta.english_verbatim: This material body is like a house in which I, the soul, am living. The nine doors leading into this body are constantly excreting foul substances. Besides me, what woman could be so foolish as to devote herself to this material body, thinking that she might find pleasure and love in this contraption?

units.sanskrit:
विदेहानां पुरे ह्यस्मिन् अहमैकैव मूढधीः।
याऽन्यमिच्छन्त्यतः स्वस्मादन्यस्मात् कान्तमच्युतात्॥ ११/८/३३॥
units.english: Certainly in this city of Videha I alone am completely foolish. I neglected the Lord, who awards us everything, even our original spiritual form, and instead I desired to enjoy sense enjoyment with many men.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Certainly in this city of Videha I alone am completely foolish. I neglected the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who awards us everything, even our original spiritual form, and instead I desired to enjoy sense gratification with many men.

units.sanskrit:
सुहृत् प्रेष्ठतमो नाथ आत्मा चायं शरीरिणाम्।
तं विक्रायात्मनैवाहं रमेऽनेन यथा रमा॥ ११/८/३४॥
units.english: The Lord is absolutely the most dear one for all living beings because He is everyone’s well-wisher and Lord. He is the Supreme Soul situated in everyone’s heart. Therefore I will now pay the price of complete surrender, and thus purchasing the Lord I will enjoy with Him just like Lakṣmīdevī.

parts.sanskrit:
सुहृत् प्रेष्ठतमो नाथ आत्मा चायं शरीरिणाम्।
तं विक्रायात्मनैवाहं रमेऽनेन यथा रमा॥ ११/८/३४॥

“भगवद्भार्यतायोग्याः काश्चिदप्सरसःस्त्रियः।
रमावेशात् कदाचित् स्युस्तास्वेका पिङ्गलाऽभवत्।
तदन्यासां महान् दोषो भगवद्भर्तृतास्मृतौ॥”
इति स्वाभाव्ये॥ ३४॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord
