units.sanskrit:
कियत् प्रियं ते व्यभजन् कामान् मे कामदा नराः।
आद्यान्तवन्तो भार्याया देवा वा कालविद्रुताः॥ ११/८/३५॥
units.english: Men provide sense enjoyment for women, but all these men, and even the gods in heaven, have a beginning and an end. They are all temporary creations who will be dragged away by time. Therefore how much actual pleasure or happiness could any of them ever give to their wives?

meta.english_verbatim: Men provide sense gratification for women, but all these men, and even the demigods in heaven, have a beginning and an end. They are all temporary creations who will be dragged away by time. Therefore how much actual pleasure or happiness could any of them ever give to their wives?

units.sanskrit:
नूनं मे भगवान् प्रीतो विष्णुः केनापि कर्मणा।
निर्वेदोऽयं दुराशाया यन्मे जातः सुखावहः॥ ११/८/३६॥
मैवं स्युर्मन्दभाग्यायाः क्लेशा निर्वेदहेतवः।
येनानुबन्धं निर्हृत्य पुरुषः शममृच्छति॥ ११/८/३७॥
units.english: Although I most stubbornly hoped to enjoy the material world, somehow or other detachment has arisen in my heart, and it is making me very happy. Therefore the Lord, Viṣṇu, must be pleased with me. Without even knowing it, I must have performed some activity satisfying to Him.

meta.english_verbatim: Although I most stubbornly hoped to enjoy the material world, somehow or other detachment has arisen in my heart, and it is making me very happy. Therefore the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Viṣṇu, must be pleased with me. Without even knowing it, I must have performed some activity satisfying to Him.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

units.sanskrit:
तेनोपकृतमादाय शिरसा ग्राम्यसङ्गताः।
त्यक्त्वा दुराशाः शरणं व्रजामि तमधीश्वरम्॥ ११/८/३८॥
units.english: A person who has developed detachment can give up the bondage of material society, friendship and love, and a person who undergoes great suffering gradually becomes, out of hopelessness, detached and indifferent to the material world. Thus, due to my great suffering, such detachment awoke in my heart; yet how could I have undergone such merciful suffering if I were actually unfortunate? Therefore, I am in fact fortunate and have received the mercy of the Lord. He must somehow or other be pleased with me.

meta.english_verbatim: A person who has developed detachment can give up the bondage of material society, friendship and love, and a person who undergoes great suffering gradually becomes, out of hopelessness, detached and indifferent to the material world. Thus, due to my great suffering, such detachment awoke in my heart; yet how could I have undergone such merciful suffering if I were actually unfortunate? Therefore, I am in fact fortunate and have received the mercy of the Lord. He must somehow or other be pleased with me.

units.sanskrit:
सन्तुष्टा श्रद्धधत्येतद्७ यथालाभेन जीवती।
विहराम्यमुनैवाहमात्मना रमणेन वै॥ ११/८/३९॥
units.english: I am now completely satisfied, and I have full faith in the Lord’s mercy. Therefore I will maintain myself with whatever comes of its own accord. I shall enjoy life with only the Lord, because He is the real source of love and happiness.

meta.english_verbatim: I am now completely satisfied, and I have full faith in the Lord’s mercy. Therefore I will maintain myself with whatever comes of its own accord. I shall enjoy life with only the Lord, because He is the real source of love and happiness.

units.sanskrit:
संसारकूपे पतितं विषयैर्मुषितेक्षणम्।
ग्रस्तं कालाहिनाऽऽत्मानं कोऽन्योऽस्मात् त्रातुमीश्वरः॥ ११/८/४०॥
units.english: The intelligence of the living being is stolen away by activities of sense enjoyment, and thus he falls into the dark well of material existence. Within that well he is then seized by the deadly serpent of time. Who else but the Lord could save the poor living being from such a hopeless condition?

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The intelligence of the living entity is stolen away by activities of sense gratification, and thus he falls into the dark well of material existence. Within that well he is then seized by the deadly serpent of time. Who else but the Supreme Personality of Godhead could save the poor living entity from such a hopeless condition?

units.sanskrit:
आत्मैव ह्यात्मनो गोप्ता निर्विद्येत यदाऽखिलात्।
अप्रमत्त इदं पश्येद् ग्रस्तं कालाहिना जगत्॥ ११/८/४१॥
units.english: When the living being sees that the entire universe has been seized by the serpent of time, he becomes sober and sane and at that time detaches himself from all material sense enjoyment. In that condition the living being is qualified to be his own protector.

meta.english_verbatim: When the living entity sees that the entire universe has been seized by the serpent of time, he becomes sober and sane and at that time detaches himself from all material sense gratification. In that condition the living entity is qualified to be his own protector.

units.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
एवं व्यवसितमतिर्दुराशाः कान्ततर्षजाः।
छित्त्वोपशममास्थाय शय्यामुपविवेश ह॥ ११/८/४२॥
units.english: The avadhūta said: Thus, her mind completely made up, Piṅgalā cut off all her sinful desires to enjoy sex pleasure with lovers, and she became situated in perfect peace. Then she sat down on her bed.

meta.english_verbatim: The avadhūta said: Thus, her mind completely made up, Piṅgalā cut off all her sinful desires to enjoy sex pleasure with lovers, and she became situated in perfect peace. Then she sat down on her bed.

units.sanskrit:
आशा हि परमं दुःखं नैराश्यं परमं सुखम्।
यथा सञ्छिद्य कान्ताशां सुखं सुष्वाप पिङ्गळा॥ ११/८/४३॥
units.english: Material desire is undoubtedly the cause of the greatest unhappiness, and freedom from such desire is the cause of the greatest happiness. Therefore, completely cutting off her desire to enjoy so-called lovers, Piṅgalā very happily went to sleep.

meta.english_verbatim: Material desire is undoubtedly the cause of the greatest unhappiness, and freedom from such desire is the cause of the greatest happiness. Therefore, completely cutting off her desire to enjoy so-called lovers, Piṅgalā very happily went to sleep.

units.sanskrit:
ब्राह्मण उवाच
परिग्रहो हि दुःखाय यद्यत् प्रियतमं नृणाम्।
अनन्तसुखमाप्नोति तद् विद्वान् यस्त्वकिञ्चनः॥ ११/९/१॥
units.english: The saintly brāhmaṇa said: Everyone considers certain things within the material world to be most dear to him, and because of attachment to such things one eventually becomes miserable. One who understands this gives up material possessiveness and attachment and thus achieves unlimited happiness.

meta.english_verbatim: The saintly brāhmaṇa said: Everyone considers certain things within the material world to be most dear to him, and because of attachment to such things one eventually becomes miserable. One who understands this gives up material possessiveness and attachment and thus achieves unlimited happiness.

units.sanskrit:
न मे मानावमानौ स्तो न चिन्ता येह पुत्रिणाम्।
आत्मक्राड आत्मरतो विचरामीह बालवत्॥ ११/९/३॥
units.english: In family life, the parents are always in anxiety about their home, children and reputation. But I have nothing to do with these things. I do not worry at all about any family, and I do not care about honor and dishonor. I enjoy only the life of the soul, and I find love on the spiritual platform. Thus I wander the earth like a child.

meta.english_verbatim: In family life, the parents are always in anxiety about their home, children and reputation. But I have nothing to do with these things. I do not worry at all about any family, and I do not care about honor and dishonor. I enjoy only the life of the soul, and I find love on the spiritual platform. Thus I wander the earth like a child.

units.sanskrit:
द्वावेव चिन्तया मुक्तौ परमानन्द आप्लुतौ।
यो विमूढो जडो बालो यो गुणेभ्यः परं गतः॥ ११/९/४॥
units.english: In this world two types of people are free from all anxiety and merged in great happiness: one who is a retarded and childish fool and one who has approached the Supreme Lord, who is beyond the three modes of material nature.

meta.english_verbatim: In this world two types of people are free from all anxiety and merged in great happiness: one who is a retarded and childish fool and one who has approached the Supreme Lord, who is beyond the three modes of material nature.

units.sanskrit:
क्वचित् कुमारी त्वात्मानं वृण्वानान् गृहमागतान्।
स्वयं तानर्हयामास क्वापि यातेषु बन्धुषु॥ ११/९/५॥
units.english: Once a marriageable young girl was alone in her house because her parents and relatives had gone that day to another place. At that time a few men arrived at the house, specifically desiring to marry her. She received them with all hospitality.

meta.english_verbatim: Once a marriageable young girl was alone in her house because her parents and relatives had gone that day to another place. At that time a few men arrived at the house, specifically desiring to marry her. She received them with all hospitality.

units.sanskrit:
तेषामभ्यवहारार्थं शालीन् दृषदि पार्थिव।
अवघ्नन्त्याः प्रकोष्ठस्थाः शङ्खाश्चक्रुः स्वनं महत्॥ ११/९/६॥
units.english: The girl went to a private place and began to make preparations so that the unexpected male guests could eat. As she was beating the rice, the conchshell bracelets on her arms were colliding and making a loud noise.

meta.english_verbatim: The girl went to a private place and began to make preparations so that the unexpected male guests could eat. As she was beating the rice, the conchshell bracelets on her arms were colliding and making a loud noise.

units.sanskrit:
सा तं जुगुप्सितं मत्वा महती व्रीळिता ततः।
बभञ्जैकैकशः शङ्खान् द्वौ द्वौ पाण्योरशेषयत्॥ ११/९/७॥
units.english: The young girl feared that the men would consider her family to be poor because their daughter was busily engaged in the menial task of husking rice. Being very intelligent, the shy girl broke the shell bracelets from her arms, leaving just two on each wrist.

meta.english_verbatim: The young girl feared that the men would consider her family to be poor because their daughter was busily engaged in the menial task of husking rice. Being very intelligent, the shy girl broke the shell bracelets from her arms, leaving just two on each wrist.

units.sanskrit:
उभयोरप्यभूद् घोषो अवघ्नन्त्याः स्म शङ्खयोः।
तत्राप्येकं निरभिनदेकस्मान्नाभवद् ध्वनिः॥ ११/९/८॥
units.english: Thereafter, as the young girl continued to husk the rice, the two bracelets on each wrist continued to collide and make noise. Therefore she took one bracelet off each arm, and with only one left on each wrist there was no more noise.

meta.english_verbatim: Thereafter, as the young girl continued to husk the rice, the two bracelets on each wrist continued to collide and make noise. Therefore she took one bracelet off each arm, and with only one left on each wrist there was no more noise.

units.sanskrit:
अनुशिक्ष इमं तस्या उपदेशमरिन्दम।
लोकाननुचरन्नेतॉल्लोकतत्वविवित्सया॥ ११/९/९॥
units.english: O subduer of the enemy, I travel throughout the surface of the earth learning constantly about the nature of this world, and thus I personally witnessed the lesson of the young girl.

meta.english_verbatim: O subduer of the enemy, I travel throughout the surface of the earth learning constantly about the nature of this world, and thus I personally witnessed the lesson of the young girl.

units.sanskrit:
वासो बहूनां कलहो भवेद् वार्ता द्वयोरपि।
एक एव चरेत् तस्मात् कुमार्या इव कङ्कणः॥ ११/९/१०॥
units.english: When many people live together in one place there will undoubtedly be quarreling. And even if only two people live together there will be frivolous conversation and disagreement. Therefore, to avoid conflict, one should live alone, as we learn from the example of the bracelet of the young girl.

parts.sanskrit:
वासो बहूनां कलहो भवेद् वार्ता द्वयोरपि।
एक एव चरेत् तस्मात् कुमार्या इव कङ्कणः॥ ११/९/१०॥

“असज्जनैस्तु संवासो न कर्तव्यः कथञ्चन।
यावद्यावच्च बहुभिः सज्जनैः स तु मुक्तिदः॥”
इति षाड्गुण्ये ॥ १०॥

meta.english_verbatim: When many people live together in one place there will undoubtedly be quarreling. And even if only two people live together there will be frivolous conversation and disagreement. Therefore, to avoid conflict, one should live alone, as we learn from the example of the bracelet of the young girl.

units.sanskrit:
मन एकत्र संयुञ्ज्याज्जितश्वासो जितासनः।
वैराग्याभ्यासयोगेन ह्वियमाणमतन्द्रितः॥ ११/९/११॥
units.english: Having perfected the yoga sitting postures and conquered the breathing process, one should make the mind steady by detachment and the regulated practice of yoga. Thus one should carefully fix the mind on the single goal of yoga practice.

meta.english_verbatim: Having perfected the yoga sitting postures and conquered the breathing process, one should make the mind steady by detachment and the regulated practice of yoga. Thus one should carefully fix the mind on the single goal of yoga practice.

units.sanskrit:
यस्मिन् मनो लब्धपदं यदेतच्छनैःशनैर्मुञ्चति कर्मरेणून्।
सत्वेन वृद्धेन रजस्तमश्च विधूय निर्वाणमुपैत्यनिन्धनम्॥ ११/९/१२॥
units.english: The mind can be controlled when it is fixed on the Lord. Having achieved a stable situation, the mind becomes free from polluted desires to execute material activities; thus as the mode of goodness increases in strength, one can completely give up the modes of passion and ignorance, and gradually one transcends even the material mode of goodness. When the mind is freed from the fuel of the modes of nature, the fire of material existence is extinguished. Then one achieves the transcendental platform of direct relationship with the object of his meditation, the Supreme Lord.

parts.sanskrit:
यस्मिन् मनो लब्धपदं यदेतच्छनैःशनैर्मुञ्चति कर्मरेणून्।
सत्वेन वृद्धेन रजस्तमश्च विधूय निर्वाणमुपैत्यनिन्धनम्॥ ११/९/१२॥

“बाह्यं मनो विलीनं स्यान्मुक्तौ चिन्मात्रकं मनः।
तेनैवानुभवेत् सर्वं स्वात्माभिन्नेन मुक्तिगः॥”
इति मुक्तितत्त्वे॥ १२॥

units.sanskrit:
तदेवमात्मन्यवरुद्धचित्तो न वेद किञ्चिद् बहिरन्तरं वा।
यथेषुकारो नृपतिं व्रजन्तमिषौ गतात्मा न ददर्श पार्श्वे॥ ११/९/१३॥
units.english: Thus, when one’s consciousness is completely fixed on the Absolute Truth, the Lord, one no longer sees duality, or internal and external reality. The example is given of the arrow maker who was so absorbed in making a straight arrow that he did not even see or notice the king himself, who was passing right next to him.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

The example is given of the arrow maker who was so absorbed in making a straight arrow that he did not even see or notice the king himself, who was passing right next to him.

units.sanskrit:
एकचार्यनिकेतः स्यादप्रमत्तो गुहाशयः।
अलक्ष्यमाण आचारैर्मुनिरेकोऽल्पतोषणः॥ ११/९/१४॥
units.english: A saintly person should remain alone and constantly travel without any fixed residence. Being alert, he should remain secluded and should act in such a way that he is not recognized or noticed by others. Moving without companions, he should not speak more than required.

meta.english_verbatim: A saintly person should remain alone and constantly travel without any fixed residence. Being alert, he should remain secluded and should act in such a way that he is not recognized or noticed by others. Moving without companions, he should not speak more than required.

units.sanskrit:
गृहारम्भो हि दुःखाय विफलश्चाध्रुवात्मनः।
सर्पः परकृतं वेश्म प्रविश्य सुखमेधते॥ ११/९/१५॥
units.english: When a person living in a temporary material body tries to construct a happy home, the result is fruitless and miserable. The snake, however, enters a home that has been built by others and prospers happily.

meta.english_verbatim: When a person living in a temporary material body tries to construct a happy home, the result is fruitless and miserable. The snake, however, enters a home that has been built by others and prospers happily.

units.sanskrit:
एको नारायणो देवः पूर्वसृष्टं स्वमायया।
संहृत्य कालकलया कल्पान्त इदमीश्वरः॥ ११/९/१६॥
units.english: The Lord of the universe, Nārāyaṇa, is the worshipable God of all living beings. Without extraneous assistance, the Lord creates this universe by His own potency, and at the time of annihilation the Lord destroys the universe through His personal expansion of time and withdraws all of the cosmos, including all the conditioned living beings, within Himself. Thus, His unlimited Self is the shelter and reservoir of all potencies. The subtle pradhāna, the basis of all cosmic manifestation, is conserved within the Lord and is in this way not different from Him. In the aftermath of annihilation the Lord stands alone.

meta.english_verbatim: The Lord of the universe, Nārāyaṇa, is the worshipable God of all living entities. Without extraneous assistance, the Lord creates this universe by His own potency, and at the time of annihilation the Lord destroys the universe through His personal expansion of time and withdraws all of the cosmos, including all the conditioned living entities, within Himself. Thus, His unlimited Self is the shelter and reservoir of all potencies. The subtle pradhāna, the basis of all cosmic manifestation, is conserved within the Lord and is in this way not different from Him. In the aftermath of annihilation the Lord stands alone.

units.sanskrit:
एक एवाद्वितीयोऽभूदात्माधारोऽखिलाश्रयः।
कालेनात्मानुभावेन साम्यं नीतासु शक्तिषु॥ ११/९/१७॥
सत्वादिष्वादिपुरुषः प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः।
परावराणां परम आस्ते कैवल्यसाञ्ज्ञतः॥ ११/९/१८॥
units.english: When the Lord displays His own potency in the form of time and guides His material potencies, such as the mode of goodness, into a neutral condition of equilibrium, He remains as the supreme controller of that neutral state, called pradhāna, as well as of the living beings. He is also the supreme worshipable object for all beings, including liberated souls, gods and ordinary conditioned souls. The Lord is eternally free from any material designation, and He constitutes the totality of spiritual bliss, which one experiences by seeing the Lord’s spiritual form. The Lord thus exhibits the fullest meaning of the word “liberation.”

parts.sanskrit:
एक एवाद्वितीयोऽभूदात्माधारोऽखिलाश्रयः।
कालेनात्मानुभावेन साम्यं नीतासु शक्तिषु॥ ११/९/१७॥
सत्वादिष्वादिपुरुषः प्रधानपुरुषेश्वरः।
परावराणां परम आस्ते कैवल्यसाञ्ज्ञतः॥ ११/९/१८॥

“कालप्रकृतिजीवादौ लयेऽसत्यप्रवर्तनात्।
तन्निमित्तस्य कार्यस्य विष्णुरेक इतीर्यते।
स हि कालादिकं सर्वं वर्तयत्यमितद्युतिः॥”
इति तत्त्वलये।
“प्रकृतिश्च गुणाश्चैव शक्यत्वाच्छक्तयः स्मृताः।
विष्णोः स्वरूपभूता तु शकनाच्छक्तिरुच्यते॥”
इति शक्तिविवेके॥ १६-१८॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: When the Supreme Personality of Godhead displays His own potency in the form of time and guides His material potencies, such as the mode of goodness, into a neutral condition of equilibrium, He remains as the supreme controller of that neutral state, called pradhāna, as well as of the living entities. He is also the supreme worshipable object for all beings, including liberated souls, demigods and ordinary conditioned souls. The Lord is eternally free from any material designation, and He constitutes the totality of spiritual bliss, which one experiences by seeing the Lord’s spiritual form. The Lord thus exhibits the fullest meaning of the word “liberation.”

units.sanskrit:
केवलानुभवानन्दसन्दोहो निरुपाधिकः।
कालेनात्मानुभावेन स्वमायां त्रिगुणात्मिकाम्॥ ११/९/१९॥
units.english: O subduer of the enemies, at the time of creation the Lord expands His own transcendental potency in the form of time, and agitating His material energy, māyā, composed of the three modes of material nature, He creates the mahat-tattva.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: O subduer of the enemies, at the time of creation the Personality of Godhead expands His own transcendental potency in the form of time, and agitating His material energy, māyā, composed of the three modes of material nature, He creates the mahat-tattva.

units.sanskrit:
संक्षोभयन् सृजत्यादौ तया सूत्रमरिन्दम।
तामाहुस्त्रिगुणां व्यक्तिं सृजतीं विश्वतोमुखम्।
यस्मिन् प्रोतमिदं विश्वं येन संसरते पुमान्॥ ११/९/२०॥
units.english: According to great sages, that which is the basis of the three modes of material nature and which manifests the variegated universe is called the sūtra or mahat-tattva. Indeed, this universe is resting within that mahat-tattva, and due to its potency the living being undergoes material existence.

meta.english_verbatim: According to great sages, that which is the basis of the three modes of material nature and which manifests the variegated universe is called the sūtra or mahat-tattva. Indeed, this universe is resting within that mahat-tattva, and due to its potency the living entity undergoes material existence.

units.sanskrit:
यथोर्णनाभिर्हृदयदूर्णां सन्तत्य वक्त्रत:।
तया विहृत्य भूयस्तां ग्रसत्येवं महेश्वरः ॥ ११/९/२१॥
units.english: Just as from within himself the spider expands thread through his mouth, plays with it for some time and eventually swallows it, similarly, the Lord expands His personal potency from within Himself. Thus, the Lord displays the network of cosmic manifestation, utilizes it according to His purpose and eventually withdraws it completely within Himself.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Just as from within himself the spider expands thread through his mouth, plays with it for some time and eventually swallows it, similarly, the Supreme Personality of Godhead expands His personal potency from within Himself. Thus, the Lord displays the network of cosmic manifestation, utilizes it according to His purpose and eventually withdraws it completely within Himself.

units.sanskrit:
यत्रयत्र मनो देही धारयेत् सकलं धिया।
स्नेहाद् द्वेषाद् भयाद् वापि याति तत्तत्सरूपताम्॥ ११/९/२२॥
units.english: If out of love, hate or fear an embodied soul fixes his mind with intelligence and complete concentration upon a particular bodily form, he will certainly attain the form that he is meditating upon.

meta.english_verbatim: If out of love, hate or fear an embodied soul fixes his mind with intelligence and complete concentration upon a particular bodily form, he will certainly attain the form that he is meditating upon.

units.sanskrit:
कीटः पेशस्करं ध्यायन् कुड्यां तेन प्रवेशितः।
याति तत्समतां राजन् पूर्वरूपमसन्त्यजन्॥ ११/९/२३॥
units.english: O King, once a wasp forced a weaker insect to enter his hive and kept him trapped there. In great fear the weak insect constantly meditated upon his captor, and without giving up his body, he gradually achieved the same state of existence as the wasp. Thus one achieves a state of existence according to one’s constant concentration.

parts.sanskrit:
कीटः पेशस्करं ध्यायन् कुड्यां तेन प्रवेशितः।
याति तत्समतां राजन् पूर्वरूपमसन्त्यजन्॥ ११/९/२३॥

“भयादपि हरिं भक्त्या चिन्तयंस्तत्सरूपताम्।
पेशस्कारिवदायाति द्विषन् द्वेषसरूपताम्।
सुखरूपस्य हि द्वेषो दुःखरूप इतीर्यते।
तस्माद् दुःखं सदा याति द्वेषवान् पुरुषोत्तमे।
नृसिंहद्वेषतो दुःखं रक्षोरूपेण रावणः।
अगाच्च रामविद्वेषाच्छिशुपालस्तथैव च।
ततो भक्त्या परं यातो द्वेषरूपस्त्वधोगतिम्।
तस्मात् सर्वगुणोद्रेकिविद्वेषात् सर्वदोषवान्।
भवेदिति सरूपत्वं द्वेषादेः पुरुषस्य हि॥”
इति भागवततन्त्रे।
“तं यथायथोपासते तदेव भवति” “तं भूतिरिति देवा उपासाञ्चक्रिरे ते बभूवुस्तस्माद्धाप्येतर्हि सुप्तो भूर्भूरित्येव प्रश्वसित्यभूरित्यसुरास्ते ह पराबभूवुः” इत्यादि च।
“सत्यप्यत्यल्पविद्वेषे भोजनं दास्यतीति तु।
स्नेहबाहुल्यतः कीटः पेशस्कारिसमो भवेत्।
द्वेषे सर्वात्मना नष्टे स्नेहे चैव विवर्धति।
सरूपता तदैव स्यात् कीटस्यैवं हरेरपि।
अत्यल्पोऽपि हरेर्द्वेषः स्नेहस्यानुदयङ्करः।
सोऽयं विशेषो नान्यस्य फलदाता च केशवः।
नहि पेशस्कृतः किञ्चित् फलदातृत्वमिष्यते।
स्वातन्त्र्याद् विद्विषां चैव केशवो न सुखप्रदः॥”
इति स्वातन्त्र्यविवेके॥ २३॥

In great fear the weak insect constantly meditated upon his captor, and without giving up his body, he gradually achieved the same state of existence as the wasp. Thus one achieves a state of existence according to one’s constant concentration.

units.sanskrit:
एवं गुरुभ्य एतेभ्य एषा मे शिक्षिता मतिः।
स्वात्मोपशिक्षितां बुद्धिं शृणु मे वदतः प्रभो॥ ११/९/२४॥
units.english: O King, from all these teachers I have acquired great wisdom. Now please listen as I explain what I learned from my own body.

meta.english_verbatim: O King, from all these spiritual masters I have acquired great wisdom. Now please listen as I explain what I learned from my own body.

units.sanskrit:
देहो गुरुर्मम विरक्तिविवेकहेतुः
बिभ्रत् स्म सत्वनिधनं सततात्युदर्कम्।
तत्वान्यनेन विमृशामि यथा तथापि
पारक्यमित्यवसितो विचराम्यसङ्गः॥ ११/९/२५॥
units.english: The material body is also my teacher because it teaches me detachment. Being subject to creation and destruction, it always comes to a painful end. Thus, although using my body to acquire knowledge, I always remember that it will ultimately be consumed by others, and remaining detached, I move about this world.

parts.sanskrit:
देहो गुरुर्मम विरक्तिविवेकहेतुः
बिभ्रत् स्म सत्वनिधनं सततात्युदर्कम्।
तत्वान्यनेन विमृशामि यथा तथापि
पारक्यमित्यवसितो विचराम्यसङ्गः॥ ११/९/२५॥
सत्त्वनिधनः सत्त्वं निधीयतेऽस्मिन् परमेश्वर इति। सततमतिशयेनोच्चैरर्करूप सुखरूप इति सततात्युदर्को भगवान्॥२५॥

Thus, although using my body to acquire knowledge, I always remember that it will ultimately be consumed by others, and remaining detached, I move about this world.

units.sanskrit:
जायात्मजार्थपशुभृत्यगृहाप्तवर्गान्
पुष्णाति यः प्रियचिकार्षया वितन्वन्।
सोऽन्ते सुकृच्छ्रमवरुद्धमनाः स्वदेहं
सृष्ट्वा स्वबीजमिव सीदति वृक्षधर्मा॥ ११/९/२६॥
units.english: A man attached to the body accumulates money with great struggle to expand and protect the position of his wife, children, property, domestic animals, servants, homes, relatives, friends, and so on. He does all this for the gratification of his own body. As a tree before dying produces the seed of a future tree, the dying body manifests the seed of one’s next material body in the form of one’s accumulated karma. Thus assuring the continuation of material existence, the material body sinks down and dies.

parts.sanskrit:
जायात्मजार्थपशुभृत्यगृहाप्तवर्गान्
पुष्णाति यः प्रियचिकार्षया वितन्वन्।
सोऽन्ते सुकृच्छ्रमवरुद्धमनाः स्वदेहं
सृष्ट्वा स्वबीजमिव सीदति वृक्षधर्मा॥ ११/९/२६॥
बीजार्थमारोपणादिकं कुर्वन्निति॥ २६॥

units.sanskrit:
जिह्वैकतोऽमुमपकर्षति कर्हि तर्षा
शिश्नोऽन्यतस्त्वगुदरं श्रवणं कुतश्चित्।
घ्राणोऽन्यतश्चपलदृक् क्वच कर्मशक्तिः
बह्व्यः सपत्नय इव गेहपतिं लुनन्ति॥ ११/९/२७॥
units.english: A man who has many wives is constantly harassed by them. He is responsible for their maintenance, and thus all the ladies constantly pull him in different directions, each struggling for her self-interest. Similarly, the material senses harass the conditioned soul, pulling him in many different directions at once. On one side the tongue is pulling him to arrange tasty food; then thirst drags him to get a suitable drink. Simultaneously the sex organs clamor for satisfaction, and the sense of touch demands soft, sensuous objects. The belly harasses him until it is filled, the ears demand to hear pleasing sounds, the sense of smell hankers for pleasant aromas, and the fickle eyes clamor for pleasing sights. Thus the senses, organs and limbs, all desiring satisfaction, pull the living being in many directions.

units.sanskrit:
सृष्ट्वा पुराणि विविधान्यजयाऽऽत्मशक्त्या
वृक्षान् सरीसृपपशून् खगदंशमत्स्यान्।
तैस्तैरतृप्तहृदयः पुरुषं विधाय
ब्रह्मावबोधधिषणं मुदमाप देवः॥ ११/९/२८॥
units.english: The Lord, expanding His own potency, māyā-śakti, created innumerable species of life to house the conditioned souls. Yet by creating the forms of trees, reptiles, animals, birds, snakes and so on, the Lord was not satisfied within His heart. Then He created human life, which offers the conditioned soul sufficient intelligence to perceive the Absolute Truth, and became pleased.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, expanding His own potency, māyā-śakti, created innumerable species of life to house the conditioned souls. Yet by creating the forms of trees, reptiles, animals, birds, snakes and so on, the Lord was not satisfied within His heart. Then He created human life, which offers the conditioned soul sufficient intelligence to perceive the Absolute Truth, and became pleased.

units.sanskrit:
लब्ध्वा सुदुर्लभमिदं बहुसम्भवान्ते
मानुष्यमर्थदमनित्यमपीह धीरः।
तूर्णं यतेत न पतेदनुमृत्यु याव
निःश्रेयसाय विषयः खलु सर्वतः स्यात्॥ ११/९/२९॥
units.english: After many, many births and deaths one achieves the rare human form of life, which, although temporary, affords one the opportunity to attain the highest perfection. Thus a sober human being should quickly endeavor for the ultimate perfection of life as long as his body, which is always subject to death, has not fallen down and died. After all, sense enjoyment is available even in the most abominable species of life, whereas Kṛṣṇa consciousness is possible only for a human being.

meta.english_verbatim: After many, many births and deaths one achieves the rare human form of life, which, although temporary, affords one the opportunity to attain the highest perfection. Thus a sober human being should quickly endeavor for the ultimate perfection of life as long as his body, which is always subject to death, has not fallen down and died. After all, sense gratification is available even in the most abominable species of life, whereas Kṛṣṇa consciousness is possible only for a human being.

units.sanskrit:
एवं सञ्जातवैराग्यो विज्ञानालोक आत्मनि।
विचरामि महीमेतां मुक्तसङ्गोऽनहङ्कृतिः॥ ११/९/३०॥
units.english: Having learned from my teachers, I remain situated in realization of the Lord and, fully renounced and enlightened by realized spiritual knowledge, wander the earth without attachment or false ego.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Having learned from my spiritual masters, I remain situated in realization of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and, fully renounced and enlightened by realized spiritual knowledge, wander the earth without attachment or false ego.

units.sanskrit:
नह्येकस्माद् गुरोर्ज्ञानं सुस्थितं स्यात् सुपुष्कळम्।
ब्रह्मैतदद्वितीयं वै गीयते बहुधर्षिभिः॥ ११/९/३१॥
units.english: Although the Absolute Truth is one without a second, the sages have described Him in many different ways. Therefore one may not be able to acquire very firm or complete knowledge from one teacher.

parts.sanskrit:
नह्येकस्माद् गुरोर्ज्ञानं सुस्थितं स्यात् सुपुष्कळम्।
ब्रह्मैतदद्वितीयं वै गीयते बहुधर्षिभिः॥ ११/९/३१॥

“एकस्मात् तु गुरोर्ज्ञानं जायते नैव कस्यचित्।
एकस्मादेव जायेत योग्याद् ब्रह्मपदस्य तु।
स्वयं चोपदिशेज्ज्ञानं वैरिञ्चिपदयोगिनि।
अनुग्रहात् तेन चापि ज्ञानं दत्वा विमुक्तिदः।
ज्ञानं प्राप्य बहुभ्योऽपि नर्ते मुक्तिश्चतुर्मुखात्।
ज्ञानमप्राप्य तेषां तु ज्ञानदो विष्णुरेव हि॥”
इति गुरुविवेके॥ ३१॥

meta.english_verbatim: Although the Absolute Truth is one without a second, the sages have described Him in many different ways. Therefore one may not be able to acquire very firm or complete knowledge from one spiritual master.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
इत्युक्त्वा स यदुं विप्रस्तमामन्त्र्याङ्ग धीरधीः।
वन्दितोऽभ्यर्चितो राज्ञा ययौ प्रीतो यथागतम्॥ ११/९/३२॥
units.english: The Lord said: Having thus spoken to King Yadu, the wise brāhmaṇa accepted obeisances and worship from the King and felt pleased within himself. Then bidding farewell, he left exactly as he had come.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Having thus spoken to King Yadu, the wise brāhmaṇa accepted obeisances and worship from the King and felt pleased within himself. Then bidding farewell, he left exactly as he had come.

units.sanskrit:
अवधूतवचः श्रुत्वा सर्वेषां नः प्रपूर्वजः।
सर्वसङ्गविनिर्मुक्तः समचित्तो बभूव ह॥ ११/९/३३॥
units.english: O Uddhava, hearing the words of the avadhūta, the saintly King Yadu, who is the forefather of our own ancestors, became free from all material attachment, and thus his mind was evenly fixed on the spiritual platform.

meta.english_verbatim: O Uddhava, hearing the words of the avadhūta, the saintly King Yadu, who is the forefather of our own ancestors, became free from all material attachment, and thus his mind was evenly fixed on the spiritual platform.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
मयोदितेष्ववहितः स्वधर्मेषु मदाश्रयः।
वर्णाश्रमकुलाचारमकामात्मा समाचरेत्॥ ११/१०/१॥
units.english: The Lord said: Taking full shelter in Me, with the mind carefully fixed in the devotion of the Lord as spoken by Me, one should live without personal desire and practice the social and occupational system called varṇāśrama.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: Taking full shelter in Me, with the mind carefully fixed in the devotional service of the Lord as spoken by Me, one should live without personal desire and practice the social and occupational system called varṇāśrama.

units.sanskrit:
अन्वीक्षेत विशुद्धात्मा देहिनां विषयात्मनाम्।
गुणेषु तत्वज्ञानेन१ सर्वारम्भविपर्ययम्॥ ११/१०/२॥
units.english: A purified soul should see that because the conditioned souls who are dedicated to sense enjoyment have falsely accepted the objects of sense pleasure as truth, all of their endeavors are doomed to failure.

meta.english_verbatim: A purified soul should see that because the conditioned souls who are dedicated to sense gratification have falsely accepted the objects of sense pleasure as truth, all of their endeavors are doomed to failure.

units.sanskrit:
सुप्तस्य विषयालोको ध्यायतो वा मनोरथः।
नानात्मकत्वाद् विफलस्तथाऽभेदोऽन्यधीगुणैः॥ ११/१०/३॥
units.english: One who is sleeping may see many objects of sense enjoyment in a dream, but such pleasurable things are merely creations of the mind and are thus ultimately useless. Similarly, the living being who is asleep to his spiritual identity also sees many sense objects, but these innumerable objects of temporary gratification are creations of the Lord’s illusory potency and have no permanent existence. One who meditates upon them, impelled by the senses, uselessly engages his intelligence.

parts.sanskrit:
सुप्तस्य विषयालोको ध्यायतो वा मनोरथः।
नानात्मकत्वाद् विफलस्तथाऽभेदोऽन्यधीगुणैः॥ ११/१०/३॥

बुद्धिगुणैः कामक्रोधादिभिरभेदो विफलः।
“वस्तुस्थितेरन्यथात्वं नानात्वमिति कीर्तितम्।
ज्ञानस्यैव तु नानात्वान्न स्यात् कामाद्यहम्मतिः।
कामादिषु स्वधीस्थेषु केवलं जीवसंस्थितिः।
इति बुद्धिरभेदः स्यात् स न कार्यः कथञ्चन।
अदुष्टकामश्चिद्रूपो जीवाभिन्नः स्वरूपतः।
दुष्टकामो मनोधर्मस्तस्माद् ध्येयः सदैव सः॥”
इति विवेके॥ ३॥

meta.english_verbatim: One who is sleeping may see many objects of sense gratification in a dream, but such pleasurable things are merely creations of the mind and are thus ultimately useless. Similarly, the living entity who is asleep to his spiritual identity also sees many sense objects, but these innumerable objects of temporary gratification are creations of the Lord’s illusory potency and have no permanent existence. One who meditates upon them, impelled by the senses, uselessly engages his intelligence.

units.sanskrit:
निवृत्तं कर्म सेवेत प्रवृत्तं मत्परस्त्यजेत्।
जिज्ञासायां सम्प्रवृत्तो नाद्रियेत् कर्मचोदनाम्॥ ११/१०/४॥
units.english: One who has fixed Me within his mind as the goal of life should give up activities based on sense enjoyment and should instead execute work governed by the regulative principles for advancement. When, however, one is fully engaged in searching out the ultimate truth of the soul, one should not accept the scriptural injunctions governing actions aimed at results.

parts.sanskrit:
निवृत्तं कर्म सेवेत प्रवृत्तं मत्परस्त्यजेत्।
जिज्ञासायां सम्प्रवृत्तो नाद्रियेत् कर्मचोदनाम्॥ ११/१०/४॥

“निष्कामं ज्ञानपूर्वं तु निवृत्तमिह चोच्यते।
निवृत्तं सेवमानस्तु ब्रह्माभ्येति सनातनम्॥”
इति भारते॥ ४॥

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: One who has fixed Me within his mind as the goal of life should give up activities based on sense gratification and should instead execute work governed by the regulative principles for advancement. When, however, one is fully engaged in searching out the ultimate truth of the soul, one should not accept the scriptural injunctions governing fruitive activities.

units.sanskrit:
यमानभीक्ष्णं सेवेत नियमान् मत्परः क्वचित्।
मदभिज्ञं गुरुं शान्तमुपासीत मदात्मकम्॥ ११/१०/५॥
units.english: One who has accepted Me as the supreme goal of life should strictly observe the scriptural injunctions forbidding sinful activities and, as far as possible, should execute the injunctions prescribing minor regulative duties such as cleanliness. Ultimately, however, one should approach a bona fide teacher who is full in knowledge of Me as I am, who is peaceful, and who by spiritual elevation is not different from Me.

parts.sanskrit:
यमानभीक्ष्णं सेवेत नियमान् मत्परः क्वचित्।
मदभिज्ञं गुरुं शान्तमुपासीत मदात्मकम्॥ ११/१०/५॥
“मामेव नित्यं ध्यायेद् यो मदात्मा स प्रकीर्तितः” इति च॥ ५॥

meta.english_verbatim: One who has accepted Me as the supreme goal of life should strictly observe the scriptural injunctions forbidding sinful activities and, as far as possible, should execute the injunctions prescribing minor regulative duties such as cleanliness. Ultimately, however, one should approach a bona fide spiritual master who is full in knowledge of Me as I am, who is peaceful, and who by spiritual elevation is not different from Me.

units.sanskrit:
अमान्यमत्सरो दक्षो निगमे दृढसौहृदः।
असत्वरोऽर्थजिज्ञासुरनसूयुरमोघवाक्॥ ११/१०/६॥
units.english: The servant or disciple of the teacher should be free from false prestige, never considering himself to be the doer. He should be active and never lazy and should give up all sense of proprietorship over the objects of the senses, including his wife, children, home and society. He should be endowed with feelings of loving friendship toward the teacher and should never become deviated or bewildered. The servant or disciple should always desire advancement in spiritual understanding, should not envy anyone and should always avoid useless conversation.

meta.english_verbatim: The servant or disciple of the spiritual master should be free from false prestige, never considering himself to be the doer. He should be active and never lazy and should give up all sense of proprietorship over the objects of the senses, including his wife, children, home and society. He should be endowed with feelings of loving friendship toward the spiritual master and should never become deviated or bewildered. The servant or disciple should always desire advancement in spiritual understanding, should not envy anyone and should always avoid useless conversation.

units.sanskrit:
जायापत्यगृहक्षेत्रस्वजनद्रविणादिषु।
उदासीनः समं पश्येत् सर्वेष्वर्थमिवात्मनः॥ ११/१०/७॥
units.english: One should see one’s real self-interest in life in all circumstances and should therefore remain detached from wife, children, home, land, relatives, friends, wealth and so on.

meta.english_verbatim: One should see one’s real self-interest in life in all circumstances and should therefore remain detached from wife, children, home, land, relatives, friends, wealth and so on.

units.sanskrit:
विलक्षणः स्थूलसूक्ष्माद् देहादात्मेक्षिता स्वदृक्।
यथाग्निर्दारुणो दाह्याद् दाहकोऽन्यः प्रकाशकः॥ ११/१०/८
निरोधोत्पत्त्यणुबृहन्नानात्वं तत्कृतान् गुणान्।
अनुप्रविष्ट आधत्ते एवं देहगुणान् परः॥ ११/१०/९॥
units.english: Just as fire may appear differently as dormant, manifest, weak, brilliant and so on, according to the condition of the fuel, similarly, the spirit soul enters a material body and accepts particular bodily characteristics.

meta.english_verbatim: Just as fire may appear differently as dormant, manifest, weak, brilliant and so on, according to the condition of the fuel, similarly, the spirit soul enters a material body and accepts particular bodily characteristics.

units.sanskrit:
योऽसौ गुणैर्विरचितो देहोऽयं पुरुषस्य हि।
संसारस्तन्निबन्धोऽयं पुंसोऽविद्यास्थितात्मनः॥ ११/१०/१०॥
units.english: The subtle and gross material bodies are created by the material modes of nature, which expand from the potency of the Lord. Material existence occurs when the living being falsely accepts the qualities of the gross and subtle bodies as being his own factual nature. This illusory state, however, can be destroyed by real knowledge.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The subtle and gross material bodies are created by the material modes of nature, which expand from the potency of the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Material existence occurs when the living entity falsely accepts the qualities of the gross and subtle bodies as being his own factual nature. This illusory state, however, can be destroyed by real knowledge.

units.sanskrit:
तस्माज्जिज्ञासयाऽऽत्मानमात्मस्थं केवलं परम्।
सङ्गम्य निरसेदस्य वस्तुबुद्धिं यथाक्रमम्॥ ११/१०/११॥
units.english: Therefore, by the cultivation of knowledge one should approach the Lord situated within oneself. By understanding the Lord’s pure, transcendental existence, one should gradually give up the false vision of the material world as independent reality.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Therefore, by the cultivation of knowledge one should approach the Supreme Personality of Godhead situated within oneself. By understanding the Lord’s pure, transcendental existence, one should gradually give up the false vision of the material world as independent reality.

units.sanskrit:
आचार्योऽरणिराद्या स्यादन्तेवास्युत्तरारणिः।
तत्सन्धानं प्रवचनं विद्यावह्निः सुखावहः॥ ११/१०/१२॥
units.english: The teacher can be compared to the lower kindling stick, the disciple to the upper kindling stick, and the instruction given by the guru to the third stick placed in between. The transcendental knowledge communicated from guru to disciple is compared to the fire arising from the contact of these, which burns the darkness of ignorance to ashes, bringing great happiness both to guru and disciple.

meta.english_verbatim: The spiritual master can be compared to the lower kindling stick, the disciple to the upper kindling stick, and the instruction given by the guru to the third stick placed in between. The transcendental knowledge communicated from guru to disciple is compared to the fire arising from the contact of these, which burns the darkness of ignorance to ashes, bringing great happiness both to guru and disciple.

units.sanskrit:
वैशारदी साऽतिविशुद्धबुद्धिर्धुनोति मायां गुणसम्प्रसूतिम्।
गुणांश्च सन्दह्य यदात्म्यमेतत् स्वयं च शाम्यत्यसमिद् यथाग्निः॥ ११/१०/१३॥
units.english: By submissively hearing from an expert teacher, the expert disciple develops pure knowledge, which repels the onslaught of material illusion arising from the three modes of material nature. Finally this pure knowledge itself ceases, just as fire ceases when the stock of fuel has been consumed.

meta.english_verbatim: By submissively hearing from an expert spiritual master, the expert disciple develops pure knowledge, which repels the onslaught of material illusion arising from the three modes of material nature. Finally this pure knowledge itself ceases, just as fire ceases when the stock of fuel has been consumed.

units.sanskrit:
अथैषां कर्मकतॄणां भोक्तॄणां सुखदुःखयोः।
नानात्वमथ नित्यत्वं लोककालागमात्मनाम्॥ ११/१०/१४॥
मन्यसे सर्वभावानां संस्था ह्यौत्पत्तिका तथा।
तत्तदाकृतिभेदेन जायते भिद्यते च धीः॥ ११/१०/१५॥
एवमप्यत्र सर्वेषां देहिनां देहयोगतः।
कालावयवतः सन्ति भावा जन्मादयोऽसकृत्॥ ११/१०/१६॥
units.english: My dear Uddhava, I have thus explained to you perfect knowledge. There are philosophers, however, who challenge My conclusion. They state that the natural position of the living being is to engage in actions aimed at results, and they see him as the enjoyer of the happiness and unhappiness that accrue from his own work. According to this materialistic philosophy, the world, time, the revealed scriptures and the self are all variegated and eternal, existing as a perpetual flow of transformations. Knowledge, moreover, cannot be one or eternal, because it arises from the different and changing forms of objects; thus knowledge itself is always subject to change. Even if you accept such a philosophy, My dear Uddhava, there will still be perpetual birth, death, old age and disease, since all living beings must accept a material body subject to the influence of time.

parts.sanskrit:
अथैषां कर्मकतॄणां भोक्तॄणां सुखदुःखयोः।
नानात्वमथ नित्यत्वं लोककालागमात्मनाम्॥ ११/१०/१४॥
मन्यसे सर्वभावानां संस्था ह्यौत्पत्तिका तथा।
तत्तदाकृतिभेदेन जायते भिद्यते च धीः॥ ११/१०/१५॥
एवमप्यत्र सर्वेषां देहिनां देहयोगतः।
कालावयवतः सन्ति भावा जन्मादयोऽसकृत्॥ ११/१०/१६॥

“अदेहधर्मवान् विष्णुर्देहधर्मवदीर्यते।
जीवस्त्वदेहधर्माऽपि परतो देहधर्मवान्।
स्वयं त्वनभिमानः सन्नज्ञानामेव दर्शयेत्।
विष्णुर्जीवस्त्वभीमानी यावद् विष्णुपदं व्रजेत्॥”
इति विष्णुसंहितायाम्।
“अवस्त्वशक्तमुद्दिष्टं शक्तं वस्त्विह भण्यते।
तस्मादेकं परं ब्रह्म वस्तुशब्दोदितं सदा॥”
इति लक्षणे॥ ११॥
“पिशाचवत् स्थिता माया तूच्चते जीवगा सदा।
दह्यन्ते तद्गुणाः सर्वे सा च प्रातिस्विकी नरे॥”
इति वैभाव्ये।
“एतच्छब्देन दुःखादिरपरोक्षतयोच्यते।
क्वचिद् विश्वं क्वचिद् ब्रह्म क्वचिन्निन्द्यमुदीर्यते॥”
इति तन्त्रनिरुक्ते।
“बाह्यान्तःकरणाज्जन्यं ज्ञानं नश्यति मुक्तिगे।
स्वरूपज्ञानतो भोगान् मुक्तौ भुङ्क्ते यथेष्टतः॥”
इति मुक्तितत्त्वे॥ १३॥
“देहापेक्षमनित्यत्वं जीवानां जननं तथा।
स्वतस्त्वजाश्च नित्याश्च बहवः सुखरूपिणः।
उत्तमा जीवसङ्घास्तु नीचा वै नित्यदुःखिनः॥”
इति जीवतत्त्वे॥ १४-१५॥

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Uddhava, I have thus explained to you perfect knowledge. There are philosophers, however, who challenge My conclusion. They state that the natural position of the living entity is to engage in fruitive activities, and they see him as the enjoyer of the happiness and unhappiness that accrue from his own work. According to this materialistic philosophy, the world, time, the revealed scriptures and the self are all variegated and eternal, existing as a perpetual flow of transformations. Knowledge, moreover, cannot be one or eternal, because it arises from the different and changing forms of objects; thus knowledge itself is always subject to change. Even if you accept such a philosophy, My dear Uddhava, there will still be perpetual birth, death, old age and disease, since all living entities must accept a material body subject to the influence of time.

units.sanskrit:
तत्रापि कर्मणां कर्तुरस्वातन्त्र्यं च लक्ष्यते।
भोक्तुश्च सुखदुःखानां कोन्वर्थो विवशं भजेत्॥ ११/१०/१७॥
units.english: Although the performer of actions aimed at results desires perpetual happiness, it is clearly observed that materialistic workers are often unhappy and only occasionally satisfied, thus proving that they are not independent or in control of their destiny. When a person is always under the superior control of another, how can he expect any valuable results from his own actions aimed at results?

parts.sanskrit:
तत्रापि कर्मणां कर्तुरस्वातन्त्र्यं च लक्ष्यते।
भोक्तुश्च सुखदुःखानां कोन्वर्थो विवशं भजेत्॥ ११/१०/१७॥

“स्वाधिकानां वशत्वात् तु परमं सुखमेव तु।
तदन्येषां वशे यस्तु किं सुखं तस्य भण्यताम्।
स्वाधिकानां वशत्वं च तेषु भक्तिमतः सुखम्।
तदन्येषां तु दुःखाय तस्माद् भक्तोऽधिको भवेत्॥”
इति च॥ १७॥

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: Although the performer of fruitive activities desires perpetual happiness, it is clearly observed that materialistic workers are often unhappy and only occasionally satisfied, thus proving that they are not independent or in control of their destiny. When a person is always under the superior control of another, how can he expect any valuable results from his own fruitive actions?

units.sanskrit:
न देहिनां सुखं किञ्चिद् विद्यते विदुषामपि।
तथा च दुःखमूढानां तथाऽहङ्कारिणां परम्॥ ११/१०/१८॥
units.english: It is observed within the material world that sometimes even an intelligent person is not happy. Similarly, sometimes even a great fool is happy. The concept of becoming happy through expertly performing material activities is simply a useless exhibition of false egotism.

parts.sanskrit:
न देहिनां सुखं किञ्चिद् विद्यते विदुषामपि।
तथा च दुःखमूढानां तथाऽहङ्कारिणां परम्॥ ११/१०/१८॥

विदुषामपि देहमानिनां यदा न विद्यते सुखं तदा दुःखमूढानमहङ्कारिणां च किम्वित्यर्थः।
“पुनःशब्दे प्रस्तुतार्थे तथाशब्द उदीर्यते” इति शाब्दे॥ १८॥

meta.english_verbatim: It is observed within the material world that sometimes even an intelligent person is not happy. Similarly, sometimes even a great fool is happy. The concept of becoming happy through expertly performing material activities is simply a useless exhibition of false egotism.

units.sanskrit:
यदि प्राप्तिं विघातं च जानन्ति सुखदुःखयोः।
तेऽप्यद्धा न विदुर्योगं मृत्युर्न प्रभवेद् यथा॥ ११/१०/१९॥
units.english: Even if people know how to achieve happiness and avoid unhappiness, they still do not know the process by which death will not be able to exert its power over them.

parts.sanskrit:
यदि प्राप्तिं विघातं च जानन्ति सुखदुःखयोः।
तेऽप्यद्धा न विदुर्योगं मृत्युर्न प्रभवेद् यथा॥ ११/१०/१९॥
ये तु विद्वत्त्वेन प्रसिद्धाः प्राकृतानां तेऽप्यद्धा न विदुः, देहमानिनश्चेत्। दुःखमूढा अधीराः अहङ्कारिणो विशेषतोऽप्यविद्यमानगुणाभिमानिनः॥ १९॥

meta.english_verbatim: Even if people know how to achieve happiness and avoid unhappiness, they still do not know the process by which death will not be able to exert its power over them.

units.sanskrit:
कोन्वर्थः सुखयत्येनं कामो वा मृत्युमन्तिके।
आघातं नीयमानस्य वध्यस्येव पदेपदे॥ ११/१०/२०॥
units.english: Death is not at all pleasing, and since everyone is exactly like a condemned man being led to the place of execution, what possible happiness can people derive from material objects or the gratification they provide?

meta.english_verbatim: Death is not at all pleasing, and since everyone is exactly like a condemned man being led to the place of execution, what possible happiness can people derive from material objects or the gratification they provide?

units.sanskrit:
श्रुतं च दृष्टवन्नङ्क्ष्येत् स्पर्धासूयात्ययाप्ययैः।
बह्वन्तरायैर्विहतं कृषिवच्चापि निष्फलम्॥ ११/१०/२१॥
units.english: That material happiness of which we hear, such as promotion to heavenly planets for celestial enjoyment, is just like that material happiness we have already experienced. Both are polluted by jealousy, envy, decay and death. Therefore, just as an attempt to raise crops becomes fruitless if there are many problems like crop disease, insect plague or drought, similarly, the attempt to attain material happiness, either on earth or on the heavenly planets, is always fruitless because of innumerable obstacles.

meta.english_verbatim: That material happiness of which we hear, such as promotion to heavenly planets for celestial enjoyment, is just like that material happiness we have already experienced. Both are polluted by jealousy, envy, decay and death. Therefore, just as an attempt to raise crops becomes fruitless if there are many problems like crop disease, insect plague or drought, similarly, the attempt to attain material happiness, either on earth or on the heavenly planets, is always fruitless because of innumerable obstacles.

units.sanskrit:
अन्तरायैरविहतो यदि धर्मः स्वनुष्ठितः।
तेनापि निर्जितं स्थानं यथा गच्छति तच्छृणु॥ ११/१०/२२॥
units.english: If one performs Vedic sacrifices and fruitive rituals without any mistake or contamination, one will achieve a heavenly situation in the next life. But even this result, which is only achieved by perfect performance of fruitive rituals, will be vanquished by time. Now hear of this.

meta.english_verbatim: If one performs Vedic sacrifices and fruitive rituals without any mistake or contamination, one will achieve a heavenly situation in the next life. But even this result, which is only achieved by perfect performance of fruitive rituals, will be vanquished by time. Now hear of this.

units.sanskrit:
इष्ट्वैव देवता यज्ञैः स्वर्लोकं याति याज्ञिकः।
भुञ्जीत देववत् तत्र भोगान् दिव्यान् निजार्जितान्॥ ११/१०/२३॥
units.english: If on earth one performs sacrifices for the satisfaction of the gods, he goes to the heavenly planets, where, just like a god, he enjoys all of the heavenly pleasures he has earned by his performances.

meta.english_verbatim: If on earth one performs sacrifices for the satisfaction of the demigods, he goes to the heavenly planets, where, just like a demigod, he enjoys all of the heavenly pleasures he has earned by his performances.

units.sanskrit:
स्वपुण्योपचिते तत्र विमान उपगीयते।
गन्धर्वैर्विहरन् मध्ये देवीनां हृद्यवेषधृक्॥ ११/१०/२४॥
units.english: Having achieved the heavenly planets, the performer of ritualistic sacrifices travels in a glowing airplane, which he obtains as the result of his piety on earth. Being glorified by songs sung by the Gandharvas and dressed in wonderfully charming clothes, he enjoys life surrounded by heavenly goddesses.

meta.english_verbatim: Having achieved the heavenly planets, the performer of ritualistic sacrifices travels in a glowing airplane, which he obtains as the result of his piety on earth. Being glorified by songs sung by the Gandharvas and dressed in wonderfully charming clothes, he enjoys life surrounded by heavenly goddesses.

units.sanskrit:
स्त्रीभिः कामगयानेन किङ्किणीजालमालिना।
क्राडन् न वेदात्मपातं सुराक्राडेषु निर्वृतः॥ ११/१०/२५॥
units.english: Accompanied by heavenly women, the enjoyer of the fruits of sacrifice goes on pleasure rides in a wonderful airplane, which is decorated with circles of tinkling bells and which flies wherever he desires. Being relaxed, comfortable and happy in the heavenly pleasure gardens, he does not consider that he is exhausting the fruits of his piety and will soon fall down to the mortal world.

meta.english_verbatim: Accompanied by heavenly women, the enjoyer of the fruits of sacrifice goes on pleasure rides in a wonderful airplane, which is decorated with circles of tinkling bells and which flies wherever he desires. Being relaxed, comfortable and happy in the heavenly pleasure gardens, he does not consider that he is exhausting the fruits of his piety and will soon fall down to the mortal world.

units.sanskrit:
तावत् प्रमोदते स्वर्गे यावत् पुण्यं समाप्यते।
क्षीणपुण्यः पतत्यर्वागनिच्छन् कालचालितः॥ ११/१०/२६॥
units.english: Until his pious results are used up, the performer of sacrifice enjoys life in the heavenly planets. When the pious results are exhausted, however, he falls down from the pleasure gardens of heaven, being moved against his desire by the force of eternal time.

meta.english_verbatim: Until his pious results are used up, the performer of sacrifice enjoys life in the heavenly planets. When the pious results are exhausted, however, he falls down from the pleasure gardens of heaven, being moved against his desire by the force of eternal time.

units.sanskrit:
यद्यधर्मरतः सङ्गादसतामजितेन्द्रियः।
कामात्मा कृपणो लुब्धः स्त्रैणो भूतविहिंसकः॥ ११/१०/२७॥
पशूनविधिनाऽऽलभ्य प्रेतभूतगणान् यजन्।
नरकानवशो जन्तुर्गत्वा यात्युद्बणं तमः॥ ११/१०/२८॥
कर्माणि दुःखोदर्काणि कुर्वन् देहेन तैः पुनः।
देहमाभजते तत्र किं सुखं मर्त्यधर्मिणः॥ ११/१०/२९॥
units.english: If a human being is engaged in sinful, irreligious activities, either because of bad association or because of his failure to control his senses, then such a person will certainly develop a personality full of material desires. He thus becomes miserly toward others, greedy and always anxious to exploit the bodies of women. When the mind is so polluted one becomes violent and aggressive and without the authority of Vedic injunctions slaughters innocent animals for sense enjoyment. Worshiping ghosts and spirits, the bewildered person falls fully into the grip of unauthorized activities and thus goes to hell, where he receives a material body infected by the darkest modes of nature. In such a degraded body, he unfortunately continues to perform inauspicious activities that greatly increase his future unhappiness, and therefore he again accepts a similar material body. What possible happiness can there be for one who engages in activities inevitably terminating in death?

meta.english_verbatim: If a human being is engaged in sinful, irreligious activities, either because of bad association or because of his failure to control his senses, then such a person will certainly develop a personality full of material desires. In such a degraded body, he unfortunately continues to perform inauspicious activities that greatly increase his future unhappiness, and therefore he again accepts a similar material body. What possible happiness can there be for one who engages in activities inevitably terminating in death?

units.sanskrit:
लोकानां लोकपालानां मद्भयं कल्पजीविनाम्।
ब्रह्मणोपि भयं मत्तो द्विपरार्धपरायुषः॥ ११/१०/३०॥
units.english: In all the planetary systems, from the heavenly to the hellish, and for all of the great gods who live for one thousand yuga cycles, there is fear of Me in My form of time. Even Brahmā, who possesses the supreme life span of 311,040,000,000,000 years, is also afraid of Me.

meta.english_verbatim: In all the planetary systems, from the heavenly to the hellish, and for all of the great demigods who live for one thousand yuga cycles, there is fear of Me in My form of time. Even Brahmā, who possesses the supreme life span of 311,040,000,000,000 years, is also afraid of Me.

units.sanskrit:
गुणाः सृजन्ति कर्माणि कालो नु सृजते गुणान्।
जीवस्तु गुणसंयुक्तो भुङ्क्ते कर्मफलान्यसौ॥ ११/१०/३१॥
units.english: The material senses create material activities, either pious or sinful, and the modes of nature set the material senses into motion. The living being, being fully engaged by the material senses and modes of nature, experiences the various results of actions aimed at results.

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: The material senses create material activities, either pious or sinful, and the modes of nature set the material senses into motion. The living entity, being fully engaged by the material senses and modes of nature, experiences the various results of fruitive work.

units.sanskrit:
यावत् स्याद् गुणवैषम्यं तावन्नानात्वमात्मनः।
नानात्वमात्मनो यावत् पारतन्त्र्यं तदैव हि॥ ११/१०/३२॥
units.english: As long as the living being thinks that the modes of material nature have separate existences, he will be obliged to take birth in many different forms and will experience varieties of material existence. Therefore, the living being remains completely dependent on actions aimed at results under the modes of nature.

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: As long as the living entity thinks that the modes of material nature have separate existences, he will be obliged to take birth in many different forms and will experience varieties of material existence. Therefore, the living entity remains completely dependent on fruitive activities under the modes of nature.

units.sanskrit:
यावदस्यास्वतन्त्रत्वं तावदीश्वरतो भयम्।
य एतत् समुपासीरंस्ते मुह्यन्ति शुचार्पिताः॥ ११/१०/३३॥
units.english: The conditioned soul who remains dependent on actions aimed at results under the material modes of nature will continue to fear Me, the Lord, since I impose the results of one’s actions aimed at results. Those who accept the material concept of life, taking the variegatedness of the modes of nature to be factual, devote themselves to material enjoyment and are therefore always absorbed in lamentation and grief.

parts.sanskrit:
यावदस्यास्वतन्त्रत्वं तावदीश्वरतो भयम्।
य एतत् समुपासीरंस्ते मुह्यन्ति शुचार्पिताः॥ ११/१०/३३॥
‘यावत् स्याद् गुणवैषम्यम्’ इत्यादि य उपासीरंस्ते मुह्यन्ति। गुणसंयुक्तः कर्मफलानि भुङ्क्ते॥ ३१-३३॥

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord
fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: The conditioned soul who remains dependent on fruitive activities under the material modes of nature will continue to fear Me, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, since I impose the results of one’s fruitive activities. Those who accept the material concept of life, taking the variegatedness of the modes of nature to be factual, devote themselves to material enjoyment and are therefore always absorbed in lamentation and grief.

units.sanskrit:
काल आत्माऽऽगमो लोकः स्वभावो धर्म एव च।
इति मां बहुधा प्राहुर्गुणव्यतिकरेऽसति॥ ११/१०/३४॥
units.english: When there is agitation and interaction of the material modes of nature, the living beings then describe Me in various ways such as all-powerful time, the Self, Vedic knowledge, the universe, one’s own nature, religious ceremonies and so on.

parts.sanskrit:
काल आत्माऽऽगमो लोकः स्वभावो धर्म एव च।
इति मां बहुधा प्राहुर्गुणव्यतिकरेऽसति॥ ११/१०/३४॥

असति गुणव्यतिकरे कालादिनामानं मामेवाहुरिति स्वसिद्धान्तः।
“कालः सर्वगुणोद्रेकादाप्तत्वादात्मनामकः।
आगमोऽवगतेरस्य लोको ज्ञानस्वरूपतः।
स्ववशत्वात् स्वभावोऽयं धारणाद् धर्म इत्यपि।
उपासते सदा मुक्ताः
परानन्दैकभागिनः।
तदेतत् तत्त्वमज्ञात्वा प्राहुर्दुर्मतयः परे।
यावत् तु गुणवैषम्यं तावन्नानात्वमात्मनः।
भेदबुद्धिस्तु यावत् स्यात् तावदीश्वरतन्त्रता।
यावदीश्वरतन्त्रत्वं तावत् तस्माद् भयं भवेत्।
उपासते य एवं तु नित्यशोके पतन्ति ते।
महातमस्यनानन्दे तस्मान्नैवं विचिन्तयेत्।
तस्मान्नित्यं तु नानात्वं जीवानामीशतन्त्रता।
स्वाधिकानां वशत्वं च मुक्तावपि सदेष्यते।
एवं ज्ञात्वा विमुच्यन्ते परानन्दं व्रजन्ति च॥”
इति तन्त्रभागवते॥ ३४॥

meta.english_verbatim: When there is agitation and interaction of the material modes of nature, the living entities then describe Me in various ways such as all-powerful time, the Self, Vedic knowledge, the universe, one’s own nature, religious ceremonies and so on.

units.sanskrit:
उद्धव उवाच
गुणेषु वर्तमानोऽपि देहजेष्वनपावृतः।
गुणैर्न बध्यतेऽदेही बध्यते वा कथं विभो॥ ११/१०/३५॥
units.english: Uddhava said: O my Lord, a living being situated within the material body is surrounded by the modes of nature and the happiness and distress that are born of activities caused by these modes. How is it possible that he is not bound by this material encirclement? It may also be said that the living being is ultimately transcendental and has nothing to do with the material world. Then how is he ever bound by material nature?

parts.sanskrit:
उद्धव उवाच
गुणेषु वर्तमानोऽपि देहजेष्वनपावृतः।
गुणैर्न बध्यतेऽदेही बध्यते वा कथं विभो॥ ११/१०/३५॥
अदेही परमात्मा। बद्ध्यते चेत् कथं बद्ध्यते॥ ३५॥

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

How is it possible that he is not bound by this material encirclement? It may also be said that the living entity is ultimately transcendental and has nothing to do with the material world.
