units.sanskrit:
युक्तयः सन्ति सर्वत्र भाषन्ते ब्राह्मणा यथा।
मायां मदीयामुद्गृह्य वदतां किं नु दुर्घटम्॥ ११/२२/४॥
units.english: Lord Kṛṣṇa replied: Because all material elements are present everywhere, it is reasonable that different learned brāhmaṇas have analyzed them in different ways. All such philosophers spoke under the shelter of My mystic potency, and thus they could say anything without contradicting the truth.

meta.english_verbatim: Lord Kṛṣṇa replied: Because all material elements are present everywhere, it is reasonable that different learned brāhmaṇas have analyzed them in different ways. All such philosophers spoke under the shelter of My mystic potency, and thus they could say anything without contradicting the truth.

units.sanskrit:
नैतदेवं यथात्थ त्वं यदहं वच्मि तत् तथा।
एवं विवदतां हेतुः शक्तयो मे दुरत्ययाः॥ ११/२२/५॥
units.english: When philosophers argue, “I don’t choose to analyze this particular case in the same way that you have,” it is simply My own insurmountable energies that are motivating their analytic disagreements.

meta.english_verbatim: When philosophers argue, “I don’t choose to analyze this particular case in the same way that you have,” it is simply My own insurmountable energies that are motivating their analytic disagreements.

units.sanskrit:
यासां व्यतिकरादासीद् विकल्पो वदतां पदम्।
प्राप्ते शमदमे व्येति वादस्तमनुशाम्यति॥ ११/२२/६॥
units.english: By interaction of My energies different opinions arise. But for those who have fixed their intelligence on Me and controlled their senses, differences of perception disappear, and consequently the very cause for argument is removed.

parts.sanskrit:
यासां व्यतिकरादासीद् विकल्पो वदतां पदम्।
प्राप्ते शमदमे व्येति वादस्तमनुशाम्यति॥ ११/२२/६॥

मायां मदीयां मत्सामर्थ्यम्।
“विष्णोः सामर्थ्यमालम्ब्य तत्त्वसङ्ख्यां मुनीश्वराः।
चक्रुर्हि तदविज्ञाय विवदन्त्यल्पबुद्धयः।
तत्रापि कारणं विष्णोः शक्तिर्यस्या विकारतः।
अव्यक्तादेर्विकल्पोऽयं मनसः सम्प्रजायते।
विरुद्धकल्पनं तच्च वासुदेवैकनिष्ठया।
निरहङ्कारया नश्येद् विवादैकाश्रयं हि तत्॥”
इति तन्त्रभागवते।
यासां सकाशादव्यक्तादिव्यतिकराद् विकल्पो विरुद्धकल्पः। स हि विवादश्रयः। तत्त्वसङ्ख्या विवक्षाभेदेन बहुधा भवति॥ ४-६॥

meta.english_verbatim: By interaction of My energies different opinions arise. But for those who have fixed their intelligence on Me and controlled their senses, differences of perception disappear, and consequently the very cause for argument is removed.

units.sanskrit:
परस्परानुप्रवेशात् तत्वानां पुरुषर्षभ।
पौर्वापर्यप्रसंख्यानं यथा वक्तुर्विवक्षितम्॥ ११/२२/७॥
units.english: O best among men, because subtle and gross elements mutually enter into one another, philosophers may calculate the number of basic material elements in different ways, according to their personal desire.

meta.english_verbatim: O best among men, because subtle and gross elements mutually enter into one another, philosophers may calculate the number of basic material elements in different ways, according to their personal desire.

units.sanskrit:
एकस्मिन्नपि दृश्यन्ते प्रविष्टानीतराणि च।
पूर्वस्मिन् वाऽपरस्मिन् वा तत्वे तत्वानि सर्वशः॥ ११/२२/८॥
units.english: All subtle material elements are actually present within their gross effects; similarly, all gross elements are present within their subtle causes, since material creation takes place by progressive manifestation of elements from subtle to gross. Thus we can find all material elements within any single element.

meta.english_verbatim: All subtle material elements are actually present within their gross effects; similarly, all gross elements are present within their subtle causes, since material creation takes place by progressive manifestation of elements from subtle to gross. Thus we can find all material elements within any single element.

units.sanskrit:
पौर्वापर्यमतोऽमीषां प्रसङ्ख्यानमपीच्छताम्।
यथा विविक्तं यद् युक्तं गृह्णीमो युक्तिसम्भवात्॥ ११/२२/९॥
units.english: Therefore, no matter which of these thinkers is speaking, and regardless of whether in their calculations they include material elements within their previous subtle causes or else within their subsequent manifest products, I accept their conclusions as authoritative, because a logical explanation can always be given for each of the different theories.

meta.english_verbatim: Therefore, no matter which of these thinkers is speaking, and regardless of whether in their calculations they include material elements within their previous subtle causes or else within their subsequent manifest products, I accept their conclusions as authoritative, because a logical explanation can always be given for each of the different theories.

units.sanskrit:
अनाद्यविद्यायुक्तस्य पुरुषस्यात्मवेदनम्।
स्वतो न सम्भवेद् यस्मात् ततोऽन्यः पुरुषो भवेत्॥ ११/२२/१०॥
units.english: Because a person who has been covered by ignorance since time immemorial is not capable of effecting his own self-realization, there must be some other personality who is in factual knowledge of the Absolute Truth and can impart this knowledge to him.

parts.sanskrit:
अनाद्यविद्यायुक्तस्य पुरुषस्यात्मवेदनम्।
स्वतो न सम्भवेद् यस्मात् ततोऽन्यः पुरुषो भवेत्॥ ११/२२/१०॥
सर्वथा जीवादन्यः परमेश्वरोऽङ्गीकर्तव्यः। जीवस्य स्वत एव ज्ञानायोगात्॥ १०॥

meta.english_verbatim: Because a person who has been covered by ignorance since time immemorial is not capable of effecting his own self-realization, there must be some other personality who is in factual knowledge of the Absolute Truth and can impart this knowledge to him.

units.sanskrit:
पुरुषेश्वरयोरत्र न वैलक्षण्यमण्वपि।
तदन्यकल्पनाऽपार्था ज्ञानं च प्रकृतेर्गुणः॥ ११/२२/११॥
units.english: According to knowledge in the material mode of goodness, there is no qualitative difference between the living being and the supreme controller. The imagination of qualitative difference between them is useless speculation.

parts.sanskrit:
पुरुषेश्वरयोरत्र न वैलक्षण्यमण्वपि।
तदन्यकल्पनाऽपार्था ज्ञानं च प्रकृतेर्गुणः॥ ११/२२/११॥

स च पुरुषरूपेण तत्स्थितो ज्ञानमुत्पादयति। ईश्वररूपेण बहिःस्थितः फलं ददाति। नच तयोः स्वरूपयोः किञ्चिद् वैलक्षण्यम्। तयोश्चान्यत्वकल्पना तत्स्वरूपादपगमनप्रयोजनानर्थकारिणीत्यर्थः। ज्ञानस्वरूपस्य जीवस्य कथं ज्ञानोत्पादनमित्यतो वक्ति- ज्ञानं च प्रकृतेर्गुण इति॥ जन्यज्ञानं प्रकृतेर्गुणः।
“स्वरूपभूतं ज्ञानं
तु सदा जीवस्य विष्णुना।
नियतं प्राकृतं ज्ञानं भक्त्या तेनैव दीयते॥”
इति च॥ ११॥

meta.english_verbatim: According to knowledge in the material mode of goodness, there is no qualitative difference between the living entity and the supreme controller. The imagination of qualitative difference between them is useless speculation.

units.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसाम्ये तु प्रकृतेर्नात्मनो गुणाः।
सत्वं रजस्तम इति स्थित्युत्पत्त्यन्तहेतवः॥ ११/२२/१२॥
units.english: Nature exists originally as the equilibrium of the three material modes, which pertain only to nature, not to the transcendental spirit soul. These modes — goodness, passion and ignorance — are the effective causes of the creation, maintenance and destruction of this universe.

parts.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेर्गुणसाम्ये तु प्रकृतेर्नात्मनो गुणाः।
सत्वं रजस्तम इति स्थित्युत्पत्त्यन्तहेतवः॥ ११/२२/१२॥
जन्यज्ञानस्य प्राकृतत्वं साधयति- प्रकृतेर्गुणसाम्ये त्वित्यादिना॥ १२॥

meta.english_verbatim: Nature exists originally as the equilibrium of the three material modes, which pertain only to nature, not to the transcendental spirit soul. These modes — goodness, passion and ignorance — are the effective causes of the creation, maintenance and destruction of this universe.

units.sanskrit:
सत्वं ज्ञानं रजः कर्म तमोऽज्ञानमिहोच्यते।
गुणव्यतिकरः कालः स्वभावः सूत्रमेव च॥ ११/२२/१३॥
units.english: In this world the mode of goodness is recognized as knowledge, the mode of passion as actions aimed at results, and the mode of darkness as ignorance. Time is perceived as the agitated interaction of the material modes, and the totality of functional propensity is embodied by the primeval sūtra, or mahat-tattva.

parts.sanskrit:
सत्वं ज्ञानं रजः कर्म तमोऽज्ञानमिहोच्यते।
गुणव्यतिकरः कालः स्वभावः सूत्रमेव च॥ ११/२२/१३॥

“अन्तःस्थः पुरुषो नाम ज्ञानदः सर्वदेहिनाम्।
बहिःस्थ ईश्वरो नाम ज्ञानादिफलदो हरिः॥”
इति मात्स्ये।
“पुरुषाख्यो हृद्गतस्तु विष्णुर्जीवविबोधकः।
फलदात्रा तु बाह्येन य ईशेन भिदां वदेत्।
तथैवान्यस्वरूपेषु विष्णोर्यो भेददर्शकः।
ये च जीवेश्वराभेदं पश्यन्तोऽनर्थभागिनः॥”
इति ब्राह्मे।
कालो भगवान्॥ १३॥

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: In this world the mode of goodness is recognized as knowledge, the mode of passion as fruitive work, and the mode of darkness as ignorance. Time is perceived as the agitated interaction of the material modes, and the totality of functional propensity is embodied by the primeval sūtra, or mahat-tattva.

units.sanskrit:
पुरुषः प्रकृतिर्व्यक्तमहङ्कारो नभोऽनिलः।
ज्योतिरापः क्षितिरिति तत्वान्युक्तानि मे नव॥ ११/२२/१४॥
units.english: I have described the nine basic elements as the enjoying soul, nature, nature’s primeval manifestation of the mahat-tattva, false ego, ether, air, fire, water and earth.

meta.english_verbatim: I have described the nine basic elements as the enjoying soul, nature, nature’s primeval manifestation of the mahat-tattva, false ego, ether, air, fire, water and earth.

units.sanskrit:
श्रोत्रं त्वग् दर्शनं घ्राणो जिह्वेति ज्ञानशक्तयः।
वाक्पाण्युपस्थपाय्वङ्घ्रि कर्माण्यङ्गोभयं मनः॥ ११/२२/१५॥
units.english: Hearing, touch, sight, smell and taste are the five knowledge-acquiring senses, My dear Uddhava, and speech, the hands, the genitals, the anus and the legs constitute the five working senses. The mind belongs to both these categories.

meta.english_verbatim: Hearing, touch, sight, smell and taste are the five knowledge-acquiring senses, My dear Uddhava, and speech, the hands, the genitals, the anus and the legs constitute the five working senses. The mind belongs to both these categories.

units.sanskrit:
शब्दः स्पर्शो रसो गन्धो रूपं चेत्यर्थजातयः।
गत्युक्त्युत्सर्गशिल्पानि कर्मायतनसिद्धयः॥ ११/२२/१६॥
units.english: Sound, touch, taste, smell and form are the objects of the knowledge-acquiring senses, and movement, speech, excretion and manufacture are functions of the working senses.

meta.english_verbatim: Sound, touch, taste, smell and form are the objects of the knowledge-acquiring senses, and movement, speech, excretion and manufacture are functions of the working senses.

units.sanskrit:
सर्गादौ प्रकृतिर्ह्यस्य कार्यकारणरूपिणी।
सत्वादिभिर्गुणैर्धत्ते पुरुषोऽव्यक्तमीक्षते॥ ११/२२/१७॥
units.english: In the beginning of creation nature assumes, by the modes of goodness, passion and ignorance, its form as the embodiment of all subtle causes and gross manifestations within the universe. The Lord does not enter the interaction of material manifestation but merely glances upon nature.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: In the beginning of creation nature assumes, by the modes of goodness, passion and ignorance, its form as the embodiment of all subtle causes and gross manifestations within the universe. The Supreme Personality of Godhead does not enter the interaction of material manifestation but merely glances upon nature.

units.sanskrit:
व्यक्तादयो विकुर्वाणा धातवो पुरुषेक्षया।
लब्धवीर्याः सृजन्त्यण्डं संहताः प्रकृतेर्बलात्॥ ११/२२/१८॥
units.english: As the material elements, headed by the mahat-tattva, are transformed, they receive their specific potencies from the glance of the Supreme Lord, and being amalgamated by the power of nature, they create the universal egg.

parts.sanskrit:
व्यक्तादयो विकुर्वाणा धातवो पुरुषेक्षया।
लब्धवीर्याः सृजन्त्यण्डं संहताः प्रकृतेर्बलात्॥ ११/२२/१८॥

‘नवैकादश पञ्च त्रीन्’ इत्युक्तानि- पुरुषः प्रकृतिरित्यादीनि॥
उत्सर्गस्य द्विविधत्वात् पञ्चकद्वयम्॥
त्रीनिति त्रिगुणानिति वक्तुं गुणप्रवृत्तिमाह- सर्गादावित्यादिना॥
कार्यकारणभावादन्योन्यानुप्रवेशो युक्त इति वक्तुं सृष्ट्युक्तिः।
“सृज्यस्रष्टृस्वरूपत्वादन्योन्यानुप्रवेशिनः।
तिष्ठन्ति तात्विका देवा विशेषप्राप्तिकारणात्॥”
इति नैसर्गे॥
अन्वेकमप्येष्वित्युक्तत्वात् पुरुषो हिरण्यगर्भः।
“यदा पुरुषशब्देन विरिञ्चस्यैव वाच्यता।
परस्य पृथगुक्त्यैव व्यक्तस्तत्र तु शङ्करः।
तदाऽहङ्कारशब्देन स्कन्दस्यैव वचो भवेत्॥”
इति विवेके॥ १४-१८॥

meta.english_verbatim: As the material elements, headed by the mahat-tattva, are transformed, they receive their specific potencies from the glance of the Supreme Lord, and being amalgamated by the power of nature, they create the universal egg.

units.sanskrit:
सप्तैव धातव इति यत्रार्थाः पञ्च खादयः।
ज्ञानमात्मोभयाधारस्ततो देहेन्द्रियासवः॥ ११/२२/१९॥
units.english: According to some philosophers there are seven elements, namely earth, water, fire, air and ether, along with the conscious spirit soul and the Supreme Soul, who is the basis of both the material elements and the ordinary spirit soul. According to this theory, the body, senses, life air and all material phenomena are produced from these seven elements.

parts.sanskrit:
सप्तैव धातव इति यत्रार्थाः पञ्च खादयः।
ज्ञानमात्मोभयाधारस्ततो देहेन्द्रियासवः॥ ११/२२/१९॥

सत्वादीन् गत्यादींश्च विना परमात्मना सह षड्विंशतिः। महदहङ्कारौ ब्रह्मरुद्रावङ्गीकृत्य स्कन्दं विना परमात्मना सह पञ्चविंशतिः।
“विषयेन्द्रियप्रकृतिदेवताः परमात्मना।
पञ्चविंशतितत्त्वानि सङ्ख्यातानि विदो विदुः॥”
इति च।
“ज्ञानशब्दोदितो ब्रह्मा तदाधारो हरिः स्मृतः” इति च।
ततो ज्ञानं विना परमात्मानमङ्गीकृत्यैव देहेन्द्रियाण्यसुश्च नव तत्त्वानि।
“सर्वदेहाभिमानी तु देहिनां तु दिवाकरः।
इन्द्रियात्मेन्द्र एवैकः प्राणो नाम प्रजापतिः॥”
इति च॥ १९॥

meta.english_verbatim: According to some philosophers there are seven elements, namely earth, water, fire, air and ether, along with the conscious spirit soul and the Supreme Soul, who is the basis of both the material elements and the ordinary spirit soul. According to this theory, the body, senses, life air and all material phenomena are produced from these seven elements.

units.sanskrit:
षडित्यत्रापि भूतानि पञ्च षष्ठः परः पुमान्।
तैर्युक्त आत्मसम्भूतैः सृष्ट्वेदं समुपाविशत्॥ ११/२२/२०॥
units.english: Other philosophers state that there are six elements — the five physical elements (earth, water, fire, air and ether) and the sixth element, the Lord. That Supreme Lord, endowed with the elements that He has brought forth from Himself, creates this universe and then personally enters within it.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: Other philosophers state that there are six elements — the five physical elements (earth, water, fire, air and ether) and the sixth element, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That Supreme Lord, endowed with the elements that He has brought forth from Himself, creates this universe and then personally enters within it.

units.sanskrit:
चत्वार्येवेति तत्रापि तेज आपोऽन्नमात्मनः।
जातानि तैरिदं जातं जन्मावयविनः खलु॥ ११/२२/२१॥
units.english: Some philosophers propose the existence of four basic elements, of which three — fire, water and earth — emanate from the fourth, the Self. Once existing, these elements produce the cosmic manifestation, in which all material creation takes place.

parts.sanskrit:
चत्वार्येवेति तत्रापि तेज आपोऽन्नमात्मनः।
जातानि तैरिदं जातं जन्मावयविनः खलु॥ ११/२२/२१॥
अवयविनो जन्म तैः खलु॥ २१॥

meta.english_verbatim: Some philosophers propose the existence of four basic elements, of which three — fire, water and earth — emanate from the fourth, the Self. Once existing, these elements produce the cosmic manifestation, in which all material creation takes place.

units.sanskrit:
सङ्ख्याने सप्तदशके भूतमात्रेन्द्रियाणि च।
पञ्चपञ्चैकमनसा आत्मा सप्तदशः स्मृतः॥ ११/२२/२२॥
units.english: Some calculate the existence of seventeen basic elements, namely the five gross elements, the five objects of perception, the five sensory organs, the mind, and the soul as the seventeenth element.

parts.sanskrit:
सङ्ख्याने सप्तदशके भूतमात्रेन्द्रियाणि च।
पञ्चपञ्चैकमनसा आत्मा सप्तदशः स्मृतः॥ ११/२२/२२॥

“भूतानि मात्राश्च परस्तत्त्वैकादशकं स्मृतम्” इति च।
भूतमात्रेत्यारभ्यात् तत्सिद्धेरेकादशानां पृथगनुक्तिः॥ २२॥

meta.english_verbatim: Some calculate the existence of seventeen basic elements, namely the five gross elements, the five objects of perception, the five sensory organs, the mind, and the soul as the seventeenth element.

units.sanskrit:
तद्वत् षोडशसङ्ख्यानि आत्मना मन उच्यते।
भूतेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चैव मन आत्मा त्रयोदश॥ ११/२२/२३॥
units.english: According to the calculation of sixteen elements, the only difference from the previous theory is that the soul is identified with the mind. If we think in terms of five physical elements, five senses, the mind, the individual soul and the Supreme Lord, there are thirteen elements.

parts.sanskrit:
तद्वत् षोडशसङ्ख्यानि आत्मना मन उच्यते।
भूतेन्द्रियाणि पञ्चैव मन आत्मा त्रयोदश॥ ११/२२/२३॥

आत्मना सहैव मन उच्यते।
“आत्मनः सन्निधिस्थत्वान्मनसस्तु तदुक्तितः।
उक्तो भवेत् परात्माऽपि तत्त्वषोडशकं यदा॥”
इति च।
आत्मशब्देन ब्रह्मा परमात्मा चोभावुच्येते।
“भूतेन्द्रियाणि च मनो ब्रह्मा विष्णुस्तथैव च।
एवं त्रयोदशैवाहुस्तत्त्वानि मुनयो वराः॥”
इति च।
“आत्मेति परमात्मा च विरिञ्चश्चापि कथ्यते।
वायुर्मनश्च देहश्च स्वयमित्यपि कुत्रचित्॥”
इति प्रत्यये॥ २३॥

meta.english_verbatim: According to the calculation of sixteen elements, the only difference from the previous theory is that the soul is identified with the mind. If we think in terms of five physical elements, five senses, the mind, the individual soul and the Supreme Lord, there are thirteen elements.

units.sanskrit:
इति नानाप्रसङ्ख्यानं तत्वानामृषिभिः कृतम्।
सर्वं न्याय्यं युक्तिमत्त्वाद् विदुषां किमशोभनम्॥ ११/२२/२४॥
units.english: Thus great philosophers have analyzed the material elements in many different ways. All of their proposals are reasonable, since they are all presented with ample logic. Indeed, such philosophical brilliance is expected of the truly learned.

meta.english_verbatim: Thus great philosophers have analyzed the material elements in many different ways. All of their proposals are reasonable, since they are all presented with ample logic. Indeed, such philosophical brilliance is expected of the truly learned.

units.sanskrit:
उद्धव उवाच
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चोभौ यद्यप्यात्मविलक्षणौ।
अन्योन्यापाश्रयात् कृष्ण दृश्यते न भिदा तयोः॥ ११/२२/२५॥
units.english: Uddhava inquired: Although nature and the living being are constitutionally distinct, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, there appears to be no difference between them, because they are found residing within one another. Thus the soul appears to be within nature and nature within the soul.

parts.sanskrit:
उद्धव उवाच
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चोभौ यद्यप्यात्मविलक्षणौ।
अन्योन्यापाश्रयात् कृष्ण दृश्यते न भिदा तयोः॥ ११/२२/२५॥
यद्यपि परमात्मा प्रकृतिश्च विलक्षणौ तथाऽपि तयोर्वैलक्षण्यं न लक्ष्यते। “अन्तरं च भिदा चेति वैलक्षण्यं प्रकीर्तितम्” इति च। तद्वैलक्षण्यं कुतो न दृश्यत इति प्रश्नाभिप्रायः॥ २५॥

meta.english_verbatim: Śrī Uddhava inquired: Although nature and the living entity are constitutionally distinct, O Lord Kṛṣṇa, there appears to be no difference between them, because they are found residing within one another. Thus the soul appears to be within nature and nature within the soul.

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

units.sanskrit:
त्वत्तो ज्ञानं हि जीवानां प्रमोषस्तनुशक्तितः।
त्वमेव ह्यात्ममायाया गतिं वेत्थ नचापरः॥ ११/२२/२७॥
units.english: From You alone the knowledge of the living beings arises, and by Your potency that knowledge is stolen away. Indeed, no one but Yourself can understand the real nature of Your illusory potency.

parts.sanskrit:
त्वत्तो ज्ञानं हि जीवानां प्रमोषस्तनुशक्तितः।
त्वमेव ह्यात्ममायाया गतिं वेत्थ नचापरः॥ ११/२२/२७॥

“आधारः प्रकृतेर्विष्णुर्नाधारस्तु हरेः क्वचित्।
तथाऽप्यव्यक्तगो यद्वद् दृश्यते मन्दचेतसाम्॥”
इति पाद्मे॥ २७॥

meta.english_verbatim: From You alone the knowledge of the living beings arises, and by Your potency that knowledge is stolen away. Indeed, no one but Yourself can understand the real nature of Your illusory potency.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चेति विकल्पः पुरुषर्षभ।
एष वैकारिकः सर्गो गुणव्यतिकरात्मकः॥ ११/२२/२८॥
units.english: The Lord said: O best among men, material nature and its enjoyer are clearly distinct. This manifest creation undergoes constant transformation, being founded upon the agitation of the modes of nature.

parts.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चेति विकल्पः पुरुषर्षभ।
एष वैकारिकः सर्गो गुणव्यतिकरात्मकः॥ ११/२२/२८॥

प्रकृतिः पुरुषश्चेत्येव अन्योन्यविलक्षणावेव। एषः विकल्पः। वैलक्षण्यादर्शनं विरुद्धकल्पनमेव। यस्माद् गुणव्यतिकरात्मकः सर्गो विकारनिमित्तः। स च गुणव्यतिकरस्त्रिविधः सत्त्वरजस्तमसामेकैकप्राधान्येन। तत्र तमःप्रधानानामेव विरुद्धकल्पनं तस्मात् तम एवात्र कारणमित्यर्थः॥ २८॥

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: O best among men, material nature and its enjoyer are clearly distinct. This manifest creation undergoes constant transformation, being founded upon the agitation of the modes of nature.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

units.sanskrit:
ममाङ्ग माया गुणमय्यनेकधा विकल्पबुद्धिं च गुणैर्विधत्ते।
वैकारिकस्त्रिविधोऽध्यात्ममेकमथाधिदैवमधिभूतमन्यत्॥ ११/२२/२९॥
units.english: My dear Uddhava, My material energy, comprising three modes and acting through them, manifests the varieties of creation along with varieties of consciousness for perceiving them. The manifest result of material transformation is understood in three aspects: adhyātmic, adhidaivic and adhibhautic.

parts.sanskrit:
ममाङ्ग माया गुणमय्यनेकधा विकल्पबुद्धिं च गुणैर्विधत्ते।
वैकारिकस्त्रिविधोऽध्यात्ममेकमथाधिदैवमधिभूतमन्यत्॥ ११/२२/२९॥

तत्रापि प्रकृतिरेव कारणमीश्वरेच्छा च। विकाराज्जातत्वाद् वैकारिक इत्युच्यत अहङ्कारस्त्रिविधोऽपि।
“वैकारिको महांश्चैव तथाऽहङ्कार एव च।
तथैव सात्त्विकश्चांशो वैकारिक इति त्रिधा॥”
इति शब्दनिर्णये॥ २९॥

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Uddhava, My material energy, comprising three modes and acting through them, manifests the varieties of creation along with varieties of consciousness for perceiving them. The manifest result of material transformation is understood in three aspects: adhyātmic, adhidaivic and adhibhautic.

units.sanskrit:
दृग् रूपमर्कश्च परत्र रन्धेर परस्परं सिध्यति न स्वतोऽसौ।
आत्मा यदेषामुपराम आद्यः स्वयाऽनुभूत्याऽखिलसिद्ध्यसिद्धिः ॥ ११/२२/३०॥
units.english: Sight, visible form and the reflected image of the sun within the aperture of the eye all work together to reveal one another. But the original sun standing in the sky is self-manifested. Similarly, the Supreme Soul, the original cause of all entities, who is thus separate from all of them, acts by the illumination of His own transcendental experience as the ultimate source of manifestation of all mutually manifesting objects.

parts.sanskrit:
दृग् रूपमर्कश्च परत्र रन्धेर परस्परं सिध्यति न स्वतोऽसौ।
आत्मा यदेषामुपराम आद्यः स्वयाऽनुभूत्याऽखिलसिद्ध्यसिद्धिः ॥ ११/२२/३०॥

अध्यात्ममिन्द्रियाणि। तैरेव विपरीतं ज्ञानं जायते।
“अहङ्कारे विद्यमाने भ्रमो भवति नान्यदा।
सम्यग् ज्ञानं हरेः शक्त्या तन्मुक्तस्य विशेषतः।
देवतानुग्रहो नित्यो मुक्तस्यापि ह्यपेक्ष्यते।
नित्यं तत्प्रतिबिम्बत्वाज्जीवानामेव कृत्स्नशः।
बाह्यज्ञानं च मुक्तस्य न जडाहङ्कृतेः क्वचित्।
किन्तु स्वरूपशक्त्यैव देवेभ्यश्चाभिजायते॥”
इति ब्रह्मतर्के।
“पश्यन्नपि जगत् सर्वं चिद्बलेनैव पश्यति।
कुतो मुक्तस्य तु जडं चिद्रूपस्य
व्यपेक्ष्यते
॥”
इति च।
एषामुपरमे मुक्तौ। चक्षुरिति पुनर्वचनमवधारणार्थम्॥ ३०॥

meta.english_verbatim: Sight, visible form and the reflected image of the sun within the aperture of the eye all work together to reveal one another. But the original sun standing in the sky is self-manifested. Similarly, the Supreme Soul, the original cause of all entities, who is thus separate from all of them, acts by the illumination of His own transcendental experience as the ultimate source of manifestation of all mutually manifesting objects.

units.sanskrit: एवं त्वगादि श्रवणादि चक्षुर्जिह्वादिना सादि च चित्तयुक्तम्॥ ११/२२/३१॥
units.english: Similarly, the sense organs, namely the skin, ears, eyes, tongue and nose — as well as the functions of the subtle body, namely conditioned consciousness, mind, intelligence and false ego — can all be analyzed in terms of the threefold distinction of sense, object of perception and presiding deity.

meta.english_verbatim: Similarly, the sense organs, namely the skin, ears, eyes, tongue and nose — as well as the functions of the subtle body, namely conditioned consciousness, mind, intelligence and false ego — can all be analyzed in terms of the threefold distinction of sense, object of perception and presiding deity.

units.sanskrit:
योऽसौ गुणक्षोभकृतो विकारः प्रधानमूलो जगतः प्रसूतिः।
अहं त्रिवृन्मोहविकल्पहेतुर्वैकारिकस्तामस ऐन्दियश्च॥ ११/२२/३२॥
units.english: When the three modes of nature are agitated, the resultant transformation appears as the element false ego in three phases — goodness, passion and ignorance. Generated from the mahat-tattva, which is itself produced from the unmanifest pradhāna, this false ego becomes the cause of all material illusion and duality.

parts.sanskrit:
योऽसौ गुणक्षोभकृतो विकारः प्रधानमूलो जगतः प्रसूतिः।
अहं त्रिवृन्मोहविकल्पहेतुर्वैकारिकस्तामस ऐन्दियश्च॥ ११/२२/३२॥
योऽसौ भ्रमहेतुर्विकारः स गुणक्षोभकृतः। आत्मा तु परिज्ञानस्वरूपो न गुणक्षोभकृतः॥ ३२॥

meta.english_verbatim: When the three modes of nature are agitated, the resultant transformation appears as the element false ego in three phases — goodness, passion and ignorance. Generated from the mahat-tattva, which is itself produced from the unmanifest pradhāna, this false ego becomes the cause of all material illusion and duality.

units.sanskrit:
आत्मा परिज्ञानमयो विवादो ह्यस्तीति नास्तीति भिदाऽर्थनिष्ठः।
व्यर्थोऽपि नैवोपरमेत पुंसां मत्तः परावृत्तधियां स्वलोकात्॥ ११/२२/३३॥
units.english: The speculative argument of philosophers — “This world is real,” “No, it is not real” — is based upon incomplete knowledge of the Supreme Soul and is simply aimed at understanding material dualities. Although such argument is useless, persons who have turned their attention away from Me, their own true Self, are unable to give it up.

parts.sanskrit:
आत्मा परिज्ञानमयो विवादो ह्यस्तीति नास्तीति भिदाऽर्थनिष्ठः।
व्यर्थोऽपि नैवोपरमेत पुंसां मत्तः परावृत्तधियां स्वलोकात्॥ ११/२२/३३॥

भिदा विपर्ययेण विद्यमानं नास्ति अविद्यमानमस्तीति विवादः।
“असदस्ति च सन्नास्तीत्येवं भेदाद् विवादनम्।
सदैव हरिपादाब्जविमुखानां प्रवर्तते॥”
इति च॥ ३३॥

meta.english_verbatim: The speculative argument of philosophers — “This world is real,” “No, it is not real” — is based upon incomplete knowledge of the Supreme Soul and is simply aimed at understanding material dualities. Although such argument is useless, persons who have turned their attention away from Me, their own true Self, are unable to give it up.

units.sanskrit:
उध्दव उवाच
त्वत्तः परावृत्तधियः स्वकृतैः कर्मभिः प्रभो।
उच्चावचान् यथा देहान् गृह्णन्ति विसृजन्ति च॥ ११/२२/३४॥
units.english: Uddhava said: O supreme master, the intelligence of those dedicated to actions aimed at results is certainly deviated from You. Please explain to me how such persons accept superior and inferior bodies by their materialistic activities and then give up such bodies. O Govinda, this topic is very difficult for foolish persons to understand. Being cheated by illusion in this world, they generally do not become aware of these facts.

meta.english_verbatim: Śrī Uddhava said: O supreme master, the intelligence of those dedicated to fruitive activities is certainly deviated from You. Please explain to me how such persons accept superior and inferior bodies by their materialistic activities and then give up such bodies. O Govinda, this topic is very difficult for foolish persons to understand. Being cheated by illusion in this world, they generally do not become aware of these facts.

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed
fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

units.sanskrit:
तन्ममाख्याहि गोविन्द दुर्विभाव्यमनात्मभिः।
न ह्येतत् प्रायशो लोके विद्वांसोऽञ्चन्ति वञ्चिताः॥ ११/२२/३५॥
श्रीभगवानुवाच
मनः कर्ममयं नॄणामिन्द्रियैः पञ्चभिर्युतम्।
लोकाल्लोकं प्रयात्यन्यमात्मा तदनुवर्तते॥ ११/२२/३६॥
units.english: Lord Kṛṣṇa said: The material mind of men is shaped by the reactions of actions aimed at results. Along with the five senses, it travels from one material body to another. The spirit soul, although different from this mind, follows it.

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: Lord Kṛṣṇa said: The material mind of men is shaped by the reactions of fruitive work. Along with the five senses, it travels from one material body to another. The spirit soul, although different from this mind, follows it.

units.sanskrit:
ध्यायन्मनो हि विषयान् दृष्टान् वाऽनुश्रुतानथ।
उद्यत् सीदत् कर्मतन्त्रं स्मृतिस्तदनु शाम्यति॥ ११/२२/३७॥
units.english: The mind, bound to the reactions of actions aimed at results, always meditates on the objects of the senses, both those that are seen in this world and those that are heard about from Vedic authority. Consequently, the mind appears to come into being and to suffer annihilation along with its objects of perception, and thus its ability to distinguish past and future is lost.

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

meta.english_verbatim: The mind, bound to the reactions of fruitive work, always meditates on the objects of the senses, both those that are seen in this world and those that are heard about from Vedic authority. Consequently, the mind appears to come into being and to suffer annihilation along with its objects of perception, and thus its ability to distinguish past and future is lost.

units.sanskrit:
विषयाभिनिवेशेन नात्मानं यत् स्मरेन्मनः।
जन्तोर्वै कस्यचिद्धेतोर्मृत्युरत्यन्तविस्मृतिः॥ ११/२२/३८॥
units.english: When the living being passes from the present body to the next body, which is created by his own karma, he becomes absorbed in the pleasurable and painful sensations of the new body and completely forgets the experience of the previous body. This total forgetfulness of one’s previous material identity, which comes about for one reason or another, is called death.

parts.sanskrit:
विषयाभिनिवेशेन नात्मानं यत् स्मरेन्मनः।
जन्तोर्वै कस्यचिद्धेतोर्मृत्युरत्यन्तविस्मृतिः॥ ११/२२/३८॥
विषयाभिनिवेशेन उत्तरदेहाभिनिवेशेन पूर्वदेहास्मरणं यत् तन्मृत्युः॥ ३८॥

meta.english_verbatim: When the living entity passes from the present body to the next body, which is created by his own karma, he becomes absorbed in the pleasurable and painful sensations of the new body and completely forgets the experience of the previous body. This total forgetfulness of one’s previous material identity, which comes about for one reason or another, is called death.

units.sanskrit:
जन्म त्वात्मतया पुंसः सर्वभावेन भूरिद।
विषयस्वीकृतिं प्राहुर्यथा स्वप्नमनोरथः॥ ११/२२/३९॥
units.english: O most charitable Uddhava, what is called birth is simply a person’s total identification with a new body. One accepts the new body just as one completely accepts the experience of a dream or a fantasy as reality.

meta.english_verbatim: O most charitable Uddhava, what is called birth is simply a person’s total identification with a new body. One accepts the new body just as one completely accepts the experience of a dream or a fantasy as reality.

units.sanskrit:
स्वप्नं मनोरथं चार्थं प्राक्तनं न स्मरत्यसौ।
तत्र पूर्वमिवात्मानमपूर्वं चानुपश्यति॥ ११/२२/४०॥
units.english: Just as a person experiencing a dream or daydream does not remember his previous dreams or daydreams, a person situated in his present body, although having existed prior to it, thinks that he has only recently come into being.

meta.english_verbatim: Just as a person experiencing a dream or daydream does not remember his previous dreams or daydreams, a person situated in his present body, although having existed prior to it, thinks that he has only recently come into being.

units.sanskrit:
ईदृशायास विज्ञाय त्रैविध्यं भाति वस्तुनि।
बहिरन्तर्भिदाहेतुर्जनोऽसज्जनकृद् यथा॥ ११/२२/४१॥
units.english: Because the mind, which is the resting place of the senses, has created the identification with a new body, the threefold material variety of high, middle and low class appears as if present within the reality of the soul. Thus the self creates external and internal duality, just as a man might give birth to a bad son.

parts.sanskrit:
ईदृशायास विज्ञाय त्रैविध्यं भाति वस्तुनि।
बहिरन्तर्भिदाहेतुर्जनोऽसज्जनकृद् यथा॥ ११/२२/४१॥

ईदृशं वर्तमानम्, आयः एष्यन्, स अतीत इति त्रैविध्यं भाति। विज्ञाय वस्तुनि विज्ञाते सति । दीर्घलोपः “अत्रा ते” इतिवत् । “क्षैप्रे दीर्घलोपः” इति सूत्रात्। अयमेवात्मानात्मनोर्विशेषहेतुः। यथा प्रायोऽसज्जनोऽसज्जनमेव जनयतीति पितृज्ञानात् पुत्रदौरात्म्यं ज्ञायते, एवमनित्यत्वादनात्मत्वं देहादेरित्यर्थः॥ ४१॥

meta.english_verbatim: Because the mind, which is the resting place of the senses, has created the identification with a new body, the threefold material variety of high, middle and low class appears as if present within the reality of the soul. Thus the self creates external and internal duality, just as a man might give birth to a bad son.

units.sanskrit:
नित्यदा ह्यङ्ग भूतानि भवन्ति न भवन्ति च।
कालेनालक्ष्यवेगेन सूक्ष्मत्वात् तन्न दृश्यते॥ ११/२२/४२॥
units.english: My dear Uddhava, material bodies are constantly undergoing creation and destruction by the force of time, whose swiftness is imperceptible. But because of the subtle nature of time, no one sees this.

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Uddhava, material bodies are constantly undergoing creation and destruction by the force of time, whose swiftness is imperceptible. But because of the subtle nature of time, no one sees this.

units.sanskrit:
यथाऽर्चिषां स्रोतसां च फलानां वा वनस्पतेः।
तथैव सर्वभूतानां वयोऽवस्था च तत्कृता॥ ११/२२/४३॥
units.english: The different stages of transformation of all material bodies occur just like those of the flame of a candle, the current of a river, or the fruits of a tree.

meta.english_verbatim: The different stages of transformation of all material bodies occur just like those of the flame of a candle, the current of a river, or the fruits of a tree.

units.sanskrit:
सोऽयं दीपोऽर्चिषां यद्वत् स्रोतसां तदिदं जलम्।
सोऽयं पुमानिति नृणां मृषा गीर्भिर्मृषायुषाम्॥ ११/२२/४४॥
units.english: Although the illumination of a lamp consists of innumerable rays of light undergoing constant creation, transformation and destruction, a person with illusory intelligence who sees the light for a moment will speak falsely, saying, “This is the light of the lamp.” As one observes a flowing river, ever-new water passes by and goes far away, yet a foolish person, observing one point in the river, falsely states, “This is the water of the river.” Similarly, although the material body of a human being is constantly undergoing transformation, those who are simply wasting their lives falsely think and say that each particular stage of the body is the person’s real identity.

meta.english_verbatim: Although the illumination of a lamp consists of innumerable rays of light undergoing constant creation, transformation and destruction, a person with illusory intelligence who sees the light for a moment will speak falsely, saying, “This is the light of the lamp.” As one observes a flowing river, ever-new water passes by and goes far away, yet a foolish person, observing one point in the river, falsely states, “This is the water of the river.” Similarly, although the material body of a human being is constantly undergoing transformation, those who are simply wasting their lives falsely think and say that each particular stage of the body is the person’s real identity.

units.sanskrit:
आद्यः स्वकर्मबीजेन जायते सोऽव्ययः पुमान्।
म्रियते चामरो भ्रान्त्या यथाऽग्निर्दारुसंयुतः॥ ११/२२/४५॥
units.english: A person does not actually take birth out of the seed of past activities, nor, being immortal, does he die. By illusion the living being appears to be born and to die, just as fire in connection with firewood appears to begin and then cease to exist.

parts.sanskrit:
आद्यः स्वकर्मबीजेन जायते सोऽव्ययः पुमान्।
म्रियते चामरो भ्रान्त्या यथाऽग्निर्दारुसंयुतः॥ ११/२२/४५॥

सोऽयमेवेति मृषा।
“स चायमिति तु ज्ञानं न मृषाऽयं स एव तु।
इति ज्ञानं मृषैव स्यात् भेदाभेदौ यतस्तनोः।
अभेद एव जीवस्य नित्यं प्रत्येकशः पृथक्।
दीपदेहनदीवारिफलादीनां पृथक् स्वतः।
भेदाभेदौ परिज्ञेयौ कार्यकारणयोरपि।
गुणस्य गुणिनश्चैव जातिव्यक्त्योस्तथैव च।
तथाऽवयव्यवयवयोः क्रियायास्तद्वतस्तथा।
एवं जडेषु नियमश्चिद्रूपेष्वभिदैव तु॥”
इति च।
“ये धर्मा नियमेनैव धर्मिणो न वियोगिनः ।
जडस्था अप्यभिन्नास्ते भिन्नाभिन्ना वियोगिनः॥”
इति च॥ ४५॥

meta.english_verbatim: A person does not actually take birth out of the seed of past activities, nor, being immortal, does he die. By illusion the living being appears to be born and to die, just as fire in connection with firewood appears to begin and then cease to exist.

units.sanskrit:
निषेकगर्भजन्मानि बाल्यकौमारयौवनम्।
वयोमध्यं जरा मृत्युरित्यवस्थास्तनोर्नव॥ ११/२२/४६॥
units.english: Impregnation, gestation, birth, infancy, childhood, youth, middle age, old age and death are the nine ages of the body.

meta.english_verbatim: Impregnation, gestation, birth, infancy, childhood, youth, middle age, old age and death are the nine ages of the body.

units.sanskrit:
एता मनोरथमयीर्ह्यन्यस्योच्चावचास्तनूः।
गुणसङ्गादुपादत्ते क्वचित् काश्चिज्जहाति च॥ ११/२२/४७॥
units.english: Although the material body is different from the self, because of the ignorance due to material association one falsely identifies oneself with the superior and inferior bodily conditions. Sometimes a fortunate person is able to give up such mental concoction.

meta.english_verbatim: Although the material body is different from the self, because of the ignorance due to material association one falsely identifies oneself with the superior and inferior bodily conditions. Sometimes a fortunate person is able to give up such mental concoction.

units.sanskrit:
आत्मनः पितृपुत्राभ्यामनुमेयौ भवाप्ययौ।
भवाप्ययौ हि वस्तूनामभिज्ञाद्वयलक्षणौ॥ ११/२२/४८॥
units.english: By the death of one’s father or grandfather one can surmise one’s own death, and by the birth of one’s son one can understand the condition of one’s own birth. A person who thus realistically understands the creation and destruction of material bodies is no longer subject to these dualities.

parts.sanskrit:
आत्मनः पितृपुत्राभ्यामनुमेयौ भवाप्ययौ।
भवाप्ययौ हि वस्तूनामभिज्ञाद्वयलक्षणौ॥ ११/२२/४८॥

अभिज्ञाद्वयलक्षणौ अभिमानमात्रौ। तरोर्बीजविकारदृष्टान्तेन विद्वान् देहाभिमानं त्यक्त्वा संयमं याति। परमात्मनश्च भेदं जानाति प्रकृत्यादेः ।
“बीजाद्यवस्थासंयुक्ताद् वृक्षाद् द्रष्टा यथा पृथक् ।
एवं विकारिणो विष्णुर्जीवश्च पृथगेव तु॥”
इति च॥ ४८॥

meta.english_verbatim: By the death of one’s father or grandfather one can surmise one’s own death, and by the birth of one’s son one can understand the condition of one’s own birth. A person who thus realistically understands the creation and destruction of material bodies is no longer subject to these dualities.

units.sanskrit:
तरोर्बीजविकाराभ्यां यो विद्वान् जन्मसंयमौ।
तरोर्विलक्षणो दृष्ट एवं द्रष्टा तनोः पृथक्॥ ११/२२/४९॥
units.english: One who observes the birth of a tree from its seed and the ultimate death of the tree after maturity certainly remains a distinct observer separate from the tree. In the same way, the witness of the birth and death of the material body remains separate from it.

meta.english_verbatim: One who observes the birth of a tree from its seed and the ultimate death of the tree after maturity certainly remains a distinct observer separate from the tree. In the same way, the witness of the birth and death of the material body remains separate from it.

units.sanskrit:
प्रकृतेरेवमात्मानमविविच्याबुधः पुमान्।
तत्वेन स्पर्शसम्मूढः संसारं प्रतिपद्यते॥ ११/२२/५०॥
units.english: An unintelligent man, failing to distinguish himself from material nature, thinks nature to be real. By contact with it he becomes completely bewildered and enters into the cycle of material existence.

meta.english_verbatim: An unintelligent man, failing to distinguish himself from material nature, thinks nature to be real. By contact with it he becomes completely bewildered and enters into the cycle of material existence.

units.sanskrit:
सत्वसङ्गाद् ऋषीन् देवान् रजसाऽऽसुरमानुषान्।
तमसा भूततिर्यक्त्वं भ्रामितो याति कर्मभिः॥ ११/२२/५१॥
units.english: Made to wander because of his actions aimed at results, the conditioned soul, by contact with the mode of goodness, takes birth among the sages or gods. By contact with the mode of passion he becomes a demon or human being, and by association with the mode of ignorance he takes birth as a ghost or in the animal kingdom.

meta.english_verbatim: Made to wander because of his fruitive work, the conditioned soul, by contact with the mode of goodness, takes birth among the sages or demigods. By contact with the mode of passion he becomes a demon or human being, and by association with the mode of ignorance he takes birth as a ghost or in the animal kingdom.

english_edits.rule: fruitive activities -> actions aimed at results

units.sanskrit:
नृत्यतो गायतः पश्यन् यथैवानुकरोति तान्।
एवं बुद्धिगुणान् पश्यन्ननीहोऽप्यनुकार्यते॥ ११/२२/५२॥
units.english: Just as one may imitate persons whom one sees dancing and singing, similarly the soul, although never the doer of material activities, becomes captivated by material intelligence and is thus forced to imitate its qualities.

parts.sanskrit:
नृत्यतो गायतः पश्यन् यथैवानुकरोति तान्।
एवं बुद्धिगुणान् पश्यन्ननीहोऽप्यनुकार्यते॥ ११/२२/५२॥

“दुःखशोकादयः सर्वे ज्ञेया बुद्धिगुणा इति।
सुखज्ञाने तु जीवस्य भक्तिः स्नेहस्तथैव च।
विपर्ययेणासुराणां जीवबुद्धिगुणा मताः॥”
इति च।
“आत्मनोऽपि गुणा बुद्धिकृता बुद्धिगुणा इति ।
उच्यन्ते सुखदुःखाद्याः परमात्मकृता यथा॥”
इति त्रैकाल्ये॥ ५२॥

meta.english_verbatim: Just as one may imitate persons whom one sees dancing and singing, similarly the soul, although never the doer of material activities, becomes captivated by material intelligence and is thus forced to imitate its qualities.

units.sanskrit:
यथा मनोरथधियो विषयानुभवो मृषा।
स्वप्नदृष्टश्च दाशार्ह तथा संसार आत्मनः॥ ११/२२/५४॥
अर्थे ह्यविद्यमानेपि संसृतिर्न निवर्तते।
ध्यायतो विषयान् पुंसः स्वप्नेऽप्यर्थागमो यथा॥ ११/२२/५५॥
units.english: The soul’s material life, his experience of sense enjoyment, is actually false, O descendant of Daśārha, just like trees’ appearance of quivering when the trees are reflected in agitated water, or like the earth’s appearance of spinning due to one’s spinning his eyes around, or like the world of a fantasy or dream.

parts.sanskrit:
यथा मनोरथधियो विषयानुभवो मृषा।
स्वप्नदृष्टश्च दाशार्ह तथा संसार आत्मनः॥ ११/२२/५४॥
अर्थे ह्यविद्यमानेपि संसृतिर्न निवर्तते।
ध्यायतो विषयान् पुंसः स्वप्नेऽप्यर्थागमो यथा॥ ११/२२/५५॥
मृषा वृथा। “अल्पप्रयोजनं यत् तन्मृषेत्येव तदुच्यते” इति शब्दनिर्णये। आत्मनः स्वत एव दुःखाद्याः सुखादिवदिति मिथ्याबुद्धिरिति वा॥ ५४॥

meta.english_verbatim: The soul’s material life, his experience of sense gratification, is actually false, O descendant of Daśārha, just like trees’ appearance of quivering when the trees are reflected in agitated water, or like the earth’s appearance of spinning due to one’s spinning his eyes around, or like the world of a fantasy or dream.

units.sanskrit:
तस्मादुद्धव मा भुङ्क्ष्व विषयानसदिन्द्रियैः।
आत्माग्रहणनिष्पन्नं पश्यन् वैकल्पिकं भ्रमम्॥ ११/२२/५६॥
units.english: Therefore, O Uddhava, do not try to enjoy sense enjoyment with the material senses. See how illusion based on material dualities prevents one from realizing the self.

meta.english_verbatim: Therefore, O Uddhava, do not try to enjoy sense gratification with the material senses. See how illusion based on material dualities prevents one from realizing the self.

units.sanskrit:
क्षिप्तोऽवमानितोऽसद्भिः प्रलब्धः शापितोपि वा।
ताडितः सन्निरुद्धो वा वृत्त्या वा परिहापितः॥ ११/२२/५७॥
units.english: Even though neglected, insulted, ridiculed or envied by bad men, or even though repeatedly agitated by being beaten, tied up or deprived of one’s occupation, spat upon or polluted with urine by ignorant people, one who desires the highest goal in life should in spite of all these difficulties use his intelligence to keep himself safe on the spiritual platform.

meta.english_verbatim: Even though neglected, insulted, ridiculed or envied by bad men, or even though repeatedly agitated by being beaten, tied up or deprived of one’s occupation, spat upon or polluted with urine by ignorant people, one who desires the highest goal in life should in spite of all these difficulties use his intelligence to keep himself safe on the spiritual platform.

units.sanskrit:
विष्ठितो मूत्रितो वाऽज्ञैर्बहुधैवं प्रकम्पितः।
श्रेयस्कामः कृच्छ्रगत आत्मनाऽऽत्मानमुद्धरेत्॥ ११/२२/५८॥
उद्धव उवाच
यथैवमनुबुध्येयं वद नो वदतां वर।
सुदुःसहमहं मन्ये आत्मन्यसदतिक्रमम्॥ ११/२२/५९॥
units.english: Uddhava said: O best of all speakers, please explain to me how I may properly understand this.

meta.english_verbatim: Śrī Uddhava said: O best of all speakers, please explain to me how I may properly understand this.

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
बाह्यान्तर्भजनो ह्यत्र साधुर्वै दुर्जनेरितैः।
दुरुक्तैर्भिन्नमात्मानं यः समाधातुमीश्वरः॥ ११/२३/२॥
units.english: Lord Kṛṣṇa said: O disciple of Bṛhaspati, there is virtually no saintly man in this world capable of resettling his own mind after it has been disturbed by the insulting words of uncivilized men.

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

meta.english_verbatim: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: O disciple of Bṛhaspati, there is virtually no saintly man in this world capable of resettling his own mind after it has been disturbed by the insulting words of uncivilized men.

units.sanskrit:
न तथा तप्यते विद्धः पुमान् बाणैर्हि मर्मगैः।
यथा तुदन्ति मर्मस्था असतां परुषेषवः॥ ११/२३/३॥
units.english: Sharp arrows which pierce one’s chest and reach the heart do not cause as much suffering as the arrows of harsh, insulting words that become lodged within the heart when spoken by uncivilized men.

meta.english_verbatim: Sharp arrows which pierce one’s chest and reach the heart do not cause as much suffering as the arrows of harsh, insulting words that become lodged within the heart when spoken by uncivilized men.

units.sanskrit:
कथयन्ति महापुण्यमितिहासमिहोद्धव।
तमहं वर्णयिष्यामि निबोध सुसमाहितः॥ ११/२३/४॥
units.english: My dear Uddhava, in this regard a most pious story is told, and I shall now describe it to you. Please listen with careful attention.

meta.english_verbatim: My dear Uddhava, in this regard a most pious story is told, and I shall now describe it to you. Please listen with careful attention.

units.sanskrit:
केनचिद् भिक्षुणा गीतं परिभूतेन दुर्जनैः।
स्मरता धृतियुक्तेन विपाकं निजकर्मणः॥ ११/२३/५॥
units.english: Once a certain sannyāsī was insulted in many ways by impious men. However, with determination he remembered that he was suffering the fruit of his own previous karma. I will narrate to you his story and that which he spoke.

meta.english_verbatim: Once a certain sannyāsī was insulted in many ways by impious men. However, with determination he remembered that he was suffering the fruit of his own previous karma. I will narrate to you his story and that which he spoke.

units.sanskrit:
अवन्तीषु द्विजः कश्चिदासीदाढ्यतमः श्रिया।
वार्तावृत्तिः कदर्यस्तु कामी लुब्धोऽतिकोपनः॥ ११/२३/६॥
units.english: In the country of Avantī there once lived a certain brāhmaṇa who was very rich and gifted with all opulences, and who was engaged in the occupation of commerce. But he was a miserly person — lusty, greedy and very prone to anger.

meta.english_verbatim: In the country of Avantī there once lived a certain brāhmaṇa who was very rich and gifted with all opulences, and who was engaged in the occupation of commerce. But he was a miserly person — lusty, greedy and very prone to anger.

units.sanskrit:
ज्ञातयोऽतिथयस्तस्य वाङ्मात्रेणाप्यनर्चिताः।
शून्यावसथ आत्मापि काले कामैरनर्चितः॥ ११/२३/७॥
units.english: In his home, devoid of religiosity and lawful sense enjoyment, the family members and guests were never properly respected, even with words. He would not even allow sufficient gratification for his own body at the suitable times.

meta.english_verbatim: In his home, devoid of religiosity and lawful sense gratification, the family members and guests were never properly respected, even with words. He would not even allow sufficient gratification for his own body at the suitable times.

units.sanskrit:
दुःशीलस्य कदर्यस्य द्रुह्यतः पुत्रबान्धवान्।
दारा दुहितरो भृत्या विषण्णा नाचरन् प्रियम्॥ ११/२३/८॥
units.english: Since he was so hardhearted and miserly, his sons, in-laws, wife, daughters and servants began to feel inimical toward him. Becoming disgusted, they would never treat him with affection.

meta.english_verbatim: Since he was so hardhearted and miserly, his sons, in-laws, wife, daughters and servants began to feel inimical toward him. Becoming disgusted, they would never treat him with affection.

units.sanskrit:
तस्यैवं यक्षवित्तस्य च्युतस्योभयलोकतः।
धर्मकामविहीनस्य चुक्रुधुः पञ्चभागिनः॥ ११/२३/९॥
units.english: In this way the presiding deities of the five family sacrifices became angry at the brāhmaṇa, who, being niggardly, guarded his wealth like a Yakṣa, who had no good destination either in this world or the next, and who was totally deprived of religiosity and sense enjoyment.

meta.english_verbatim: In this way the presiding deities of the five family sacrifices became angry at the brāhmaṇa, who, being niggardly, guarded his wealth like a Yakṣa, who had no good destination either in this world or the next, and who was totally deprived of religiosity and sense enjoyment.

units.sanskrit:
तदवध्यानविस्रस्तपुण्यस्कन्धस्य भूरिद।
अर्थोऽप्यगच्छन्निधनं बह्वायासपरिभ्रमात्॥ ११/२३/१०॥
units.english: O magnanimous Uddhava, by his neglect of these gods he depleted his stock of piety and all his wealth. The accumulation of his repeated exhaustive endeavors was totally lost.

meta.english_verbatim: O magnanimous Uddhava, by his neglect of these demigods he depleted his stock of piety and all his wealth. The accumulation of his repeated exhaustive endeavors was totally lost.

units.sanskrit:
ज्ञातयो जगृहुः किञ्चित् किञ्चिद् दस्यव उद्धव।
दैवतः कालतः किञ्चिद् ब्रह्मबन्धोर्नृपार्थिवात्॥ ११/२३/११॥
units.english: Some of the wealth of this so-called brāhmaṇa was taken away by his relatives, My dear Uddhava, some by thieves, some by the whims of providence, some by the effects of time, some by ordinary men and some by government authorities.

meta.english_verbatim: Some of the wealth of this so-called brāhmaṇa was taken away by his relatives, My dear Uddhava, some by thieves, some by the whims of providence, some by the effects of time, some by ordinary men and some by government authorities.

units.sanskrit:
स एवं द्रविणे नष्टे धर्मकामविवर्जितः।
उपेक्षितश्च स्वजनैश्चिन्तामाप दुरत्ययाम्॥ ११/२३/१२॥
units.english: Finally, when his property was completely lost, he who never engaged in religiosity or sense enjoyment became ignored by his family members. Thus he began to feel unbearable anxiety.

meta.english_verbatim: Finally, when his property was completely lost, he who never engaged in religiosity or sense enjoyment became ignored by his family members. Thus he began to feel unbearable anxiety.

units.sanskrit:
तस्यैवं ध्यायतो दीर्घमगादायुस्तपस्विनः।
खिद्यतो बाष्पकण्ठस्य निर्वेदः सुमहानभूत्॥ ११/२३/१३॥
units.english: Having lost all his wealth, he felt great pain and lamentation. His throat choked up with tears, and he meditated for a long time on his fortune. Then a powerful feeling of renunciation came over him.

meta.english_verbatim: Having lost all his wealth, he felt great pain and lamentation. His throat choked up with tears, and he meditated for a long time on his fortune. Then a powerful feeling of renunciation came over him.

units.sanskrit:
स चाहेदमहो कष्टं वृथाऽऽत्मा मे सुतापितः।
न धर्माय न कामाय यस्यार्थायास ईदृशः॥ ११/२३/१४॥
units.english: The brāhmaṇa spoke as follows: O what great misfortune! I have simply tormented myself uselessly, struggling so hard for money that was not even intended for religiosity or material enjoyment.

meta.english_verbatim: The brāhmaṇa spoke as follows: O what great misfortune! I have simply tormented myself uselessly, struggling so hard for money that was not even intended for religiosity or material enjoyment.

units.sanskrit:
प्रायेणार्थः कदर्याणां न सुखाय कदाचन।
इह चात्मोपतापाय मृतस्य नरकाय च॥ ११/२३/१५॥
units.english: Generally, the wealth of misers never allows them any happiness. In this life it causes their self-torment, and when they die it sends them to hell.

meta.english_verbatim: Generally, the wealth of misers never allows them any happiness. In this life it causes their self-torment, and when they die it sends them to hell.

units.sanskrit:
यशो यशस्विनां शुभ्रं श्लाघ्या ये गुणिनां गुणाः।
लोभः स्वल्पोपि तान् हन्ति श्वित्रो रूपमिवेप्सितम्॥ ११/२३/१६॥
units.english: Whatever pure fame is possessed by the famous and whatever praiseworthy qualities are found in the virtuous are destroyed by even a small amount of greed, just as one’s attractive physical beauty is ruined by a trace of white leprosy.

meta.english_verbatim: Whatever pure fame is possessed by the famous and whatever praiseworthy qualities are found in the virtuous are destroyed by even a small amount of greed, just as one’s attractive physical beauty is ruined by a trace of white leprosy.

units.sanskrit:
अर्थस्य साधने सिद्ध उत्कर्षे रक्षणे व्यये।
नाशोपभोग आयासस्त्रासश्चिन्ता भ्रमो नृणाम्॥ ११/२३/१७॥
units.english: In the earning, attainment, increase, protection, expense, loss and enjoyment of wealth, all men experience great labor, fear, anxiety and delusion.

meta.english_verbatim: In the earning, attainment, increase, protection, expense, loss and enjoyment of wealth, all men experience great labor, fear, anxiety and delusion.

units.sanskrit:
स्तेयं हिंसाऽनृतं डम्भः कामः क्रोधः स्मयो मदः।
भेदो वैरमविश्वासः संस्पर्धा व्यसनानि च॥ ११/२३/१८॥
एते त्रयोदशानर्था ह्यर्थमूला मता नृणाम्।
तस्मादनर्थमर्थाख्यं श्रेयोर्थी दूरतस्त्यजेत्॥ ११/२३/१९॥
units.english: Theft, violence, speaking lies, duplicity, lust, anger, perplexity, pride, quarreling, enmity, faithlessness, envy and the dangers caused by women, gambling and intoxication are the fifteen undesirable qualities that contaminate men because of greed for wealth. Although these qualities are undesirable, men falsely ascribe value to them. One desiring to achieve the real benefit of life should therefore remain aloof from undesirable material wealth.

meta.english_verbatim: Theft, violence, speaking lies, duplicity, lust, anger, perplexity, pride, quarreling, enmity, faithlessness, envy and the dangers caused by women, gambling and intoxication are the fifteen undesirable qualities that contaminate men because of greed for wealth. Although these qualities are undesirable, men falsely ascribe value to them. One desiring to achieve the real benefit of life should therefore remain aloof from undesirable material wealth.

units.sanskrit:
भिद्यन्ते भ्रातरो दाराः पितरः सुहृदस्तथा।
एकयाऽर्थेच्छया सद्यः सर्वे चाप्यरयः कृताः॥ ११/२३/२०॥
units.english: Even a man’s brothers, wife, parents and friends united with him in love will immediately break off their affectionate relationships and become enemies over a single coin.

meta.english_verbatim: Even a man’s brothers, wife, parents and friends united with him in love will immediately break off their affectionate relationships and become enemies over a single coin.

units.sanskrit:
अर्थेनाल्पीयसा ह्येते संरब्धा दीप्तमन्यवः।
त्यजन्त्यसून् वृथा घ्नन्ति सहसोत्सृज्य सौहृदम्॥ ११/२३/२१॥
units.english: For even a small amount of money these relatives and friends become very agitated and their anger is inflamed. Acting as rivals, they quickly give up all sentiments of goodwill and will reject one at a moment’s notice, even to the point of committing murder.

meta.english_verbatim: For even a small amount of money these relatives and friends become very agitated and their anger is inflamed. Acting as rivals, they quickly give up all sentiments of goodwill and will reject one at a moment’s notice, even to the point of committing murder.

units.sanskrit:
लब्ध्वा जन्मान्तरैः प्रार्थ्यं मानुष्यं तद् द्विजाग्य्रताम्।
तदनादृत्य ये सर्वं घ्नन्ति यान्त्यशुभां गतिम्॥ ११/२३/२२॥
units.english: Those who obtain human life, which is prayed for even by the gods, and in that human birth become situated as first-class brāhmaṇas, are extremely fortunate. If they disregard this important opportunity, they are certainly killing their own self-interest and thus achieve a most unfortunate end.

meta.english_verbatim: Those who obtain human life, which is prayed for even by the demigods, and in that human birth become situated as first-class brāhmaṇas, are extremely fortunate. If they disregard this important opportunity, they are certainly killing their own self-interest and thus achieve a most unfortunate end.

units.sanskrit:
स्वर्गापवर्गयोर्द्वारं प्राप्य लोकमिमं पुमान्।
द्रविणे को विषज्जेत मर्त्योऽनर्थस्य धामनि॥ ११/२३/२३॥
units.english: What mortal man, having achieved this human life, which is the very gateway to both heaven and liberation, would willingly become attached to that abode of worthlessness, material property?

meta.english_verbatim: What mortal man, having achieved this human life, which is the very gateway to both heaven and liberation, would willingly become attached to that abode of worthlessness, material property?

units.sanskrit:
देवर्षिपितृभूतानि ज्ञातीनन्यांश्च भागिनः।
असंविभज्य चात्मानं यक्षवित्तः पतत्यधः॥ ११/२३/२४॥
units.english: One who fails to distribute his wealth to the proper shareholders — the gods, sages, forefathers and ordinary living beings, as well as his immediate relatives, in-laws and own self — is maintaining his wealth simply like a Yakṣa and will fall down.

meta.english_verbatim: One who fails to distribute his wealth to the proper shareholders — the demigods, sages, forefathers and ordinary living entities, as well as his immediate relatives, in-laws and own self — is maintaining his wealth simply like a Yakṣa and will fall down.

units.sanskrit:
व्यर्थयाऽर्थेहया वित्तं प्रमत्तस्य वयो बलम्।
कुशलाय न सिध्यन्ति जरठः किन्नु साधयेत्॥ ११/२३/२५॥
units.english: Discriminating persons are able to utilize their money, youth and strength to achieve perfection. But I have feverishly squandered these in the useless endeavor for further wealth. Now that I am an old man, what can I achieve?

meta.english_verbatim: Discriminating persons are able to utilize their money, youth and strength to achieve perfection. But I have feverishly squandered these in the useless endeavor for further wealth. Now that I am an old man, what can I achieve?

units.sanskrit:
तस्मात् सङ्क्ल्श्यितेऽविद्वान् व्यर्थयाऽर्थेहयाऽसकृत्।
कस्यचिन्मायया नूनं लोकोऽयं सुविमोहितः॥ ११/२३/२६॥
units.english: Why must an intelligent man suffer by his constant vain efforts to get wealth? Indeed, this whole world is most bewildered by someone’s illusory potency.

meta.english_verbatim: Why must an intelligent man suffer by his constant vain efforts to get wealth? Indeed, this whole world is most bewildered by someone’s illusory potency.

units.sanskrit:
किं धनैर्धनदैर्वा किं कामैर्वा कामदैरुत।
मृत्युना ग्रस्यमानस्य कर्मभिर्वेति जन्मभिः॥ ११/२३/२७॥
units.english: For one who is in the grips of death, what is the use of wealth or those who offer it, sense enjoyment or those who offer it, or, for that matter, any type of fruitive activity, which simply causes one to again take birth in the material world?

meta.english_verbatim: For one who is in the grips of death, what is the use of wealth or those who offer it, sense gratification or those who offer it, or, for that matter, any type of fruitive activity, which simply causes one to again take birth in the material world?

units.sanskrit:
नूनं मे भगवांस्तुष्टः सर्वदेवमयो हरिः।
येन नीतो दशामेतां निर्वेदश्चात्मनः प्लवः॥ ११/२३/२८॥
units.english: The Lord, Lord Hari, who contains within Himself all the gods, must be satisfied with me. Indeed, He has brought me to this suffering condition and forced me to experience detachment, which is the boat to carry me over this ocean of material life.

english_edits.rule: (the) Supreme Personality of Godhead -> the Lord

meta.english_verbatim: The Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Hari, who contains within Himself all the demigods, must be satisfied with me. Indeed, He has brought me to this suffering condition and forced me to experience detachment, which is the boat to carry me over this ocean of material life.

units.sanskrit:
सोहं कालावशेषेण शोषयिष्येऽङ्गमात्मनः।
अप्रमत्तोऽखिलार्थेषु यदि स्यां सिद्ध आत्मनि॥ ११/२३/२९॥
units.english: If there is any time remaining in my life, I will perform austerities and force my body to subsist on the bare necessities. Without further confusion I shall pursue that which constitutes my entire self-interest in life, and I shall remain satisfied within the self.

meta.english_verbatim: If there is any time remaining in my life, I will perform austerities and force my body to subsist on the bare necessities. Without further confusion I shall pursue that which constitutes my entire self-interest in life, and I shall remain satisfied within the self.

units.sanskrit:
तत्र मामनुमोदेरन् देवास्त्रिभुवनेश्वराः।
मुहूर्तेन ब्रह्मलोकं खद्वाङ्गः समसाधयत्॥ ११/२३/३०॥
units.english: Thus may the presiding gods of these three worlds kindly show their mercy upon me. Indeed, King Khaṭvāṅga was able to achieve the spiritual world in a single moment.

meta.english_verbatim: Thus may the presiding demigods of these three worlds kindly show their mercy upon me. Indeed, Mahārāja Khaṭvāṅga was able to achieve the spiritual world in a single moment.

units.sanskrit:
श्रीभगवानुवाच
इत्यभिप्रेत्य मनसा ह्यावन्त्यो द्विजसत्तमः।
उन्मुच्य हृदयग्रन्धिं शान्तो भिक्षुरभून्मुनिः॥ ११/२३/३१॥
units.english: Lord Kṛṣṇa continued: His mind thus determined, that most excellent Avantī brāhmaṇa was able to untie the knots of desire within his heart. He then assumed the role of a peaceful and silent sannyāsī mendicant.

english_edits.rule: honorific Śrī before a name removed

meta.english_verbatim: Lord Śrī Kṛṣṇa continued: His mind thus determined, that most excellent Avantī brāhmaṇa was able to untie the knots of desire within his heart. He then assumed the role of a peaceful and silent sannyāsī mendicant.

units.sanskrit:
स चचार महीमेतां संयतात्मेन्द्रियानिलः।
भिक्षार्थं नगरग्रामानसङ्गोऽलक्षितोऽविशत्॥ ११/२३/३२॥
units.english: He wandered about the earth, keeping his intelligence, senses and life air under control. To beg charity he traveled alone to various cities and villages. He did not advertise his advanced spiritual position and thus was not recognized by others.

meta.english_verbatim: He wandered about the earth, keeping his intelligence, senses and life air under control. To beg charity he traveled alone to various cities and villages. He did not advertise his advanced spiritual position and thus was not recognized by others.

units.sanskrit:
तं वै प्रवयसं भिक्षुमवधूतमसज्जनाः।
दृप्ताः पर्यभवन् भद्र बह्वीभिः परिभूतिभिः॥ ११/२३/३३॥
units.english: O kind Uddhava, seeing him as an old, dirty beggar, rowdy persons would dishonor him with many insults.

meta.english_verbatim: O kind Uddhava, seeing him as an old, dirty beggar, rowdy persons would dishonor him with many insults.

units.sanskrit:
केचित् त्रिवेणुं जगृहुरेके पात्रं कमण्डलुम्।
पीठं चैकेऽक्षसूत्रं च कन्थां चीराणि केचन॥ ११/२३/३४॥
units.english: Some of these persons would take away his sannyāsī rod, and some the waterpot which he was using as a begging bowl. Some took his deerskin seat, some his chanting beads, and some would steal his torn, ragged clothing. Displaying these things before him, they would pretend to offer them back but would then hide them again.

units.sanskrit:
तर्जयन्त्यपरे वाग्भिः स्तेनोऽयमिति वादिनः।
बध्नन्ति रज्ज्वा तं केचिद् बध्यतां वध्यतामिति॥ ११/२३/३७॥
units.english: Although he had taken a vow of silence, they would try to make him speak, and if he did not speak they would beat him with sticks. Others would chastise him, saying, “This man is just a thief.” And others would bind him up with rope, shouting, “Tie him up! Tie him up!”

units.sanskrit:
क्षिपन्त्येकेऽवजानन्त एष धर्मध्वजः शठः।
क्षीणवित्त इमां वृत्तिमगृहीत् स्वजनोज्झितः॥ ११/२३/३८॥
अहो एष महासारो धृतिमान् गिरिराडिव।
मौनेन साधयत्यर्थं बकवद् दृढनिश्चयः॥ ११/२३/३९॥
units.english: They would criticize and insult him, saying, “This man is just a hypocrite and a cheat. He makes a business of religion simply because he lost all his wealth and his family threw him out.”

meta.english_verbatim: They would criticize and insult him, saying, “This man is just a hypocrite and a cheat. He makes a business of religion simply because he lost all his wealth and his family threw him out.”

units.sanskrit:
इत्येके विहसन्त्येनमेके दौर्वादयन्ति च।
तं बबन्धुर्निरुरुधुर्यथा क्राडनकं द्विजम्॥ ११/२३/४०॥
units.english: Some would ridicule him by saying, “Just see this greatly powerful sage! He is as steadfast as the Himālaya Mountains. By practice of silence he strives for his goal with great determination, just like a heron.” Other persons would pass foul air upon him, and sometimes others would bind this twice-born brāhmaṇa in chains and keep him captive like a pet animal.

units.sanskrit:
एवं स भौतिकं दुःखं दैविकं दैहिकं च यत्।
भोक्तव्यमात्मनो दिष्टं प्राप्तं प्राप्तमबुध्यत॥ ११/२३/४१॥
units.english: The brāhmaṇa understood that all his suffering — from other living beings, from the higher forces of nature and from his own body — was unavoidable, being allotted to him by providence.

meta.english_verbatim: The brāhmaṇa understood that all his suffering — from other living beings, from the higher forces of nature and from his own body — was unavoidable, being allotted to him by providence.

units.sanskrit:
परिभूत इमां गाधामगायत नराधमैः।
पातयद्भिः स्वधर्मस्थो धृतिमास्थाय सात्विकीम्॥ ११/२३/४२॥
units.english: Even while being insulted by these low-class men who were trying to effect his downfall, he remained steady in his spiritual duties. Fixing his resolution in the mode of goodness, he began to chant the following song.

meta.english_verbatim: Even while being insulted by these low-class men who were trying to effect his downfall, he remained steady in his spiritual duties. Fixing his resolution in the mode of goodness, he began to chant the following song.

units.sanskrit:
भिक्षुरुवाच
नायं जनो मे सुखदुःखहेतुर्न देवताऽऽत्मा ग्रहकर्मकालाः।
मनः परं कारणमामनन्ति संसारचक्रं परिवर्तयेद् यत्॥ ११/२३/४३॥
units.english: The brāhmaṇa said: These people are not the cause of my happiness and distress. Neither are the gods, my own body, the planets, my past work, or time. Rather, it is the mind alone that causes happiness and distress and perpetuates the rotation of material life.

meta.english_verbatim: The brāhmaṇa said: These people are not the cause of my happiness and distress. Neither are the demigods, my own body, the planets, my past work, or time. Rather, it is the mind alone that causes happiness and distress and perpetuates the rotation of material life.

units.sanskrit:
मनो गुणान् वै सृजते बलीयस्ततश्च कर्माणि विलक्षणानि।
शुक्लनि कृष्णान्यथ लोहितानि तेभ्यः सवर्णा गतयो भवन्ति॥ ११/२३/४४॥
units.english: The powerful mind actuates the functions of the material modes, from which evolve the different kinds of material activities in the modes of goodness, ignorance and passion. From the activities in each of these modes develop the corresponding statuses of life.

meta.english_verbatim: The powerful mind actuates the functions of the material modes, from which evolve the different kinds of material activities in the modes of goodness, ignorance and passion. From the activities in each of these modes develop the corresponding statuses of life.

units.sanskrit:
अनीह आत्मा मनसः समीहितं हिरण्मयो मत्सख उद्विचष्टे।
मनः स्वलिङ्गं परिगृह्य कामान् जुषन् निबद्धो गुणसङ्गतोऽसौ॥ ११/२३/४५॥
units.english: Although present along with the struggling mind within the material body, the Supreme Self is not endeavoring, because He is already endowed with transcendental enlightenment. Acting as my friend, He simply witnesses from His transcendental position. I, the infinitesimal spirit soul, on the other hand, have embraced this mind, which is the mirror reflecting the image of the material world. Thus I have become engaged in enjoying objects of desire and am entangled due to contact with the modes of nature.

meta.english_verbatim: Although present along with the struggling mind within the material body, the Supersoul is not endeavoring, because He is already endowed with transcendental enlightenment. Acting as my friend, He simply witnesses from His transcendental position. I, the infinitesimal spirit soul, on the other hand, have embraced this mind, which is the mirror reflecting the image of the material world. Thus I have become engaged in enjoying objects of desire and am entangled due to contact with the modes of nature.

units.sanskrit:
दानं स्वधर्मो नियमो यमश्च श्रुतानि कर्माणि च सद्व्रतानि।
सर्वे मनोनिग्रहलक्षणान्ताः परो हि योगो मनसः समाधिः॥ ११/२३/४६॥
units.english: Charity, prescribed duties, observance of major and minor regulative principles, hearing from scripture, pious works and purifying vows all have as their final aim the subduing of the mind. Indeed, concentration of the mind on the Supreme is the highest yoga.

meta.english_verbatim: Charity, prescribed duties, observance of major and minor regulative principles, hearing from scripture, pious works and purifying vows all have as their final aim the subduing of the mind. Indeed, concentration of the mind on the Supreme is the highest yoga.

units.sanskrit:
समाहितं यस्य मनः प्रशान्तं दानादिभिः किं वद तस्य कृत्यम्।
असंयतं यस्य मनो विनश्येद् दानादिभिश्चेदपरं किमेभिः॥ ११/२३/४७॥
units.english: If one’s mind is perfectly fixed and pacified, then tell me what need does one have to perform ritualistic charity and other pious rituals? And if one’s mind remains uncontrolled, lost in ignorance, then of what use are these engagements for him?

meta.english_verbatim: If one’s mind is perfectly fixed and pacified, then tell me what need does one have to perform ritualistic charity and other pious rituals? And if one’s mind remains uncontrolled, lost in ignorance, then of what use are these engagements for him?

units.sanskrit:
मनोवशेऽन्ये हि१ भवन्ति देवा मनो हि नान्यस्य वशं समेति।
भीमो हि देवः सहसः सहीयान् नात्याविशत् तत् स हि देवदेवः॥ ११/२३/४८॥
units.english: All the senses have been under the control of the mind since time immemorial, and the mind himself never comes under the sway of any other. He is stronger than the strongest, and his godlike power is fearsome. Therefore, anyone who can bring the mind under control becomes the master of all the senses.

meta.english_verbatim: All the senses have been under the control of the mind since time immemorial, and the mind himself never comes under the sway of any other. He is stronger than the strongest, and his godlike power is fearsome. Therefore, anyone who can bring the mind under control becomes the master of all the senses.

units.sanskrit:
तं दुर्जयं शुत्रुमसह्यवेगमरुन्तुदं तन्न विजित्य केचित्।
कुर्वन्त्यसद्विग्रहमत्र मर्त्यैर्मित्रैरुदासीनरिपुं विमूढाः॥ ११/२३/४९॥
units.english: Failing to conquer this irrepressible enemy, the mind, whose urges are intolerable and who torments the heart, many people are completely bewildered and create useless quarrel with others. Thus they conclude that other people are either their friends, their enemies or parties indifferent to them.

parts.sanskrit:
तं दुर्जयं शुत्रुमसह्यवेगमरुन्तुदं तन्न विजित्य केचित्।
कुर्वन्त्यसद्विग्रहमत्र मर्त्यैर्मित्रैरुदासीनरिपुं विमूढाः॥ ११/२३/४९॥

सात्विकमनोविवक्षया देवशब्दः । तामसमनोविवक्षया शत्रुशब्दः।
“एकस्थानाधिपत्ये तु भिन्नानामपि युज्यते।
अभेदेन परामर्शः सादृश्येनापि वस्तुनोः॥”
इति प्रयोगे।
“ऋते द्वे ब्रह्मणी कस्य मनो याति वशं क्वचित्।
श्रियं सरस्वतीं वाऽपि याति वा तत्प्रसादतः॥”
इति पाद्मे।
उदासीनानां रिपुम्। सम्यग्यततां न रिपुत्वं शक्यत इत्यर्थः॥ ४८-४९॥

meta.english_verbatim: Failing to conquer this irrepressible enemy, the mind, whose urges are intolerable and who torments the heart, many people are completely bewildered and create useless quarrel with others. Thus they conclude that other people are either their friends, their enemies or parties indifferent to them.

units.sanskrit:
देहं मनोमात्रमिदं गृहीत्वा ममाहमित्यन्धधियो मनुष्याः।
एषोऽहमन्योऽयमिति भ्रमेण दुरन्तपारे तमसि भ्रमान्त॥ ११/२३/५०॥
units.english: Persons who identify with this body, which is simply the product of the material mind, are blinded in their intelligence, thinking in terms of “I” and “mine.” Because of their illusion of “this is I, but that is someone else,” they wander in endless darkness.

parts.sanskrit:
देहं मनोमात्रमिदं गृहीत्वा ममाहमित्यन्धधियो मनुष्याः।
एषोऽहमन्योऽयमिति भ्रमेण दुरन्तपारे तमसि भ्रमान्त॥ ११/२३/५०॥

अभिमानमात्रेणैव जीवस्य देहेन सम्बन्ध इति मनोमात्रम्। मनसा निर्माणमिति। अहमन्य इत्यपि देहमात्रे मन्यन्ते।
“देहमात्रं स्वमात्मानं यः परं चाभिपश्यति।
अन्धे तमसि मग्नस्य नोत्तारस्तस्य कुत्रचित्॥”
इति च॥ ५०॥

meta.english_verbatim: Persons who identify with this body, which is simply the product of the material mind, are blinded in their intelligence, thinking in terms of “I” and “mine.” Because of their illusion of “this is I, but that is someone else,” they wander in endless darkness.

units.sanskrit:
जनोऽस्य हेतुः सुखदुःखयोश्चेत् किमात्मनश्चात्र हि भौमयोस्तत्।
जिह्वां क्वचित् सन्दशति स्वदद्भिस्तद्वेदनायां कतमाय कुप्येत्॥ ११/२३/५१॥
units.english: If you say that these people are the cause of my happiness and distress, then where is the place of the soul in such a conception? This happiness and distress pertain not to the soul but to the interactions of material bodies. If someone bites his tongue with his own teeth, at whom can he become angry in his suffering?

parts.sanskrit:
जनोऽस्य हेतुः सुखदुःखयोश्चेत् किमात्मनश्चात्र हि भौमयोस्तत्।
जिह्वां क्वचित् सन्दशति स्वदद्भिस्तद्वेदनायां कतमाय कुप्येत्॥ ११/२३/५१॥
“जनशब्दः स्वतो जीवे क्वचिद् देहे च वर्तते” इति प्रयोगे॥ ५१॥

meta.english_verbatim: If you say that these people are the cause of my happiness and distress, then where is the place of the soul in such a conception? This happiness and distress pertain not to the soul but to the interactions of material bodies. If someone bites his tongue with his own teeth, at whom can he become angry in his suffering?

units.sanskrit:
दुःखस्य हेतुर्यदि देवताऽस्तु किमात्मनस्तत्र विकारयोस्तत्।
यदङ्गमङ्गेन विहन्यते क्वचित् क्रुध्येत कस्मै पुरुषः स्वदेहे॥ ११/२३/५२॥
units.english: If you say that the gods who rule the bodily senses cause suffering, still, how can such suffering apply to the spirit soul? This acting and being acted upon are merely interactions of the changeable senses and their presiding deities. When one limb of the body attacks another, with whom can the person in that body be angry?

parts.sanskrit:
दुःखस्य हेतुर्यदि देवताऽस्तु किमात्मनस्तत्र विकारयोस्तत्।
यदङ्गमङ्गेन विहन्यते क्वचित् क्रुध्येत कस्मै पुरुषः स्वदेहे॥ ११/२३/५२॥

अयोग्यक्रोधादेर्मन एव कारणम्।
“अविकाराश्च ते देवा विकारा इति शब्दिताः।
अभिमानाद् विकारस्य स्वतः शक्ता अपि ध्रुवम्॥”
इति च॥ ५२॥

meta.english_verbatim: If you say that the demigods who rule the bodily senses cause suffering, still, how can such suffering apply to the spirit soul? This acting and being acted upon are merely interactions of the changeable senses and their presiding deities. When one limb of the body attacks another, with whom can the person in that body be angry?

units.sanskrit:
आत्मा यदि स्यात् सुखदुःखहेतुः किमन्यतस्तत्र निजः स्वभावः।
न ह्यात्मनोऽन्यद् यदि तन्मृषा स्याद् क्रुध्येत कस्मै न सुखं न दुःखम्॥ ११/२३/५३॥
units.english: If the soul himself were the cause of happiness and distress, then we could not blame others, since happiness and distress would be simply the nature of the soul. According to this theory, nothing except the soul actually exists, and if we were to perceive something besides the soul, that would be illusion. Therefore, since happiness and distress do not actually exist in this concept, why become angry at oneself or others?

parts.sanskrit:
आत्मा यदि स्यात् सुखदुःखहेतुः किमन्यतस्तत्र निजः स्वभावः।
न ह्यात्मनोऽन्यद् यदि तन्मृषा स्याद् क्रुध्येत कस्मै न सुखं न दुःखम्॥ ११/२३/५३॥

नह्यात्मनः स्वभावादन्यद् भवति। यदि दृश्यते तथाऽपि मृषा स्यात्। सुखरूपं दुःखं न भवति। अतो मन एव तथा दर्शयति।
“जीवस्य सुखरूपस्य न दुःखं क्वचिदिष्यते।
अतो मनोऽभिमानेन दुःखी भवति नान्यथा॥”

units.sanskrit:
ग्रहा निमित्तं सुखदुःखयोश्चेत् किमात्मनोऽजस्य जनस्य ते वै।
ग्रहैर्ग्रहस्यैव भवन्ति पीडाः क्रुध्येत कस्मै पुरुषस्ततोऽन्यः॥ ११/२३/५४॥
units.english: And if we examine the hypothesis that the planets are the immediate cause of suffering and happiness, then also where is the relationship with the soul, who is eternal? After all, the effect of the planets applies only to things that have taken birth. Expert astrologers have moreover explained how the planets are only causing pain to each other. Therefore, since the living being is distinct from these planets and from the material body, against whom should he vent his anger?

parts.sanskrit:

ग्रहैर्ग्रहस्यैव भवन्ति पीडाः क्रुध्येत कस्मै पुरुषस्ततोऽन्यः॥ ११/२३/५४॥

meta.english_verbatim: And if we examine the hypothesis that the planets are the immediate cause of suffering and happiness, then also where is the relationship with the soul, who is eternal? units.sanskrit:
कर्मास्तु हेतुः सुखदुःखयोर्वै किमात्मनस्तद् हि जडेऽजडत्वे।
देहे स्ववित् पुरुषोऽयं सुपर्णः क्रुध्येत कस्मै न हि कर्म मूलम्॥ ११/२३/५५॥
units.english: If we assume that actions aimed at results is the cause of happiness and distress, we still are not dealing with the soul. The idea of material work arises when there is a spiritual actor who is conscious and a material body that undergoes the transformation of happiness and distress as a reaction to such work. Since the body has no life, it cannot be the actual recipient of happiness and distress, nor can the soul, who is ultimately completely spiritual and aloof from the material body. Since karma thus has no ultimate basis in either the body or the soul, at whom can one become angry?

parts.sanskrit:
